solution_title: 111th Place Solution (7th on Public) - Key Ideas
solution_summary: The solution used separate forecasting models for each of four weeks, with lags matched to each forecast horizon. Target encodings, weekday-pattern lag aggregates, sales-trend features, and weekly price differences supplied additional signals. Careful hyperparameter tuning delivered substantial gains, and one ensemble component predicted residuals relative to a 28-day mean using LightGBM. Recursive forecasting performed well on the public leaderboard but failed on cross-validation and the private evaluation.

The team combined three groups of CNN and sound-event-detection models in a weighted ensemble with threshold optimization. The author's CNN pipelines used both precomputed and on-the-fly mel-spectrograms, varying audio durations, heads, and backbones to increase diversity. Weighting losses by audio ratings helped address noisy recordings, alongside secondary labels and audio augmentation. Several alternatives failed to improve results, including second-stage training on selected slices and fine-tuning previous-year checkpoints.

solution_title: #1 Place Solution of The Slippery Appraisals team
solution_summary: The solution stacked diverse first-level XGBoost models using ExtraTrees and a linear model, then blended the two second-level predictions. The strongest features described recent demand through grouped one-to-three-week lags, historical aggregates, categorical frequencies, and parsed product attributes. Validation reproduced the two-week forecasting process by feeding first-week predictions into the next week's lag features, with week nine predictions used to train the stack. Feature selection reduced more than 300 engineered variables to 175, and later models benefited from using only the most recent training week.

solution_title: 24th Place: A Heavy Stacking Approach with 166 OOFs and Neural Meta Models
solution_summary: The solution combined diverse gradient boosting models with neural stacking and a final blend. Numeric discretization was especially effective for XGBoost, while LightGBM supplied additional diversity. An unfiltered pool of roughly 166 out-of-fold predictions fed RealMLP and TabFPN stackers, with simpler early stopping improving RealMLP CV to 0.98051. Several alternatives, including ridge stacking, pseudo-labeling, and SMOTE, were less successful.
compute: One feature-set experiment used FLAML parameters from a 1-hour run.

solution_title: Drug Detection for MOA solution post processing
solution_summary: The author proposes using drug identity to post-process predictions because experiments involving the same drug share its underlying identity. Adding a drug detector to a public kernel improved its public score from 0.01825 to 0.01816. The improvement appeared smaller on the private leaderboard, which the author attributes to less overlap between training and private-test drugs. The post asks how others incorporated drug identifiers into their final solutions.

The final submission combined four image models with BERT and TF-IDF text representations. Image embeddings and text representations were concatenated within their respective modalities before cosine-similarity matching. The main contribution was a dynamic matching threshold based on the mean of each row's six strongest similarities and quantiles of those means. Quantile-specific restriction coefficients made thresholds more restrictive for weaker similarity groups, improving over the author's static-threshold approach.

The team trained 80 models and selected eight less-correlated EfficientNet models for its ensemble. These used B4, B5, and B6 backbones at image sizes from 384 to 768, with some models including external data. The post describes rank ensembling and stacking, while reporting that mean ensembling scored about 0.9432 privately versus 0.9406 for rank ensembling. GAN and Chipnet experiments were left incomplete.

The solution added log-transformed pixel features, removed weak or redundant features, and applied robust and min-max scaling. It modeled eight classes, including a no-fault class. A voting ensemble of four boosting models used Optuna-tuned weights, and its predictions were combined with public predictions for submission. Adding Random Forest improved internal evaluation but did not perform well on the public leaderboard.

The solution combined LightGBM models using patient-group metadata features with image and multimodal neural networks. Image models used EfficientNet B1 and CAFormer S18, while auxiliary diagnostic targets enriched image training. Neural predictions became additional LightGBM features, and multimodal networks combined images with metadata through dot pooling. The expanded ensemble reported PB 176 and LB 185 in the author's notation, with ten-fold validation used across the main components.

The author trained three XGBoost models on differently curated mutation datasets, using structural, biochemical, and ESM-derived features. Feature construction focused on the 21 amino acids nearest the mutation site, including relative geometry and interactions between substitution scores and structural properties. The models used melting-temperature ranks or stability-related ddG targets, with dataset-specific filtering. A weighted blend with public structural and stability predictors achieved a reported private score of 0.542.

solution_title: ZLF's Solution in the MITSUI&CO. Commodity Prediction Challenge
solution_summary: The solution averages a four-day RNN and a single-day MLP, combining their relatively conservative and volatile predictions. Both models use all raw features, replace missing values with -1, and normalize internally with LayerNorm. Training combines MSE and ranking loss with learning-rate decay. Longer historical windows added noise, while the ensemble achieved a private score of 0.532 compared with 0.509 for the RNN alone.

solution_summary: The solution used ConvNeXt Base models trained on both the original 100-category dataset and an expanded 223-category dataset incorporating FGVC8 data. Combining the two training setups improved performance, followed by further gains from pseudo-labeling and five-fold ensembling. The final reported public and private scores were both 0.965.

The solution split patients into two groups based on their minimum observed visit interval, using cumulative information to recognize six-month patterns even when the six-month visit was missing. It constructed nine severity indicators from protein collection schedules, unique protein counts, and peptide changes. Rather than using LightGBM, the final model assigned severity coefficients through grid search. The author retained indicators that improved both training performance and leaderboard scores and reported stable final results.

Six pretrained language models were trained on the provided labels and then used to pseudo-label FB1 essays. A single DeBERTa-v3-small model was trained on the combined labeled and pseudo-labeled data for final inference. Adversarial weight perturbation improved single-model CV by 0.0007, and the final private score was 0.438587. Post-competition experiments found that batch size 1 reduced inference time to 30 minutes.

solution_summary: The solution ensembled XLM-R-large models trained on English or translated data, using the CLS token without additional layers. Models received two epochs of initial training followed by two epochs of five-fold fine-tuning on the validation set, with predictions averaged across repeated runs. Layer-wise weight decay, test-set pseudo-labels, balanced sampling, and mixed Google/Yandex translations improved performance. Additional masked-language-model pretraining on test data produced the strongest reported individual model, with approximately 0.9471 public AUC.

solution_summary: The author adjusted parameters of an open source solution with a reported leaderboard score of 0.422. They rejected the leaderboard-optimized option because they feared overfitting. The pipeline combined GPT-4o synthetic examples, Qwen-generated rationales, a contrastively trained Qwen retriever, and a causal language model reranker. Synthetic examples for known training misconceptions were filtered using a baseline model, while rare original examples were upsampled. The final reranker used yes-token logits from Qwen 2.5 32B and was AWQ-quantized after training. It achieved public and private scores of 0.641 and 0.571, while a smaller binary classification reranker was dropped for inefficiency.

The author built a diverse pool of tabular models and selected a weighted ensemble from 26 members, with some receiving zero weight. Ensemble weight searches were assessed by fitting on four folds and evaluating on the fifth. Reoptimizing weights across the whole pool was more useful than simply adding small contributions to an existing blend. The final private score was 0.94548, while a later income-token logistic regression experiment improved cross-validation AUC but had no private evaluation.

solution_summary: The solution aligned horizontal and typewell gamma-ray signals using prefix-anchored particle filtering, backward smoothing, and a small learned likelihood. Bounded spatial corrections and LightGBM path corrections complemented the particle estimates, with final selection using typewell-grouped validation. The selected ensemble combined a controller anchor at 70% weight with a six-family row median at 30%, achieving private RMSE of 7.122 ft. A retrospective five-family median achieved 7.012 ft, showing that model diversity transferred better than extensive controller tuning on repeatedly reused validation data.

solution_title: [Private27,Public28] Solution for 17th: To get code & fix it with DeepSeek

It sampled 16 responses, allocating four to code generation and twelve to boxed answers. A vLLM engine processed samples as they finished, and inference stopped once three identical answers appeared.

solution_title: 4th place solution: dynamic programming and ensembling
solution_summary: The solution used physics-based signal search rather than machine learning. Dynamic programming estimated candidate signal curves, parametric fitting recovered continuous-wave parameters, and Nelder–Mead refined them. A common judge selected the strongest candidate across search variants using the weaker detector's signal score. A frequency-dependent linear correction improved submission scores by 0.002–0.005.

The author adapted an existing Kore Beta agent into a rule-based system through repeated debugging, rule changes, and parameter tuning. The main additions were a time-indexed ledger of damage potential and route scoring across almost all candidate routes. Coordinated attacks, adaptive shipyard abandonment, expansion heuristics, and aggressive mining defined its behavior. Route-search optimization and cache management addressed runtime and memory limits, while an opponent exposed a shared weakness that could prevent early expansion.

solution_title: 122nd place🥈out of 4186 teams - AI Agent Security - Red-Teaming
solution_summary: The solution searched for workplace notification prompts that caused successful email.send calls without the benchmark's explicit consent keywords. It retained only candidates verified through execution traces, diversified recipients to obtain distinct scoring cells, and adapted generation to measured model latency. Single-hop interactions and a budget-aware stopping rule improved replay throughput. The approach scored 23.205 publicly and 20.760 privately, while the separately submitted exfiltration approach failed under private provenance tracking.

solution_title: 1st Place Solution - Trust CV (and LB a bit)

Two rounds of pseudo-labeling transferred the newer scoring criteria to older essays, while three-seed averaging reduced instability. Continuous predictions were converted to integer scores using optimized QWK thresholds, with ensemble weights also applied to individual model thresholds to limit overfitting. solution_title: A Naive Solution (28th in Private LB)

Frequency-wise statistics were converted into cluster distances without labels, improving individual models. solution_summary: The team retained two submissions: a high-public-score exfiltration attack and a benign-looking confused-deputy email request. They used a locally reconstructed private guardrail to anticipate which approach would survive hidden evaluation. The surviving request used routine business phrasing, a fake recipient, no secret payload, no preceding untrusted reads, and a final message avoiding the word “send.” The exfiltration submission fell from 92.6 public to zero private, while the confused-deputy submission achieved 15.95 private.

solution_title: Not Just Birds: Cross-Mutation Distillation meets Selective State Spaces
solution_summary: The solution combined CNN sound-event detectors with a Perch embedding branch that modeled entire recordings using Mamba and an auxiliary MLP. Soundscape pseudo-labels delivered the largest improvement by bridging the gap between focal training recordings and passive evaluation audio. Confidence filtering, waveform mixup, and cross-family teachers improved robustness, whereas repeated same-family self-training degraded performance. Classwise rank fusion and insect-group score mirroring produced 96.0% public and 95.4% private scores, although extensive public-leaderboard tuning limited confidence in generalization.

solution_summary: The selected submission extended a Select-Patch-Verify workflow with generated pytest tests to screen candidate code patches. Tree-sitter supplied function- and class-level context, and LLM self-checks and confidence assessment helped prioritize promising attempts. The pipeline reduced attempts and thinking time while using parallel processing, compression, caching, and early stopping for efficiency. It scored 0.016571 privately with four correct patches, two wrong patches, and 114 skips; a more expensive multiple-patch selection strategy performed worse overall.

The solution trained a large-kernel convolutional model on PyFstat-generated signals, using the supplied training data for validation. Correcting the signal-generation parameter ranges and combining frequency normalization with percentile-based scaling improved performance. Dense detector-channel convolutions, strong weight decay, and EMA further improved the model. The final reported scores were 0.773 private and 0.761 public, while gap-filling augmentation was abandoned because it destabilized training.

The solution trained eight CNN classifiers using full-body crops, back-fin crops, original images, and mixed crop sources. Their embeddings were concatenated and combined through a shallow MLP trained with ArcFace and dropout. Mixing full-body and back-fin training images improved diversity, increasing one back-fin model's score from 77.8% to 80.0%. Prediction-frequency heuristics then reordered candidates, improving the MLP score from 0.865 to 0.868.

The core model projected each sensor sequence into 16 dimensions and processed each of the 13 sequences with a separate four-layer GRU. Separating the sequences reduced overfitting to noisy relationships between sensors and improved convergence. This model scored 0.9839 on the private leaderboard. Combining it with XGBoost, a one-dimensional convolutional model, and public LSTM models increased the final private score to 0.98797.

The code reads the competition's sample submission and saves it as submission.csv without an index column. It copies the template values directly, with no model training or prediction generation shown. No evaluation results are reported.

The team combined diverse EEG models using raw signals, supplied spectrograms, and several signal-to-image transformations. Base models used two-stage training, first on all EEG IDs and then on samples with at least eight votes. A 2D CNN stacked out-of-fold predictions from nine models, with model selection and hyperparameters optimized using Optuna. The stacker achieved public/private scores of 0.23/0.28 compared with 0.24/0.29 for simple averaging, and its final predictions used five-seed averaging.
compute: TR models trained for 20 epochs: ten on all votes, followed by ten on vote counts ≥8.

solution_title: [34th Place Solution] Silver Lining only ( Not on LB anymore )
solution_summary: The author combined LightGBM regression ensembles for several forecast horizons with classification models using the same features. Demand was normalized by price, and rolling skewness was especially important among the temporal features. A classification threshold selected on the last 56 validation days improved validation WRMSSE from 0.494 to 0.483. The final submission omitted the tested multiplier and achieved a private score of 0.56602.

solution_title: 606th place: good CV & ensembling don't make up for mediocre individual models
solution_summary: The solution combines diverse image classifiers using stratified group five-fold validation and regularized, target-specific ensemble weights. Final submissions combine probability, power, and rank averages, followed by equally weighted rank averaging, and include two public notebook models. Large images helped, while gradient accumulation, mixed precision, and frozen BatchNorm layers accommodated limited GPU memory. Ensembling improved both CV and leaderboard scores by 0.008 over the best individual model; the selected submissions achieved private scores of 0.969 and 0.968.

solution_summary: The team ensembled 12 DeBERTa-v3-large token classifiers with diverse context lengths and external training datasets. Members first combined their own models, then voted across member ensembles; longer contexts generalized better on the private leaderboard. Training included class-weighted losses, layer freezing, EMA, and staged use of external datasets. Rule-based filtering removed malformed predictions and false positives, while mixed-precision inference allowed more models within the runtime budget.

solution_title: 123rd (public 6th) Solution - Tile-based ViT with 2D Pos-Emb & MIL pooling
solution_summary: The solution represented each image as 32 spatially arranged tiles, extracted ViT features, and combined them using 2D positional embeddings and multi-head MIL attention pooling. It predicted three main biomass targets and reconstructed two others under physical ordering constraints. Training combined metric-aligned regression losses, auxiliary consistency supervision, and distillation from a metadata teacher that was absent at inference. The reported full OOF score was 0.7615, with public/private scores of 0.78/0.62; the author suspected metadata priors and insufficiently strict validation contributed to the generalization drop.

The solution combined seven XGBoost models through hill climbing, using 30-fold stratified validation with an inner five-fold loop. Smoothed target encoding, invalid-date correction, feature removal, and majority-label correction for duplicated training rows supported the models. Date-leak postprocessing further improved predictions, while LightGBM and CatBoost were discarded for weaker scores and unreliable CV-to-leaderboard correspondence. A later update reported substantial gains from assigning 0.5 to 253 duplicate pairs in the test data.

The author adapted a public notebook and experimented with external datasets, TF-IDF settings, essay duplication, and classifier contributions. Dataset expansion and a reduced TF-IDF feature limit improved both public and private scores. Removing LightGBM and extending the n-gram range improved public scores while hurting private performance. In retrospect, the author concluded that CatBoost and LightGBM deserved greater importance and that public-score-driven decisions degraded the solution.

The solution used a two-stage pipeline: 3D organ segmentation followed by organ-level 2.5D CNN and LSTM classification. An EfficientNet V2S U-Net produced masks used to crop organs, with the kidney masks combined. Each organ was represented by 20 evenly spaced slices, adjacent slices supplied image channels, and the predicted organ mask provided an additional channel. The final submission used five-fold segmentation and ResNet50d classification models, achieving reported public and private scores of 0.65 and 0.59.
compute: Submission runtime around 180 minutes, mostly data loading.

solution_summary: The final solution combined LoFTR DS/OT, SuperPoint/SuperGlue, DKM, and MatchFormer-LargeLA and scored 0.835. The largest improvement came from upscaling images by 1.5 using Lanczos interpolation for every model except MatchFormer. Images were trimmed to dimensions divisible by eight, and keypoint coordinates were rescaled afterward. OpenCV MAGSAC removed outlier matches, while several fine-tuning and matching variants failed to improve the score.

The author trained Swin-L models at 224 and 384 resolution with five stratified folds and four-way test-time augmentation. Separate support vector regressors used each model's activations together with metadata. Ridge regression blended the four prediction streams and metadata. A further Swin-L model trained on all labeled data plus noisy pseudo-labeled test examples contributed 10% of the final prediction.

solution_title: Approach(3rd in public and 8th in private)
solution_summary: The team's best submission bagged 14 models, with logistic regression and neural networks identified as key components. This writeup focuses on the logistic regression component, using original features excluding calc features together with two-, three-, and four-way interactions. All listed features were one-hot encoded. The logistic regression model scored 0.2856 in five-fold cross-validation, 0.280 publicly, and 0.284 privately, and its diversity made it useful in the ensemble.

The final submissions ensembled 13 and 11 pretrained language models, with weights optimized by Nelder-Mead using both CV and leaderboard objectives. The larger ensemble mainly used DeBERTa-large, supplemented by ALBERT, ELECTRA, and RoBERTa, with combinations of pooled regression heads. Additional Wikipedia pretraining combined masked language modeling with filtered, fold-specific pseudo targets before competition fine-tuning. Reinitializing upper layers, pseudo-target pretraining, and ensembling provided the largest improvements; both final submissions achieved a private score of 0.449.

solution_title: 14th place decision (12th after checking LB by kaggle)
solution_summary: The author selected two standalone XGBoost models predicting price per square meter, with no final ensembling or multiplier adjustments. Careful area correction, extreme-target removal, and location-based categorical interactions drove the approach. A repeated chronological validation scheme with partial undersampling of extreme-low-price transactions guided feature selection, while built-in XGBoost cross-validation selected boosting rounds. The strongest model added sub-area interactions and importance-based feature selection, slightly improving private performance.

solution_title: 4th Place Solution: a MultiLayer Bidirectional GRU with Residual Connections
solution_summary: The best model was a residual bidirectional GRU with fully connected layers, trained jointly on tdcsfog and defog accelerometer sequences. Sequences were downsampled to 50 Hz, standardized individually, and processed whole with batch size one. Training masked unlabeled steps and added a fourth no-activity class, using cross entropy and Ranger. The best single split model scored 0.417 privately, while a five-fold averaged model scored 0.415.

solution_title: 22th Place Solution - single yolov8m with Pseudo label
solution_summary: The final submission used a single YOLOv8m detector with rotation test-time augmentation. The approach combined extensive image augmentation, iterative pseudo-labeling to recover missing annotations, corrected training-label generation, and added negative samples. Additional annotated data and small-object loss functions improved generalization and detection. A tested 2.5D DEiM variant achieved high recall but performed poorly on the leaderboard.

solution_title: 10th solution, good input image can generate a good single model (Opensource single model with LB233 PB287)
solution_summary: The solution encoded richer EEG information into images, combining 19 differential channels, a central 10-second segment, and raw EEG. EfficientViT and MixNet backbones were trained with Adan, with high-vote examples receiving extra weight and separate prediction heads for the two vote groups. Evaluation normalized contributions by EEG ID. An ensemble of 20 models provided a modest improvement, with Optuna-derived weights performing better online than a simple mean.

The solution replaced implausible values with NaN and combined AutoGluon and LightAutoML predictions with equal weights. AutoGluon used the team's 2024 collection of 200 hyperparameter configurations, while LightAutoML ran a broad collection of tree and neural models. Cleaning improved cross-validation and both leaderboard scores. Model choices emphasized cross-validation, although AutoGluon's estimates appeared somewhat optimistic.

solution_summary: The team ensembled a public DeBERTa-v3-large baseline with two variants built from the same notebook. Both variants used multi-sample dropout, and one additionally used adversarial weight perturbation with small perturbation settings. CNN and LSTM heads did not help, while concatenating the last 12 transformer layers caused inference memory exhaustion. The ensemble achieved 0.96998 publicly and 0.96028 privately.

The solution combined 11 DeBERTa-v3-large models and six DeBERTa-v3-base models trained with different learning rates. Disabling hidden dropout and jointly predicting wording and content improved the pipeline, while enhanced LightGBM feature engineering also contributed strongly. Uniform ensemble weights were preferred because Optuna-tuned weights overfit despite improving cross-validation. The best reported feature-enhanced ensemble scored 0.43551 on LB and 0.47284 on PB.

solution_summary: The final pipeline used native MXFP4 GPT-OSS-120B without fine-tuning, combining Python tool execution with eight sampled solutions and majority voting. Correcting the Harmony identity and developer-message formatting was the author's main reported improvement, reducing Python tool calls substantially. Numerous alternative selection methods and three LoRA experiments did not improve the final approach. The final submission scored 39/50 on both leaderboards, while identical-code public runs scored 39, 33, and 34.

solution_summary: The solution centered on Perch v2 feature distillation and five rounds of Noisy Student MixUp with pseudo-labeled soundscapes. Confidence-weighted window sampling and progressively greater pseudo-label exposure raised the reported single-model score from 0.921 to 0.937. A site/time FiLM model and a previous-year backbone fine-tuned without distillation supplied useful ensemble diversity. The final system equally averaged its models and applied probability-space Gaussian smoothing, which consistently improved scores.

solution_title: Congrats and 8th place Rapids solution updated!
solution_summary: The solution combined engineered light-curve features with nonlinear stacking of tree models and neural networks. Careful internal validation and simpler second-level models reduced stacking overfitting. The major improvement came from repeatedly training attention-based recurrent networks on pseudo-labeled test data and extracting their bottleneck features. Alternating GRU and LSTM models, predicting the next flux difference as an auxiliary task, and validating on true training labels helped successive iterations improve the reported leaderboard score from 0.95 to 0.80.

solution_summary: The final agent relied entirely on imitation learning from strong agents' replays. Training began with several agents, followed by freezing most of the network and fine-tuning the last three layers on Toad Brigade replays. One shared model produced unit and city-tile actions in a single forward pass per turn, with invalid-action masking and collision avoidance. Horizontal flipping helped training, while flip-based test-time augmentation offered little benefit and sometimes exceeded time limits. PPO experiments failed to improve the imitation-learning agent, with noisy per-unit advantages identified as a likely obstacle.

The final solution ensembled ResNest50 and MobileNetV2 audio classifiers. Gaussian, pink, and background noise augmentation helped, while validation scores correlated weakly with leaderboard performance. Incorporating secondary labels produced the strongest reported private score of 0.616. Sound event detection, an explicit nocall class, test denoising, and alternative losses did not improve results.

solution_title: 10th place solution: Grandmaster Powered Agentic Approach
solution_summary: The solution combined two 3D cell detectors, self-supervised appearance embeddings, a transformer linker, and track-level post-processing. A four-seed image classifier ensemble verified divisions and recovered missing daughters, while a separately linked 2.5D detector conservatively added missing tracks. Leave-one-embryo-out validation guided development, with full-fit models used for submission. The pipeline achieved 0.903 cross-validation and 0.948 private leaderboard scores; the auxiliary tracks contributed about 0.002 in cross-validation.

The pipeline trained XLM-RoBERTa with ArcFace loss to represent locations. Embedding cosine similarities and coordinate distances retrieved candidate matches. A LightGBM binary classifier then selected matches using similarity, distance, longest common subsequence, and TF-IDF features, with FLAML tuning its hyperparameters. The approach used no ensemble.

solution_title: [The 11th place] Shallow encoder-decoder model also works
solution_summary: The author trained a Conformer encoder and Transformer decoder on x/y landmark sequences with a joint CTC and cross-entropy objective. Validation held out unique phrases, while augmentation concatenated samples and corrupted decoder input characters. Training progressed from the training split to all competition and supplemental data, followed by adversarial weight perturbation. Encoder-only and autoregressive decoding both achieved 0.791 on the public leaderboard, and FP16 inference preserved accuracy while outperforming dynamic quantization in speed.

solution_title: Changing the Target Approach   ( Top 10% solution )
solution_summary: The approach modeled open-channel counts as Markov states and used LightGBM to predict whether the state would change from the previous timestep. A final LightGBM model combined this predicted change probability with iteratively predicted previous channel counts, the signal, percentage changes, and neighboring signal values. Predictions were organized into similar subbatches of 100,000 samples, with initial channel counts taken from public kernels. The model achieved 94.2+ on cross-validation and 94.389 on the private leaderboard.

solution_title: # Orbit Wars: Replay-Driven Tuning of a ProducerLite Agent
solution_summary: The final agent adapted the public Lyonel ProducerLite greedy planner, retaining its two-player policy. Four-player behavior changed only by widening the source shortlist from six to seven and reducing the ROI threshold from 1.50 to 1.45. Replay analysis identified inactivity and idle ship accumulation as key weaknesses, while local tournaments correlated poorly with public ratings. More aggressive settings and complex hybrid policies did not deliver dependable improvements; the selected final agent scored 1110.3.

The final model blended a ten-fold LightGBM model with a five-fold neural network using weights of 1 and 0.75. Numerical interaction features, target encoding, deeper trees, and strong regularization were important for tree performance. Agent-swapping augmentation and flipped test-time predictions improved results, while the neural network used binned numerical features and tree-leaf features. The best blend reported LB 416 and PB 423, but validation-based ensemble weights did not generalize reliably.

The solution used a frozen LAION-2B-pretrained OpenCLIP ViT-H/14 encoder and trained a 64-dimensional embedding head with ArcFace. Dataset selection, strong weight decay, and concatenated image dimensions were central, with size metadata improving the public score by about 0.003. Validation included held-out classes to measure zero-shot retrieval, and checkpoints were selected by MAP5 on that set. Inference used aspect-ratio- and category-dependent augmentation averaging, together with antialiased resizing.

A VGG-based coordinate regressor used mean squared error and both training and test-time augmentation. The identity classifier combined three VGG networks and three ResNets, with no augmentation applied to the aligned classifier inputs. Explicit localization supplied essential supervision because classification directly from raw images performed poorly.

An alternative trained pipeline used audio augmentation, CutMix, MixUp, and combined binary cross-entropy and focal losses, with neighboring-window predictions added during inference. solution_summary: The pipeline first localized spinal levels and keypoints, then classified severity from crops around those locations. It combined multi-view classifiers using slice features, transformers, and attention pooling with single-view 2.5D CNN classifiers. Auxiliary supervision before the transformer was important for training the multi-view models. Final predictions were refined with Nelder-Mead-guided MLP stacking and tree-based stacking.

The solution combined SuperPoint–SuperGlue and DISK–SuperGlue pipelines with LoFTR and DKM. Refinement improved SuperGlue matches, and match-level non-maximum suppression combined methods while filtering nearby keypoints by score. Adaptive augmentation transformed images using the initial matching results and then matched them again. The reported private score increased from 0.77974 for the refined SuperPoint–SuperGlue pipeline to 0.83904 with the ensemble and 0.85866 with adaptive augmentation.

The solution combined segmentation models with EfficientNet classifiers and extensive mask postprocessing. Training used geometric augmentations, stratification by mask count, and BCE plus Dice loss without preprocessing. Segmentation predictions were averaged, then filtered through cascading classifiers, pixel and small-mask thresholds, and convex hull processing. The submission scored 0.67698 publicly and 0.66713 privately; the authors attributed the decline mainly to weak segmentation models.

solution_title: 10th place solution: Fast or Slow with Graph Transformers
solution_summary: The solution used graph transformers with intermediate configuration fusion to preserve node-specific information while sharing graph computation across many configurations. Tile and layout models combined local graph processing with global attention, and XLA and NLP layouts were trained separately. Training used listMLE with large configuration batches, while unstable validation motivated diverse model ensembles. The broad ensemble scored 0.696 on the private leaderboard, while a gated APPNP submission reached 0.715.

A LightGBM model combined these outputs with simple text statistics, learning a target derived from the proportion of comparisons in which a comment was more toxic. The reported public and private scores were 0.79242 and 0.81062.

Most base models used logistic regression over words, stems, POS tags, character n-grams, and subsequence features, with probability-based feature scoring. Stem subsequence models dominated the final ensemble, while syntax, language models, and mixed stem/POS features contributed much less. Sentence-level models and ranking models supplied additional signals, and training took about 10 hours.

solution_title: 1st place solution - New augmentation method + 5 model ensemble
solution_summary: The solution combined five image embedding models operating at two image sizes, trained with ArcFace loss. Its central innovation was BlendFlip, which fills occlusions by blending flipped neighboring image content while preserving scene coherence. Concatenated embeddings were reduced to 3072 dimensions with PCA and used for nearest-neighbor retrieval. BlendFlip contributed approximately 0.03–0.04 mAP, and no re-ranking or additional post-processing was applied.

Validation stratified jointly on Class, Alpha, and Gamma, while larger image representations and Epsilon-based modeling did not help. A promising unselected CNN achieved a private score of 0.40326, and post-competition changes improved this to 0.37649.

The team explored a 3D CNN and a CNN–bidirectional LSTM pipeline for abdominal trauma classification. A U-Net trained on competition segmentation masks identified abdominal boundaries and removed uninformative slices before resizing each series to 128×128×64. The sequential pipeline reused the U-Net encoder to extract slice features and removed zero-valued feature dimensions. The 3D CNN performed poorly, while training VGG16 and ResNet50b from scratch also gave unsatisfactory results.

It used 129 landmarks with x/y coordinates, temporal sampling, standardization, and motion and hand-distance features. Pose augmentation, label smoothing, and scheduled dropout improved performance. The final fp16 ensemble achieved 0.779 public leaderboard accuracy with a reported latency of 60 ms per sample.

solution_title: 191th Place Solution: Imitation Learning for Deck 312
solution_summary: The solution trained a reactive Deck 312 policy through listwise behavior cloning over each state's complete legal-action set. Public history, resource estimates, and explicit card semantics supplied tactical context, while training-only auxiliary targets taught turn-level dependencies. The mature V76 architecture used state self-attention, action-to-state cross-attention, action self-attention, and a gated residual base policy, trained from scratch on a larger corpus. It reached 79.06% validation and 79.41% test top-1 accuracy and won 53.1% of 1,000 seat-balanced games against V67.

The author used a shared notebook and explored additional features and model blends. Experiments included pause-time features at 30, 60, and 90 and a change to TF-IDF vectorization. Adding random forest, SVM, and CatBoost models to the blend also failed to improve the score.

The author treated diabetic retinopathy grading as regression with clipped predictions and found EfficientNet-B2 and B4 strongest among the tested architectures. Training used 2015 competition data and pretrained weights, with both cropped and uncropped image variants. Attempts to align validation with leaderboard performance and use discriminative learning rates were unsuccessful. Selecting and ensembling strong models with different crops and complexity improved the reported leaderboard score to 0.814.

Useful inputs included magnitudes, parametric curve fits and fitting losses, time-series statistics, CAR tau, and colors derived from observed and fitted magnitudes. Manual feature selection and augmentation focused on non-DDF samples helped address overfitting and the train-test sampling mismatch. Color features improved the single-model leaderboard score from 0.836 to 0.815, while the reported cross-validation score remained substantially more optimistic.

The full-data model scored 0.967 on both public and private leaderboards without external data or final pseudo labeling.

solution_title: 25th Place Solution (time warpping + relative positional encoding + intermediate CTC)
solution_summary: The author adapted a previous ASL solution using alternating convolutional and transformer blocks. Random time warping and relative positional attention reportedly improved leaderboard performance by 0.01 and 0.02 respectively. Training used intermediate and final CTC losses on training plus supplementary data for 300 epochs. Fine-tuning only on training data with the final CTC loss added a reported 0.005 improvement.

The solution combined PyTorch ResNet-family models with TensorFlow EfficientNet models at several image resolutions. The PyTorch models extended an existing three-step training method with soft labels, while the TensorFlow branch also used pseudo-labeling. Ensemble weights were learned by fitting linear regression to out-of-fold predictions, and final submissions were selected using cross-validation and public scores. The two submitted ensembles achieved private leaderboard scores of 0.973 and 0.974.

solution_summary: The author focused primarily on extensive feature derivation, reporting roughly 1,300 lines of feature-processing code. The linked notebook describes an approach using solely LightGBM, while the post provides few modeling details. Six runs without a specified random seed produced LB scores of 0.433–0.436 and PB scores of 0.458–0.462. The approach was not selected for final evaluation because of its public leaderboard performance.

The strongest submission evolved from an EfficientNet B4 trained through successive classification and ArcNet heads. Experiment normalization, cell-type-specific classes, metric learning, and plate constraints improved predictions substantially. Iterative probability normalization and repeated pseudo-label training on train and test data were central to the later gains. Blending the strongest pseudo-labeled models failed, while reducing pseudo-label exposure and improving the distance metric reached a reported leaderboard score of 0.943.
compute: Mostly Kaggle GPUs; best model trained exclusively on Kaggle in about 13 runs, approximately 100 hours excluding abandoned branches.

solution_summary: The final ensemble combined two LightGBM models built on DeBERTa-Base predictions with direct DeBERTa-Large predictions. Different feature sets and hyperparameters provided diversity between the LightGBM models. DeBERTa-Large training was stabilized through last-layer reinitialization, attention pooling, layer-wise learning-rate decay, and a fixed final checkpoint. Target-specific ensemble weights optimized on out-of-fold predictions produced 0.489 CV and 0.473 private score despite a slightly worse public score.

solution_title: 7th Place Solution: Solving Bitmanipulation via String Matching and Backtracking
solution_summary: The team focused its main innovations on bit manipulation puzzles, reframing logic-gate deduction as discrete feature selection over primitive transformations and truth tables. A deterministic search detected contradictions and backtracked to recover from incorrect hypotheses. Single-bit tokenization and supervised fine-tuning with dynamic loss masking taught the model to hypothesize, evaluate, and backtrack. The approach exceeded 96% validation accuracy, while symbolic equation puzzles received no training.

The approach combined EfficientDet and Faster R-CNN FPN detectors trained with custom mosaic, MixUp, and extensive image augmentation. External wheat images were annotated and cropped, while tiny and oversized training boxes were cleaned. Nine multiscale models were fused with weighted boxes fusion and augmented inference. Two rounds of pseudo-label training improved the new-test-set private AP from 0.6787 after the first round to 0.6897 after the second.

solution_title: Computer scientist Jure Zbontar on winning the Eurovision challenge
solution_summary: The solution combined historical country-to-country voting averages with transformed betting odds. Historical averages were smoothed by adding one to both the accumulated points and observation count, while betting odds were converted using an inverse-log formula with tuned coefficients. Summed scores determined each country's predicted points, and bookmaker rankings selected semifinal qualifiers. Leave-one-event-out cross-validation guided model selection and was identified as the most important component.

The solution emphasized diversity across LightGBM, neural networks, and XGBoost, then combined their out-of-fold predictions and main features in CatBoost. Models used five-fold stratification based on weekday and binned deal probability. Text normalization, TF-IDF, image features, categorical embeddings, and locally trained word embeddings supplied complementary signals. The final stack scored 0.2171 on the public leaderboard and 0.2210 on the private leaderboard; an additional stacking layer offered no meaningful improvement.

The author used a heavy ensemble of LightGBM and neural-network models. For the neural networks, missing values were filled with zero and sequences were handled using pack_padded_sequence. The post links released code but warns that random fluctuations may prevent reproduction of the best result; most architectural details appear only in figures and are not specified in the supplied text.

The solution trained 3D U-Net and residual U-Net variants with deep supervision after intensity clipping and min-max scaling. Training used case-separated five-fold validation, volumetric crops, several augmentations, and SGD with a polynomial learning-rate schedule. Inference combined overlapping sliding-window predictions using Gaussian center weights, without test-time augmentation or post-processing. False positives near truncated bottom voxels remained a weakness affecting Dice and Hausdorff scores.
compute: 1,000 epochs, approximately 60 seconds per epoch; hardware unspecified.

solution_summary: The solution preserved most baseline predictions, leaving B and E unchanged and modifying fewer than 5% of rows. It combined one teammate's G predictions with the author's ACDF predictions, using GBMs for individual ACDF values. Previous shopping-point product choices and cost changes were useful features. State-specific rules corrected unsupported purchase values in Georgia and Florida.

solution_title: I should have won gold medal and 12th by trusting my augmentation approach
solution_summary: The author describes an augmentation approach using only tabular data. They considered it stable but did not select it for their submission. The post links a related notebook without explaining the augmentation procedure or reporting scores.

The neural network consumes play, player, and rusher features and uses attention to represent relationships between the rusher and other players. Rusher attention was the main improvement, boosting the public score by approximately 0.00020–0.00030, while play attention also contributed. Training used RAdam, a multistep learning-rate schedule, and exponential moving averages. Restricting the final training epochs to 2018–2019 data improved local validation, while several alternative architectures and regularizers failed.

solution_title: Rank 2 approach - brute force ensembling (118 oofs)
solution_summary: The solution generated diverse out-of-fold predictions using several AutoML frameworks and custom gradient-boosting models, then combined them with Ridge regression and a nonlinear TabNet ensemble. Categorizing health score was a major feature improvement, while CatBoost stacking features provided smaller gains. Separate feature sets from community engineering and automatic feature generation increased prediction diversity. Adding the original dataset improved tuned models from roughly 1.031 to 1.027 CV, and local scores closely tracked public leaderboard scores.

solution_title: 7th place solution, segmentation for detection tasks
solution_summary: The pipeline used separate 3D U-Nets to segment cervical vertebrae and fracture regions, followed by a small 3D CNN to predict final scores. Fracture masks were initialized from augmentation and bounding boxes, then refined using patient-level labels to expand supervision to 823 cases. Per-vertebra score clipping was tuned on cross-validation. The final ensemble achieved public/private scores of 0.2127/0.2634, although a single model performed similarly.

solution_title: 241st place (bronze) solution (+ GitHub) with batch sampling
solution_summary: The solution combined five EfficientNet B4 and B5 models at 384×384 and 512×512 resolutions using a weighted average with an exponential-log transformation. Models used global average pooling, a dense sigmoid head, Adam, and label smoothing of 0.05. Sampling from both the full dataset and a malignant-only dataset accelerated convergence, while a cosine learning-rate schedule included warm restarts and warm-up. Training used extensive augmentation, with a lighter augmentation pipeline for prediction, and cross-validation successfully guided submission selection.
compute: TPUs from Kaggle and Colab

solution_summary: The solution adapted STTRE to player tracking, combining temporal, spatial, and joint attention branches with role-aware attention and gated fusion. Direction normalization and random mirrored trajectories reduced the learning space, while auxiliary velocity loss encouraged physically consistent motion. A heterogeneous ensemble combined STTRE, an evolving-subgraph GNN, and a bidirectional GRU using separate speed and direction aggregation with horizon-dependent GRU weights. The reported public score was 0.519, with sharp directional cuts remaining a major weakness.

The solution generated synthetic wells that imitated the presumed annotation process, then trained candidate scorers and structured sequence decoders. It combined neighboring-well transfer, particle filtering, CNN likelihoods, forward–backward inference, and an absolute Transformer decoder. Synthetic pretraining followed by brief real-data fine-tuning and uncertainty-aware decoding produced major gains. The final uncertainty-conditioned recombination of stage corrections achieved pooled CV RMSE 5.028 and private RMSE 6.504, while further CV optimization degraded leaderboard performance.

The author used a single generalized additive model without ensembling. Validation held out three-month chunks to obtain relatively stable estimates. The model learned patterns from training years and projected them forward under assumptions about which behaviors would continue. The final submission added a spline to capture the Christmas-to-New-Year period.

The pipeline retrieves DOI and accession candidates from external citation corpora, verifies their presence in article text, and falls back to regex plus LLM filtering. Qwen classifiers were warmed up on agent-generated synthetic labels and fine-tuned on competition data, with pseudo-labeling, mention masking, article-level caps, and EMA supporting robustness and diversity. Classification contexts combine article metadata, mention snippets, availability sections, other DOIs, and table context. Cascaded inference routes uncertain cases from 14B to 32B and then 72B models, while repository-specific shortcuts and DOI-based accession removal reduce inference cost and false positives.

solution_summary: The final solution equally averaged a long model using the source prompt text and a short model excluding it. The long model targeted summary fidelity, while the short model targeted sentence structure and word quality. LightGBM trained on pooled representations improved robustness, and the short pipeline used DeBERTa-v3-large with modified overlap features and layer-freezing variants. Text cleaning, other backbones, MLM, adversarial weight perturbation, ChatGPT augmentation, and alternative regressors did not help.

solution_title: Private LB 105th / Public LB 970th solution and first medal 🥳
solution_summary: The team used only competition data and stratified five-fold validation. Their final submissions blended EfficientNet B1 NS, EfficientNet B3 NS, and ResNeXt50 models trained at 512×512, with selective test-time augmentation. Larger images consistently improved scores, and training used image augmentation, label-smoothed losses, Adam, and learning-rate schedules. The stronger selected blend achieved a private score of 0.8999.

solution_summary: The pipeline used an initial XGBoost model to remove easy negatives, separate video CNNs for player-player and player-ground contact, and a final XGBoost postprocessor. The CNNs fine-tuned resnet50-irCSN on helmet-marked crops from both camera views, with rendered tracking images added only for player-player contact. Models were trained for one epoch on all data with four seeds. Temporal postprocessing improved cross-validation by approximately 0.005 for player-player contact and 0.04 for player-ground contact.

solution_summary: The solution trained nnUnetTrainerMedialSurfaceRecall with axis-specific rotation augmentation and ensembled five folds plus an all-data model. Inference distributed flip augmentations among the six models and averaged predictions across two GPUs. Extensive topology post-processing used geodesic watershed, loop opening and filling, gap closure, and cavity manipulation. Post-processing strength varied by scroll, while merged sheets and unlabeled regions remained difficult.
compute: Inference parallelized across two T4 GPUs; ensemble inference took six hours.

solution_summary: The author explored spectrally normalized GANs and highlighted conditional GANs with projection discriminators as particularly promising. They reported strong qualitative performance from projection after trying several GAN families. The post links papers and implementations but gives no quantitative evaluation or complete training pipeline. The author states that teammates used a completely different competition solution.

The strongest agent combined behavioral cloning from strong-agent replays with PUCT Monte Carlo Tree Search. A torus-aware convolutional network predicted every player's policy and game outcome, while search added action masking, adaptive time allocation, and policy-shift-based move selection. Online opponent modeling mixed predicted policies with uniform noise to accommodate unpredictable players. The team also explored self-play reinforcement learning and fast handcrafted search, but these did not surpass the final combination.
compute: 8-core/16-thread dual-GPU machine with 32GB RAM; neural MCTS ran about 20–50 iterations per second on Kaggle servers.

solution_summary: The author adapted a translation model to Akkadian through span-masking pretraining before supervised fine-tuning. Manual sentence alignment cleanup and removal of incomplete translations improved the training data. Fine-tuning used differential learning rates, weight decay tuning, and a maximum token length of 3048. Final predictions combined three models, while pseudo-labeling, training ByT5 from scratch, and recurrent heads on T5 did not work.

solution_title: I'm ineligible for the prize - congrats to Quan Sun
solution_summary: The author explored application success rates with Excel pivot tables and engineered predictors from dates, missing fields, grant attributes, and associated people. Person-level information was represented using both individual values and aggregates across applicants. Rare categorical groups were consolidated, while missing continuous values received median imputation and separate missingness indicators. A custom generalization of random forests was trained using C# libraries developed during the competition.

The author's main submission ensembled eight models across image sizes from 256 to 768 pixels, using EfficientNet-B6 and metadata. Training incorporated 2017–2020 TFRecords, hair augmentation, and heavy test-time augmentation. Cross-validation guided experiments, while the final models trained on all available data without a validation holdout. Adding predictions from two public notebooks increased the private score from 0.9481 to 0.9484 and the public score from 0.9596 to 0.9620.

The author attempted semi-supervised joint learning of video-level and segment-level classification. Data were converted from TFRecords into memory-mapped storage, and videos were filtered to relevant annotated classes. A Transformer backbone used pooling or an RNN to generate segment predictions, with segment loss applied only where labels existed. The attempt failed because segment predictions always returned class zero, which the author suspected was an implementation bug.

solution_title: rank68_the_ simplest idea to get the first medal

Pipeline changes included setting the maximum number of contexts to 130 and specifying sequence and answer-length limits. Short- and long-answer score thresholds were set to 7.5 and 1.5. A PyTorch conversion was also tried but did not improve results.

solution_summary: The solution equally averaged predictions from two public notebooks with reported leaderboard scores of 0.654 and 0.632. It then smoothed predictions within each audio file by mixing the file-wide average at 75% with each individual row at 25%. The ensemble ran in approximately one hour. Although the public score improved slightly, the private improvement over the stronger source notebook was minimal.

solution_summary: The author trained segmentation models with Maxout activations and outputs for both the mask and the probability that a mask is present. Auxiliary downsampled masks provided additional training supervision. PCA post-processing encouraged realistic mask shapes, and binary cross-entropy performed better than a Dice-like loss.

solution_title: 8th place - gold zone!! with diversity(My part)💪💪
solution_summary: The author's contribution combined several transformer backbones with diverse pooling heads, hidden-layer concatenation, and LSTM layers. Mask-aware attention pooling was particularly effective, and DeBERTa-v3-large benefited from a special selection of three hidden layers. ELECTRA training used a small learning rate, different seeds across folds, and layer-wise learning-rate decay, alongside loss and initialization experiments. The final ensemble varied sequence length, pooling, and loss functions; reported single-model CV scores ranged from 0.4464 to 0.4555.

solution_title: 45th place - Not bad as for first competition :)

The solution adapted Agentless 1.5 to run locally with Qwen2.5 Coder 32B, using retrieved repository context to generate issue reproduction tests and repair candidates. A staged localization pipeline produced eight candidate patches using search/replace edits. Patches were screened for applicability, issue resolution, and preservation of existing unit test behavior, with samples skipped when reliable reproduction tests were unavailable. solution_summary: The author trained an SE-NeXt 50 model on 96 × 96 images because of limited compute. Test-time augmentation progressively cropped image edges, resized the crops back to the training resolution, and added horizontal flips for twelve predictions per image. Selecting the top prediction increased the private score from 0.08695 to 0.14681. Averaging probabilities for shared classes produced a worse score.

solution_summary: The final solution used one SE-ResNeXt-50-based model trained across five folds, with horizontal-flip test-time augmentation. Inputs combined the source image, relative depth, and a CoordConv channel at 128 × 128 resolution; the architecture added spatial-channel attention and hypercolumns. Adam with a triangular cyclic learning rate and weighted snapshot averaging supported training, while removing dropout improved results. Post-processing removed small masks and connected components, and higher output thresholds helped private performance.
compute: 1080 Ti and 1070 Ti GPUs for training.

solution_summary: The author's contribution combined three model types to learn cell predictions from weak image labels. Attention pooled either cropped-cell predictions or cell embeddings extracted from whole-image feature maps, while an image-level EfficientNet-B7 improved prediction ranking. Similar and duplicate images were grouped for validation, and additional HPA images expanded training data. Distilling ensemble out-of-fold predictions into a single-cell model yielded a lightweight model with a public score of 0.524.

solution_summary: The approach models each target class as three Gaussian clusters rather than a single ellipse. Class-conditional Gaussian mixtures assign six cluster labels, which become the targets for QDA; probabilities for the three positive-class clusters are then summed. Histograms of class-conditioned feature means supported the inference of three clusters per class. The writeup reports an improvement from LB 0.970 with QDA and pseudo-labeling to LB 0.975 with the six-ellipse approach.

The team combined nine neural models using a weighted average, including CNN–Transformer–LSTM hybrids, Transformer models, and a FiLM 1D U-Net. Humidity features, vertical derivatives, auxiliary derivative prediction, and full LowRes training were central ingredients. LightGBM refined selected humidity predictions from the Camaro models, although its improvement was less than 0.0004. Physical prediction replacements supplemented the learned models, and the final blend scored 0.78792 on the private leaderboard.
compute: Kmat: 3 days on RTX 3090; second stage: all 91 models trained on CPU in less than 20 minutes.

solution_summary: The solution combined several retrieved context sources with diverse DeBERTa and Llama2 models. Retrieval used three embedding query paths, sentence-based open-book contexts, and article datasets containing 270k and 480k entries. The final system used eight DeBERTa checkpoints trained with sentence-based context, since better training contexts did not improve performance. LoRA-trained Llama2 added 0.003 to the ensemble.

solution_summary: The solution combined analytical transit modeling with conservative machine learning calibration of transit depths, spectral shapes, and uncertainties. Engineered features described time-series statistics, frequency content, orbital geometry, and atmospheric physics. Linear and Ridge regressions refined baseline predictions, while PCA limited spectral dimensionality and constrained blending reduced overfitting. Quality-weighted eight-fold validation and hold-out testing supported uncertainty calibration.

solution_title: 55th place solution – Shortformer + Sliding Window + Topic-dependent Postprocessing
solution_summary: The solution combined DeBERTaV3-Large, Funnel-Large, Longformer-Large, and RoBERTa-Large with weighted ensembling. Short-context models processed essay chunks with left and right context while predicting only their central regions, improving single-model scores by over 0.005 against normal stride. BERTopic supplied essay topics for topic-specific length and probability thresholds, which further improved results. A dedicated newline token preserved formatting information across tokenizers.

solution_summary: The solution combined RoBERTa-base span extractors with convolutional heads and two text preprocessing schemes. Training included label smoothing, lowercasing augmentation, and model-specific head fine-tuning or adversarial training. Rules reconstructed systematic label noise caused by differences between raw and whitespace-normalized text, improving the best single model by about 0.009 on both validation and the public leaderboard. The selected four-model ensemble combined character-level probabilities and achieved 0.730 on the private leaderboard.

solution_summary: The pipeline classified image acquisition sources before applying optional source-aware preprocessing. It then aligned the image, rectified the ECG grid, and extracted waveforms with Net3. Correcting camera geometry and grid alignment addressed the main error source, while source-specific preprocessing improved consistency on unfamiliar sources. Reported public and private scores were 18.44 and 18.33.

The author used MD5 hashes to identify duplicate images within and across the training and test sets. Removing duplicates reduced training images from 12 million to 7.5 million and test images from 3 million to 2 million, while shared images supplied test labels from training data. ResNet-50, ResNet-101, and ResNet-152 were trained on 160×160 crops with plateau-based learning-rate reductions and all but the last layer frozen during the first epoch. Test-time augmentation and geometric-mean aggregation achieved 0.75 on the leaderboard per model, and combining the models with another geometric mean increased the score to 0.77.

solution_title: 38th Place Solution - My learnings from AI4C
solution_summary: The author blended point-wise DeBERTa-V3-Small and GraphCodeBERT-base models with a pair-wise model receiving about 20% weight. Code-cell context, preservation of markdown endings, and prioritization of class and function names helped within a 768-token budget. Careful notebook selection retained roughly 70% of the data while reducing outdated and duplicate examples, followed by final training on validation data as well. A special rule used only point-wise predictions for trailing markdown cells, while alternative attention heads, Bi-LSTM, embedding-margin methods, and sparse-attention models were unsuccessful.
compute: Free Kaggle and Google Colab; intermittently rented A5000 24GB during the final couple of weeks.

solution_summary: The method selectively reinitialized model weights using gradient information from the retain and forget sets, then retrained on retained data. It collected forget gradients through cross-entropy ascent and retain gradients through descent, matching sample counts with random retain subsets. The best configuration reinitialized 30% of convolution weights and reduced the learning rate of untouched weights to one tenth of the base rate. Warmup followed by linear learning-rate decay and randomness in retain-subset selection improved performance.

Images were processed at their original resolution by extracting six strips, selecting the eight darkest 512×512 tiles, and splitting those into 32×32 training instances. Validation used a class-stratified 80:20 patient split, with class balancing by undersampling only the training set. The final approach combined CNN and LightGBM models and also created institution-specific models. Ensembling improved the private score from approximately 0.676 to 0.668, while grayscale and histogram equalization did not help.
The post contains only a link to a Kaggle notebook. It provides no description of the approach or results. No solution methods can be extracted from the supplied text.

solution_title: 9th Place Solution: GNNs Ensemble and MLP Stacking
solution_summary: The solution combined a shared-weight MLP stack of six modified DynEdge models with four GNNs specialized by pulse-count segments. DynEdge variants changed pooling, network size, normalization, sensor embeddings, and optimizers. Training first used von Mises-Fisher loss and then Euclidean distance loss on events with fewer pulses, followed by stochastic weight averaging. A 60/40 blend of the stacked and segmented branches achieved 0.975 public and 0.976 private.
compute: Published DynEmb submission example runs in 1 hour 20 minutes.

solution_summary: The model concatenated CNN features, RNN k-max features, and attention outputs. Training used Adam with a cyclical learning rate, a step size of 500, and a batch size of 1024. The author used five folds with three epochs per fold and referred to common preprocessing from competition discussions. No numerical performance result was reported.

The solution combined neural networks, ResNet, and TabNet with statistical features, PCA features, and RankGauss preprocessing. Label smoothing, transfer learning from non-scored targets for neural networks and ResNet, and shallow training configurations improved performance. A custom thresholding neural network transformed each input with an element-wise linear function and tanh before an MLP. The final ensemble used two-stage stacking with MLP, 1D CNN, and weight optimization, with TabNet and neural networks providing useful complementarity.

The solution expanded a mouse-behavior detection pipeline with cleaned tracking coordinates, physical-scale normalization, metadata, and extensive single-mouse and pairwise motion features. It incorporated third-mouse context and frame-rate-aware temporal features to represent interactions across multiple time scales. Per-action thresholds were optimized using grouped out-of-fold predictions, followed by probability smoothing, threshold masking, class selection, and segment smoothing. Consistent feature sanitization and column alignment were applied during both training and inference.

The solution linked runs across training and test data using Markus F's kernel. Training runs containing multiple surfaces were corrected manually. Known test surfaces were then combined with the author's best submission, which had a reported leaderboard score of 0.73.

The pipeline combined three pretrained 3D segmentation models through a learned ensemble and two successive refinement networks. Random mask thresholds and coarse dropout taught the refinement stages to repair broken sheets and holes. The largest improvement came from a diffeomorphic network that warped blurred masks and applied constrained topology corrections. Combining two implementations achieved 0.621 CV and 0.615 private score before the reported post-processing comparisons, where median filtering reached 0.624 private score.
compute: Approximately 400 training epochs; Primus convergence reduced from 700 or more epochs to 400 with pretraining.

solution_summary: The team used a single RetinaNet detector with a ResNet101 backbone, selecting the best model from five folds of stage 1 training data. Training used 800×800 images, extensive augmentation, dropout in both prediction heads, and nine anchor ratios. The most consequential changes were reducing training box dimensions by 15% to address annotation differences and expanding anchor ratios. A two-model ensemble tested after submission reached 0.254 on the stage 1 test set.

The selected submission averaged multiple seeds and five folds of LightGBM regression models. Extensive behavioral feature engineering produced about 20,000 features, reduced to 500 using null importance. Repeated user-grouped validation, supplemented by simulated truncated-history train/test splits, guided decisions using weighted RMSE. Optimized thresholds converted predictions to assessment classes, producing private QWK of 0.568; a LightGBM–CatBoost blend was rejected because it did not improve cross-validation.

The author trained separate RetinaNet detectors for five levels of the class hierarchy to reduce false negatives caused by incomplete parent and child annotations. ResNet152 and ResNet101 models used class-balanced sampling, stronger augmentation, and carefully selected negative images. Predictions from original and horizontally flipped images were combined with a custom weighted box-merging heuristic. The reported merged submissions scored approximately 0.474–0.475, while Soft NMS performed worse than the custom ensemble.

solution_summary: The final approach stacked 34 diverse tabular models using a Ridge meta-learner. Base models shared stratified five-fold validation and included boosted trees, neural networks, and tabular transformers, with extensive feature engineering and original Telco dataset mappings. Adding pairwise interactions between model predictions was the largest reported improvement, raising CV to 0.91984 and private performance to 0.91837. Isotonic calibration was also retained as a second final submission despite slightly worse public performance.

The final solution combined three networks through weighted logit averaging, which worked better than probability averaging. Two models adapted BBN with ResNeSt101 and EfficientNet-B3 backbones to address long-tailed classes. The third used SE-ResNeXt50 with hierarchical targets, weighted focal loss, dataset-specific normalization, and a decaying Adam learning rate. Random crops and flips helped, and four-view test-time augmentation averaged logits.

solution_summary: The solution converted men's AdjEM ratings and women's Massey power ratings into win probabilities using a normal distribution and an assumed 70 possessions. It used error scales of 9 for men and 12 for women, with home-field adjustment for women's games. The successful submission simulated only 50 brackets without manual overrides and scored 0.05563; larger simulations performed worse.

The solution combined XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM regressors and classifiers with a Random Forest. Its main component was an ensemble whose weights were optimized within each fold using a custom Averager class. Evaluation used 30 stratified folds, classification reports, and comparison plots. No feature engineering was used, and tracked cross-validation and leaderboard progress helped select the final submission.

The solution first trained sound event detection models on labeled positive regions, then used framewise predictions to create richer pseudo labels for subsequent classifiers. It combined SED and conventional classifiers with different backbones, augmentations, and crop sizes. Class probability multipliers and instance counts from class-specific segmentation models further improved predictions. The final ensemble achieved 0.969 public and 0.971 private leaderboard scores, despite unreliable local validation caused by incomplete labels.

The final submission used a five-fold RemBERT ensemble trained with MLQA, Hindi XQuAD, and Tamil-translated SQuAD data. Several multilingual question answering models were evaluated, with RemBERT achieving the strongest reported public score of 0.788. Averaging across different model families did not work well. An incomplete mT5-base text-to-text experiment predicted letters but omitted spaces, preventing a usable submission.

solution_title: 56th Place Solution for the AI Mathematical Olympiad - Progress Prize 1 Competition
solution_summary: The approach used DeepSeek-Math-7B-RL to generate 50 candidate solutions per question, with up to three rounds of generation and code execution. solution_title: After shock, Let's talk about solutions
solution_summary: The final submission blended gradient boosting, a neural network, and several linear models, achieving a private score of 0.307. The neural network and linear models showed substantial public-to-private performance drops. The team's best standalone boosting model was omitted from the blend despite achieving a private score of 0.31. Reviewing submissions identified several variable, geographic, and weather features that performed well on both splits.

solution_title: 32nd Place Solution — LLM/VLM teacher labels + image-only CoAtNet / ConvNeXt ensemble
solution_summary: The team built teacher labels from averaged report readers and direct image readings, replacing biased site-specific labels with image readings and preserving expert labels. This post describes prediction post-processing that improved the public score by about 0.05. The method discretized each selected target's predictions by replacing them with k-means centroids, exploiting tied ranks for discrete targets. Cluster counts were chosen using out-of-fold Spearman correlation, with smoothing and a minimum improvement threshold of 0.001. Fitting clusters jointly on out-of-fold and test predictions added about 0.02 publicly, although the spelling target suffered.

The solution reused public weights in a three-stage alignment, grid-rectification, and waveform-digitization pipeline without training new models. It ran three input branches using grayscale enhancement, the original image, and HSV enhancement, then combined their signals with a weighted average. Selected branches received Savitzky–Golay smoothing and Einthoven-law correction, while slightly different pixel-to-mV scales added diversity. Preserving an unmodified branch and varying refinement across branches improved robustness across scan types.

solution_summary: This writeup describes one teammate's five-model contribution to a larger solution. SVM and FTRL used basic event and advertisement features, while XGBoost and Extra Trees used mean target values, interactions, and document similarity. An FFM combined categorical inputs with XGBoost leaf features. A second-level XGBoost ranker combined predictions and features, with the other teammate's contribution needed for the complete team solution.

The solution ensembled three LightGBM rankers trained with different candidate-generation strategies. Item2vec article embeddings and averaged customer embeddings supported personalized candidate retrieval, similarity features, and clustering. Ranking features also included neural article representations, purchase histories, cluster behavior, and LightGBM sales forecasts. Candidate diversity drove ensemble gains, and final recommendations were combined using reciprocal-rank-style weights.

solution_title: [5th Solution] - Tri's part - Token classification approach and Pseudo labeling
solution_summary: The author processed all discourse texts in an essay together and predicted discourse labels at custom [FP2] marker tokens. solution_title: 42th solution: BPE + LSTM-Transformer-CNN + DistillRoberta + Superfast Unsupervised
solution_summary: The author blended four predictors: a public model with probability post-processing, an LSTM–Transformer–CNN model, DistillRoberta, and a public unsupervised baseline adapted using DistillRoberta predictions. The adapted baseline used high- and low-scoring examples as likely AI and student references, then searched the top 20 references from each group to calculate probabilities. The final weighted blend achieved public and private scores of 0.967 and 0.918.

solution_title: 5th Place Solution for the CAFA 5 Protein Function Prediction Challenge
solution_summary: StarFunc combines sequence homology, structure alignment, protein interactions, Pfam-based logistic regression, and SPROF-GO predictions. Three random forests, one per GO aspect, combine these predictions with GO background frequencies. Experimental annotations supply training labels, while eligible existing non-experimental annotations are added with evidence-dependent confidence. The reported private wFmax was 0.56171, and the sequence component alone achieved 98.7% of the combined performance on an independent test.

solution_summary: The author fine-tuned a Swin image encoder and two multilingual or Indonesian text encoders using ArcFace embeddings. Image training used RandAugment, Ranger, mixed precision, and gradient accumulation, while the text encoders used SAM with AdamW. Learning rates warmed up before cosine decay, with a higher rate for the image embedding layer. Inference combined image and text similarities using a sixth-power formula, capped matches at 42, and added a nearest neighbor when only one match was selected.
