solution_summary: The final blend combined three BERT models and one XLNet model, using a simple BERT baseline without text preprocessing or loss weights. The main improvement came from selecting about 475,000 training records containing valid identity annotations or positive toxicity labels. Selecting identity-annotated records outperformed random selection, while including all toxic comments helped address class imbalance. Two epochs on this subset achieved a reported leaderboard score of 0.94299, and XLNet improved the blend despite implementation bugs.
compute: Trained approximately 475,000 records for two epochs in a Kaggle Kernel; hardware and runtime unspecified.

solution_title: Solution and experience sharing - 4th place (should have been 2nd)
solution_summary: The solution combined 16 XGBoost variants spanning four modeling methods, two public-script feature sets, and two post-processing approaches. It mixed linear, Poisson, multiclass-derived continuous predictions, and an undisclosed heuristic method, with offsets or cutoffs used to map predictions to ordinal classes. Weighted ensembling delivered substantial gains, and the final blend also included a variant that post-processed predictions after aggregation. Five-fold validation and public leaderboard results sometimes disagreed, while a genetic programming model was excluded despite later showing complementary value.

The final solution combined 37 submission files, including 30 generated by the author and seven from public kernels. Diversity came from different combinations of face embeddings, VGGFace versus Facenet features, and fully connected layer configurations. The strongest individual model combined features from both extractors and scored 0.893 on the public leaderboard. Weighted combination performed slightly better than simple averaging, with model quality and low correlation driving the ensemble gains.

The pipeline retrieved candidate image pairs with DINOv2/Base and cheaply filtered them using ALIKED descriptor distances before expensive LightGlue matching. It pruned the match graph to reduce reconstruction cost and improve opportunities to reconstruct small clusters. NetworkX clustering preceded repeated pycolmap incremental reconstruction, followed by native COLMAP map merging and bundle adjustment. The reported public and private scores were 43.53 and 43.34.
compute: GPU used for descriptor-distance matrix computation; hardware and runtime unspecified

solution_title: 54th Place Solution: All I Need Is fastai, timm, and DINOv3
solution_summary: The solution fine-tuned DINOv3 Huge and Large vision transformers for image-based biomass regression and averaged 42 models across seeds, folds, and target configurations. Validation used three-fold StratifiedGroupKFold with species-based strata and Sampling_Date plus State groups. Auxiliary biomass, height, and NDVI targets supported representation learning, while final total biomass and GDM predictions were derived from three primary components. The ensemble achieved reported CV of 0.773948 and public score of 0.75, with a private score of 0.63. TTA, MixUp, CutMix, and several alternative models did not improve validation.
compute: Early validation: 2× T4, 15GB, 15 min/fold. Later Google Colab Pro training: A100 80GB, 45 min/fold for Huge; A100 40GB, 25 min/fold for Large; approximately $25.

solution_summary: The final approach trained convolutional networks with mixup and random frequency/time masking on curated data and two pseudo-labeled datasets. Pseudo-labels came from high-confidence windows selected using the ratio of top-k activations to total activations, with a second dataset assigning clip-level labels from selected windows. Training combined separate losses for curated data and both pseudo-label sets, and inference used the same window-scanning strategy. Test-targeted fine-tuning reached about 0.76 but was deliberately excluded from the final submission.

The solution used batch-separated cross-validation, with nine Citeseq folds and twelve Multiome folds, and found that local gains closely tracked leaderboard gains. PCA and truncated SVD supplied reduced representations, while shallow LightGBM models selected target-specific Citeseq features. Citeseq combined single-target and multi-target neural networks with LightGBM and CatBoost; Multiome used three multi-target neural networks and CatBoost. A simple blend restricted weights to 0, 1, 2, or 3 and achieved local scores of 0.9039 for Citeseq and 0.669 for Multiome.

solution_title: 24th (-2.633) - haha nice - pairs of pairs of ...
solution_summary: The solution modeled interactions between molecular connections using shared neural networks over connection types and Euclidean distances. Pointwise convolutions and summation produced features invariant to connection ordering, translation and orthogonal transformations. A second interaction stage captured pairs of aggregated pair features, improving the reported score from -2.126 to -2.473. The best submission blended predictions and scored -2.633, while a further interaction stage could not be trained sufficiently within the available time.

solution_summary: The post describes a lightweight field-aware factorization machine implementation based on libffm. Its stated focus is optimized out-of-core performance. The implementation contributed to the competition solution, while further details are deferred to an accompanying PDF.

The solution rasterized raw and simplified strokes into three-channel images encoding stroke order, motion, and timing information. ImageNet-pretrained InceptionResNetV2 was the strongest single model, achieving a local validation score of 0.9516 with 139×139 inputs from raw drawings. Training used Adam, followed by a stage with gradient accumulation and a loss combining 10% categorical cross-entropy with 90% top-three loss. The final ensemble combined InceptionResNetV2, Xception, and ResNet50 predictions using weights based on local validation scores and correlations between predicted classes.

The solution used a single EfficientNet-B0 with an FPN and an auxiliary four-class defect classifier sharing encoder features. Training proceeded through three stages, adding pseudo-labeled test images and Dice loss before incorporating validation data for final training. The final weights averaged five checkpoints, and training used 256×512 crops. Inference skipped decoding when the classification head predicted no defect, used a fixed 0.5 classification threshold, and applied TorchScript tracing without test-time augmentation.

solution_title: LB61th PB72th solution & Please tell me your opinion!
solution_summary: The solution combined CWT image classifiers and raw-signal 1D CNNs using weights derived from out-of-fold ridge coefficients. Larger image inputs and EfficientNet models performed well, while ViT and Swin improved ensemble diversity despite lower individual validation scores. Positive ensemble weights were preferable on the private leaderboard, with the ensemble reaching 0.8783. CQT, a convolutional transformer encoder, and autoencoder anomaly detection did not improve results.

solution_title: 4th place solution - LB probing, acronym detection, and NER
solution_summary: The solution combined rule-based acronym extraction, string matching against several dataset-name inventories, and NER-based detection of name variants. Leaderboard probing estimated hidden-test properties and guided submission selection by evaluating predictions with training-label matches removed. A spaCy NER model learned from training labels, extracted acronyms, and external government dataset names, then supplied variants filtered by Jaccard similarity. Adding training-name and acronym matches produced final public and private scores of 0.614 and 0.513.

solution_summary: The final TensorFlow 2.0 solution combined BERT joint large and base models through weighted averaging of their logits. Removing duplicate answer spans and suppressing YES/NO answers improved predictions, while validation selected separate long- and short-answer thresholds. A cross-window span selection method improved private performance but was omitted from the chosen submission because it did not improve the public score. Experiments ran on free Colab TPUs, while late PyTorch TPU experiments were not completed.

solution_title: [5th Place Solution in Efficiency Prize] 327th Place in Private LB
solution_summary: The solution adapted a public baseline with Byte-Pair Encoding and an ensemble of three ComplementNB variants, three SGDClassifier variants, and one LGBMClassifier. Training data came from the DAIGT V2 dataset, with ten sources selected according to leaderboard improvements and prompt restrictions applied to three sources. SGD models used class weights, while LightGBM's n_iter was reduced to 300 to shorten inference. The author also tried batching tokenizer input to accelerate processing, although its benefit was uncertain.

The team built its optimization loop largely from public code and submissions. It accelerated some code with AI assistance, randomized run arguments, and repeatedly merged results from short parallel runs. The solution improved the best solution in 11 boxes by about 0.0002 overall, although it added little beyond another strong public solution.

solution_summary: The author shares source code for their contribution to a team solution. The brief description credits teammates with next-click features using specific sorting and weights-of-evidence features. The author reports that their best single-model leaderboard score improved from 0.9815 to 0.9828 over ten days, but gives no detailed modeling or validation pipeline.

The solution combined two pipelines in which 2.5D Faster R-CNN detectors supplied region features to DeiT-Small transformers. Training on all anatomical planes addressed unreliable image-orientation metadata, while inference used the plane requiring the least interpolation. The detector variants used ResNet-50 with three slices and ConvNeXtV2-Tiny with five slices, followed by transformer aggregation into location and aneurysm-presence predictions. Weighted averaging achieved a private score of 0.80592, improving over either individual transformer pipeline.

solution_title: 5th Place Solution: Diversity and Bug - Both Are All You Need
solution_summary: The solution blends distilled HGNetV2 and EfficientNet CNNs with ProtoSSM and a distilled SED baseline. Training combines competition focal recordings and labeled soundscapes, with focal-only validation guiding model selection. Distillation provided the largest gains, followed by augmentation and architecture changes. Shifted-window inference, temporal smoothing, and file-level scaling improved predictions, while multiplicative frequency augmentation in the dB domain unexpectedly added more than 0.01 in partial testing.

The solution combined seven XGBoost binary classifiers, each predicting whether the ordinal response exceeded a different threshold, and summed their probabilities. Features included product dummy variables, medical keyword counts, and target-derived keyword summaries. Iterative boundary optimization maximized kappa, including separate boundaries for subsets defined by selected binary variables. Repeated and nested cross-validation guided calibration evaluation, and some solutions were combined using median predictions. The highest private score reported was 0.68002, although that submission was not selected for the final pair.

solution_title: [2nd place] My approach - LightGBM quantile regression
solution_summary: The author trained LightGBM models to predict each bandit's original threshold and selected actions greedily using decay-adjusted predictions. The strongest variant switched between the 60th percentile prediction before step 750 and the 65th percentile afterward, achieving a reported score of 1521.1. Training used 20,000–30,000 selected competition episodes, with features capturing rewards, decay-adjusted hit rates, opponent actions, recency, and relative ranks. Local evaluation used win rate and cumulative chosen-threshold differences, with the latter providing a more stable comparison than rewards. Reinforcement learning and quantile regression below the median were unsuccessful.

The solution repeatedly ran LKH from the best available arrangement, perturbing permutation assignments between three strings. It initialized from the standard permutation sequence, swapped selected one-cycles, removed redundant non-mandatory permutations, and introduced wildcards. Thousands of runs produced a score of 2431 before progress stalled. Adding wildcard support to LKH MinMax CTSP and running it overnight improved the score to 2430.

solution_summary: The team's best single model combined text representations, image quality features, aggregate features, and Ridge-derived features. Text inputs included SVD features, TF-IDF over descriptions and titles, and title counts. NIMA supplied image quality features, and the reported public leaderboard score was around 2210 as written in the post. solution_title: A solution that I hope will earn a silver medal (currently in 29th place)
solution_summary: The team extended the public Relicbound bot with five rule-based modifications. Ships intensified relic searches when scoring indicated undiscovered rewards, accumulated energy while harvesting, and used SAP attacks to disrupt opponents. A coordinated attack near the end of the game targeted opposing harvest areas. Board-change prediction improved routing, while score-based occupancy estimates enabled attacks on unseen opponents.

solution_title: 81st Place Solution for Bengali.Ai Speech Recognition.
solution_summary: The approach fine-tuned Wav2Vec2 using the normalized Bengali Common Voice 13 dataset. Training ran for 15 epochs with a learning rate of 1e-4. Optuna optimized decoding parameters, selecting alpha 0.3802723523729998, beta 0.053996879617918436, and a beam width of 1024. The reported public scores were 0.432 and 0.435, with both submissions scoring 0.518 on the private evaluation.

solution_title: Kaggle's The Hunt for Prohibited Content Competition
solution_summary: The solution used logistic regression in Vowpal Wabbit with text features, raw advertisement fields, and feature interactions. Combining ranked predictions from the full-data model and a model trained on proven blocked and unblocked advertisements improved performance. Log loss consistently outperformed the other tested losses, while combining models using different losses did not help. The implementation included grid search, sample weighting, and bootstrap bagging, and achieved a score of 0.98527.

solution_title: AdaBoost, SSD: object detection for lions counting
solution_summary: The approach progressed from AdaBoost detectors to a VGG-based Single Shot Multibox Detector, ultimately using large image tiles. Square training boxes were constructed around annotated dots, and resizing plus tiling improved pup detection. Attempts to combine multiscale features, learn image scale, and add a counting regression objective were unsuccessful. Stacking provided a further improvement of about 1.5 leaderboard points.

solution_summary: The solution used a U-Net with an EfficientB3 encoder, trained on resized overlapping TIFF tiles and additional hand-labeled data. Five folds were balanced by example count, and global Dice was used to evaluate models. Cross-entropy training followed by Lovasz softmax fine-tuning and Adam with SAM improved performance and stability. Center-crop stitching was the largest reported inference improvement, while model ensembles did not improve results and submissions mostly used a single model.

solution_title: [Updated] Solution sharing: Private LB 0.695 in 12 mins

solution_title: My Strategy & The Dangers of Public Notebooks
solution_summary: The author developed a leaderboard-tuned last-value forecast as a hedge and a main autoregressive tree-model ensemble. The main pipeline combined custom preprocessing with a public baseline's preprocessing and incorporated the discrete nature of microbusiness density. It forecast every test period recursively using XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM, after removing a meta-model. GRUs, linear regression, and ARMA were unsuccessful, and the author also removed submission code that incorrectly scaled private-period predictions.

solution_title: 13th place solution - How I survived the shakeup
solution_summary: The solution combined Swin, ViT, ResNeXt, and EfficientNet models using ridge regression trained on out-of-fold predictions. Training decisions prioritized stable cross-validation under a 10-fold split stratified by 20 target bins, with fixed short training runs instead of early stopping. Binary cross-entropy worked best overall, while a Swin model trained with binned multiclass cross-entropy was the strongest individual model. Horizontal-flip inference and architectural diversity helped the ensemble reach a CV score of 17.134049.

solution_title: My Part of Team's Solution (Punch Cards Are All You Need, LB Rank 24)
solution_summary: The author trained bi-encoders to predict markdown-code adjacency from cosine similarity, using multiple-negatives ranking loss and hard negatives from the same notebook. Synthetic beginning and ending code cells improved handling of introductory and summary markdown cells. The final team solution combined CodeBERT and GraphCodeBERT bi-encoders with a pointwise DeBERTa-v3-base model. Ensembling fractional predictions with optimized weights and confidence-dependent adjustments achieved 0.8824, while length-sorted batching kept inference efficient.
compute: Single model trained for 3 epochs in 17 hours on an A6000; inference took 1 hour 20 minutes.

solution_summary: The solution combined three prompt attacks designed to produce different scoring patterns across the hidden judges. Gemma chat-template injection, identity-conditioned instructions, and a modified essay-counting prompt produced complementary disagreements. The author submitted six variants of each attack and optimized the submission seed and final essay indices using public leaderboard feedback. The final submission scored 29.829 on the private leaderboard, with imperfect reliability of the third attack limiting performance.
compute: Approximately three weeks spent developing the third attack.

solution_title: [Working Note] When a Guardrail Erases Its Own Benchmark
solution_summary: The team audited the public guardrail and scorer to determine which failure predicates could actually receive credit. This reduced public optimization to maximizing sentinel-bearing posts within the replay budget, using lower generation overhead and a template-state multi-post construction. Repeated evaluations revealed substantial score noise, so small single-run gains were treated cautiously. Public exfiltration finalists scored zero privately, while a retained clean confused-deputy hedge transferred exactly at 11.915.
compute: Hosted evaluator; inference engine settings were fixed. Minimal reachability proof was CPU-only.

solution_title: Solution Write up For CommonLit - Evaluate Student Summaries
solution_summary: The author fine-tuned separate DeBERTa backbones for student summaries and prompts, with two additional heads predicting wording and content scores. These predictions were fed into a LightGBM ensemble alongside n-gram features. DeBERTa used random holdout validation, while LightGBM used K-fold cross-validation. The author proposed larger backbones and prompt-separated validation as future improvements.

The author improved an MLP by adding LayerNorm to gene and cell features, normalizing them row-wise. This reduced the private score from 0.01625 to 0.01616 and the public score from 0.01834 to 0.01824. Adding row-wise normalized features to TabNet also helped, although the reported public improvement was smaller.

solution_title: 203 Place Solution for the Detect Sleep States Competition
solution_summary: The submitted approach used a neural network followed by peak-based postprocessing to detect sleep events. The author credited public notebooks and code by tubotubo. Boosting models, TSFresh, and blending with public kernels were reported as unsuccessful, with no numerical results provided.

The approach trained U-Net and LinkNet segmentation models with EfficientNet-B3 backbones on downscaled, overlapping image crops. Base training combined Dice and binary cross-entropy losses with Lookahead and cosine warm restarts, followed by lower-rate Adam fine-tuning using test-set pseudo-labels. Individual models achieved a private score of 0.945, while the submitted merged version scored 0.943. Offline analysis showed that pseudo-labeling increased Dice scores but also false detections, and merging amplified shared prediction errors.

This component searches for input crops whose properties match those observed in the training outputs. It compares attributes such as color counts and symmetry, repeatedly sampling crops until a match is found. The published implementation solves four public tasks, while additional properties and some luck allowed it to solve six.

The solution combined SE-ResNeXt101, PNASNet5Large, and SENet154 with test-time augmentation, achieving a leaderboard score of 0.650. Five-fold iterative stratification supported validation, while cosine warm restarts enabled convergence in about 15 epochs. Scheduled mixup and increased dropout improved individual models. Inference thresholds were adjusted to match the validation-derived average of 5.2 labels per image.
compute: 15 epochs with 3 restarts to converge; GPU model unspecified.

solution_summary: The team combined simulated annealing, a genetic algorithm, and iterated local search with controlled kicks to optimize word orderings. Rapid annealing, cutoff restarts, and fixing the first word helped escape persistent local optima. Genetic crossover reused diverse local solutions, while threshold-based local search and score-history exclusion further expanded exploration. The genetic algorithm improved id 3 from about 195.0 to 191.7 and id 5 from 28.8 to 28.5.
compute: Approximately 30 minutes per simulated annealing trial; GPU resources used, hardware unspecified.

solution_title: 1st place - A lot of features, a lot of models, and a little bit of luck
solution_summary: The solution centered on extensive feature engineering, especially numerical digit interactions and target/count encodings. Encodings also used the original dataset and auxiliary targets such as employment status and debt-to-income ratio. A diverse ensemble contained 100 models, with XGBoost providing the strongest individual result at approximately 0.92818 CV and 0.92923 private score. Ridge and HC were the strongest ensemble methods, while nonlinear stacking performed substantially worse.

The solution decomposed sales into day-of-week, country GDP, store, product, and day-of-year effects before forecasting the remaining curve. A constant forecast trajectory performed much better than continuing the upward trend. Holiday adjustments substantially improved leaderboard scores and were estimated from median normalized values from the previous year. These adjustments accounted for delayed effects, moving holidays, and three Kenyan holidays absent from the holiday package.

The post presents a BERT fine-tuning baseline for detecting insincere Quora questions and points to related project code and execution scripts. Its reported validation F1 is 0.63 for the positive class and 0.81 macro averaged. A tensor2tensor comparison performs worse, with positive-class F1 of 0.21 and macro F1 of 0.58. The post supplies limited pipeline details beyond the baseline and validation results.

The solution reconstructed ordered column and row groups to recover leaked targets and build grouped features. Recovered test targets augmented training for gradient boosting models, with the strongest submissions using 97 and 110 column groups. Features combined raw columns, group statistics, and sums of important groups, followed by importance-based selection and four-fold tuning. The final prediction was a weighted sum of 23 LightGBM and XGBoost models, with weights adjusted using out-of-fold and leak predictions.

solution_title: 39th solution-Attention Gated Resnet18 ( single model without cv)
solution_summary: The solution used Attention Gated Networks with ResNet18 backbones, combining attended features from the final three blocks. Three crop-size models were ensembled using full-resolution predictions and a fixed threshold of 0.2. Training used competition PNGs and external HPA RGBY images, SGD with momentum, and a combined soft F1 and focal loss. The reported score pairs were 0.604/0.540 for the size ensemble and 0.601/0.547 with oversampling; cross-validation was not used.

The authors initialized football policies by cloning strong submissions, then improved them with a custom IMPALA actor-critic system. KL penalties preserved useful initial behavior and stabilized successive rounds of reinforcement learning. A deeper convolutional network combined player relationships, game state, and action-history features, with additional information available only to the critic. Training mixed self-play with a diverse fixed opponent pool, while a separate internal evaluation pool reduced the noise of leaderboard comparisons. Simple goal-based rewards worked better than elaborate mode-specific rewards, and their strongest individual agent outperformed attempted combinations.
compute: Each experiment ran in one Docker container with actor and learner in separate threads; inference took 0.01–0.15 seconds per action.

solution_title: 102nd Place Solution - Clustering And Refinement with Reconstruction Loss To Beat Public Codes
solution_summary: The solution refines initial velocity maps from models or public prediction CSVs using clustering and a physics-based loss. Replacing cluster velocities with their medians improved MAE from 25.6 to 25.4, with replacement skipped for maps exhibiting many clusters. FlatVel samples were identified through shot symmetry and constrained to share velocities across each depth before physics refinement. Compute and memory limits restricted final refinement to two steps per test sample, while training or fine-tuning alternative neural models did not beat the public baselines.
compute: Physics refinement required shot splitting and gradient accumulation; final processing used two steps per test sample. A 40-step example took a few minutes. TPU v4 use is also mentioned.

solution_title: Our Approach - Similarity-Based Sampling Bad Teaching (12th on public leaderboard)
solution_summary: The solution performs machine unlearning through a student trained against a good teacher and a bad teacher. The student starts from the original model, while the bad teacher receives limited pretraining on retained data. Similarity-based sampling and weighting emphasize retained examples near forgotten examples, and batch ordering emphasizes forgetting before reconstruction. The authors report strong local and public results, but their submission did not reach final evaluation, possibly because of a timeout.

The final submission used CatBoost with geometry features derived from pairwise atomic distances. Percentiles and counts for atom pairs, improved by duplicating atoms across periodic boundaries, were the main contribution and produced a score below 0.062. LSTM representations added to CatBoost gave inconsistent improvements and were excluded from the final submission. Standalone LSTM and CNN models performed worse, while a small number of high-error samples dominated validation loss.

solution_title: My simple trick for this competition
solution_summary: The post describes combining a binary outlier predictor with a regression model for non-outliers. The final prediction interpolates between the fixed outlier value of -33.21928 and the non-outlier regression output using the binary prediction. This improved local cross-validation by 0.015 compared with direct training on the same features. The reported classifier AUC was 0.914, and the non-outlier regression CV score was 1.545.

The author trained paired models with half-point targets rounded upward and downward, then averaged their predictions to reflect the original integer rubric. The final submission used an OOF-informed weighted ensemble of DeBERTa variants, several other transformers, and an embedding-based SVR. Adversarial training, layer-wise learning rates, weight initialization, pretrained weight decay, and a maximum text length of 768 were reported as helpful. Despite agreement between cross-validation and the public leaderboard, the submission suffered a substantial private-leaderboard decline.
compute: Training used Kaggle notebooks and the free Colab plan; hardware and training duration were not specified.

solution_title: 303rd / Bronze: Sub-voxel localization + a learned coordinate head
solution_summary: The solution refined detections from a public temporal-UNet3D and ILP pipeline using local soft-argmax, with z refinement providing most of the initial gain. Its stronger variant used a public learned coordinate head for y/x and supplied refined z coordinates to the edge model. Motion-relinker tuning and protected raw-ILP overrides raised the public score to 0.955, while a separate soft-argmax variant scored 0.954. Both variants were selected to hedge coordinate-transfer risk, and development replay was interpreted cautiously because the detector and edge model had seen its movies.

solution_summary: The solution ensembled ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNetB3 U-Nets trained at two patch scales with five folds grouped by whole-slide image. Excluding uninformative regions and using strong augmentation helped maintain agreement between local validation and the public leaderboard. Inference combined flip augmentation, overlapping tiles, and simple averaging across folds and models. Pseudo-labels and the supplied d48 hand labels brought little private-score benefit, while choosing a threshold for public performance proved costly. The reported scores were 0.9429 local CV, 0.927 public, and 0.947 private.

solution_summary: The author's contribution used a 2.5D U-Net with an EfficientNet B7 backbone, taking slices n−2, n, and n+2 as three input channels. Images were resized to 640 pixels and cropped to 384×384 during training, with around 100 epochs and AdamW optimization. Lighter augmentation improved the public score from 0.882 to 0.884 and the private score from 0.870 to 0.872. The team used both case-grouped and case-stratified folds to address test cases shared with training, although the author felt they overemphasized those shared cases.

solution_title: just a short tutorial to get 25th place
solution_summary: The author removed classes associated with attributes and followed a linked Torchvision tutorial. Input images had a minimum edge length of 800 pixels. The reported public and private scores were 0.22209 and 0.20699, respectively, with no further training or modeling details provided.

The solution fine-tuned Gemma-2-9B-IT for three-class preference classification using LoRA in BF16. A first model trained on official and deduplicated supplementary data generated pseudo-labels for 30,000 UltraFeedback samples, after which a fresh model was trained on the combined data. Custom truncation preserved portions of the prompt and both responses, while inference used longer sequences and response-order swapping. Rule-based probability overrides handled empty or identical responses.

solution_summary: The author combined EfficientNet image features with metadata and a spatial attention head, using noisy-student weights in the illustrated B3 model. External 2018 data and malignant upsampling were retained, while the 2019 portion was excluded after experiments. Sprinkle augmentation reduced overfitting but slowed learning, prompting the addition of attention. The final ensemble averaged strong CV models selected for lower prediction correlations across image sizes, EfficientNet variants, and data ratios.

solution_summary: The solution uses R scripts to load data, extract features, merge datasets, and fit XGBoost models for click prediction. Feature extraction includes phone, search, and visit datasets. A reduced-data run is recommended to verify expected results before running the full submission pipeline. The full pipeline has substantial memory requirements attributed to the implementation and R's memory handling.

solution_summary: The solution combined LightGBM, MLP, and 1D CNN models with target-specific ensemble weights. Eight prediction periods used different gaps between prediction dates and historical target features to respect test-time availability. Roughly 440 features captured player engagement history, recent baseball activity, and aggregated event-model predictions. Time-based validation across several months guided feature selection, while shared streaming feature generation kept training and inference consistent.

The team combined sensor-based tree models with neural models using video from both camera views and tracking features. Their video pipeline used 2.5D convolutions, residual 3D blocks and GeM pooling, while separate tree models handled player-to-player and player-to-ground contact. A second stage used four LightGBM models with temporal shifts of predictions and sensor data, followed by averaging and temporal smoothing. The combined CNN/GBDT component achieved 0.778 cross-validation and 0.773 private scores.

solution_summary: The solution ensembled eight landmark embedding models, combining DOLG architectures with EfficientNet–Swin hybrids and retrained models from earlier solutions. Training progressed from clean data at low resolution to a larger noisy dataset at higher resolutions. Dynamic-margin sub-ArcFace heads and a staged freezing procedure supported effective embedding training. Recognition postprocessing reused the previous year’s method, primarily to identify non-landmark images, and validation used the labeled 2019 test set.

solution_summary: The team combined more than 120 base models through two layers of stacking. Their strongest individual network used a two-level bidirectional GRU, max pooling, skip connections, and concatenated 900-dimensional GloVe and FastText embeddings. Neural networks, Extra Trees, and LightGBM formed first-level meta-models using predictions, uppercase counts, and rank-transformed inputs. A final weighted average of ranked meta-model outputs reached 0.9881, while a third stacking layer added no value.

The solution combined optimized regular tree tilings, a modified Sparrow packer, and a C++ billiard refinement algorithm. Treating a fixed block of trees as one object helped Sparrow handle larger configurations, while billiard typically reduced its resulting side length by about 0.2%. The team generated more diverse starting configurations by splicing and symmetrizing existing solutions. Population-based refinement and collision repairs during expansion further improved the search.

The final submissions combined EfficientNet B4 and ViT models or used only ViT models. EfficientNet used 2020 data, while transformer experiments also included selected classes from the 2019 dataset. Heavy image augmentation, label smoothing of 0.3, AdamP, and cosine warm restarts supported training. A blend weighted 0.4 toward EfficientNet and 0.6 toward ViT scored 0.9011 privately; a variant using a ViT trained only on 2020 data reached 0.9017.

solution_summary: The team combined diverse image models, primarily Swin Transformers, with weighted ensembling and a ridge ensemble for one group of models. Some networks also incorporated the provided binary attributes and image dimensions. Image hashes linked overlapping images to metadata from the previous PetFinder competition, which fed a second-stage GBDT alongside neural predictions. Training this second stage on the entire current dataset appeared helpful, although metadata feature experiments frequently overfit and worsened leaderboard scores.

The final approach lightly modified the public ARChitects2024 solution, which other experiments did not surpass. Each task received 24 epochs of test-time training with a batch size of four and two gradient accumulation steps. Training examples, inference examples, and DFS branching were reduced to save time, and two subprocesses accelerated inference. Two submissions were selected for consistent behavior, although some tasks still exceeded the 12-hour limit.

solution_summary: The pipeline first localized disc levels and spinal canals with CenterNet detectors, then classified severity from cropped sagittal and axial slices. Separate center and side classifiers combined 2D slice encoders with attention, sharing learning across disc levels and normalizing left and right inputs. Annotation correction, auxiliary losses, severe-class weighting, and diverse models supported accuracy. Averaging 30 models improved CV from a best single-model score of 0.3858 to 0.3643, followed by temperature scaling for spinal canal predictions.

The solution retrieves candidate items using multiple strategies and ranks them with interaction features and gradient-boosted classifiers. Recent popularity, repurchases, collaborative filtering, and embedding similarity drive retrieval and feature construction. A six-week training window and last-week validation showed stable validation-to-leaderboard correlation, while weekly negative downsampling controlled dataset size. The final ensemble of five LightGBM and seven CatBoost classifiers achieved a reported leaderboard score of 0.0371.

solution_title: Circular way to think about solution
solution_summary: The author proposes building a closed route by expanding a small circular linked list. Each iteration considers adjacent route nodes and inserts an unvisited neighbor at the position with the lowest incremental cost. The insertion objective adds two edge costs and subtracts the replaced edge cost. The implementation became progressively slower despite caching, and no competitive score is reported.

The solution paired EfficientNet-B7 study classification with a Faster R-CNN detector using an EfficientNet-B7 FPN backbone. Classification pretraining combined multiple chest X-ray datasets through shared-backbone, multi-head learning, while detection pretraining used RSNA pneumonia data. Five-fold ensembles, horizontal-flip TTA, sharpness-aware minimization, and attention-based detector features supported the final approach. Fixed feature attention improved image-level CV mAP from 0.563 to 0.567, and the combined system with both forms of TTA reached 0.628 on the private leaderboard.

solution_title: 173rd Place Solution: From 0.880 Baseline to 0.957 SOTA
solution_summary: The author developed a 3D cell detection and tracking pipeline through 66 controlled iterations, combining U-Net detection, spatial augmentation, graph optimization, and biological motion constraints. Error decomposition identified missed detections as a much larger bottleneck than association errors, motivating peak-preserving fusion of two detection seeds. Division maturity, sister symmetry and divergence, bidirectional edge support, and clearance-gated relinking improved tracking, reaching a public score of 0.957 from roughly 0.880. Sparse local division labels led to unreliable validation, and the author attributed weaker private generalization to sensitivity in detection and division thresholds.

solution_title: 2nd Place Solution for the Regression with an Abalone Dataset Competition
solution_summary: The author applied an existing AutoML workflow with little competition-specific adjustment. Dataset-origin classification and statistical tests supported adding the original data to training. Customized OpenFE generated about 200 features, followed by automated pruning, which the author considered the most influential component. Customized AutoGluon selected models and built a five-layer stack, although three layers achieved the same submission score.

solution_summary: The final CPU pipeline combined a Perch-based anchor with a complementary five-fold SED ensemble using EfficientNet-B0-family, EfficientNetV2-S, and NFNet-L0 models. Diversity came from backbone choice, mel resolution, pseudo-label training, and combining clip-level and framewise evidence. Rank blending handled calibration differences, followed by a small auxiliary branch, weak taxonomy smoothing, and selective high-confidence SED rescue. The submission scored 0.95036 publicly and 0.94352 privately; custom XC pretraining and embedding distillation did not become main final branches.

solution_title: 66th Place Solution for the Bengali.AI Speech Recognition Competition
solution_summary: The team fine-tuned ai4bharat/indicwav2vec_v1_bengali for three epochs and applied a language model afterward. Training mixed SLR53, SLR37, Common Voice 13, and selected fractions of the competition training and validation splits to preserve speech diversity for out-of-distribution samples. Their validation scores correlated poorly with leaderboard scores despite excluding Common Voice samples from validation. Other pretrained models and volume or noise augmentation performed worse, and punctuation handling was omitted because of limited time.

The solution combined LightGBM with an encoder-decoder Transformer for answer correctness prediction. LightGBM used historical user, question, tag, timing, and TrueSkill features constructed without future information. The Transformer encoded exercise information and decoded prior responses and lecture history with a sequence window of 100. Chronological holdouts were used for validation. A three-model ensemble added a LightGBM variant without TrueSkill features and used conditional maximum/minimum predictions plus weighted blending, achieving approximately 0.793 AUC.
compute: Kaggle environment, then Google Colab with GPU and 25GB RAM; LightGBM training around 15 hours, Transformer over 10 hours per epoch.

solution_summary: The author described a nearly single-model recommendation pipeline using action-specific covisitation candidates, extensive association features, and a LightGBM ranker. Candidate weighting incorporated item frequency, event separation, direction, and recency, with Optuna tuning the retrieval combination. One ranker jointly learned clicks, carts, and orders using different relevance gains, 5% negative sampling, and roughly 400 features from two weeks of data. The described model scored 0.604 publicly and 0.603 privately, nearly matching the ensemble, with Treelite accelerating inference.

The team combined complementary pipelines for IMU-only and full-sensor sequences, including temporal models and pretrained image classifiers applied to resized sensor matrices. Shared improvements included handedness normalization, corrections for incorrectly worn devices, quaternion handling, and strong sensor-specific augmentation. Auxiliary tasks and diverse architectures strengthened the ensemble. An online Hungarian assignment limiting each subject to two predictions per gesture-orientation pair raised private performance from 0.864 to 0.878, although results depended on sequence arrival order.

The solution used a U-Net with ASPP and a ResNeXt50 backbone on 1024×1024 tiles resized to 480×480. ASPP dilation settings were matched to the backbone's 15×15 feature map, while mixed precision enabled batches of at least 32 on a P100 GPU. Training used five folds, geometric and color augmentation, and holdout-based epoch tuning. Inference used overlapping tiles and discarded edge predictions to reduce boundary artifacts.
compute: P100 GPU; mixed-precision training with batch size at least 32.

solution_title: 7th Place Solution: Transfer Was the Real Attack
solution_summary: The author used timing probes to infer which attack families survived hidden guardrail replay, then prioritized short, direct Email actions. Unique recipients created distinct scoring opportunities, while the scorer's final-message authorization check enabled confused-deputy scoring. The selected Email submission scored 34.630 public and 34.510 private; a Mapping hedge scored 105.300 public but zero private. The decisive insight was to measure hidden-route survival before optimizing public score or throughput.
compute: Submissions often took 10–14 hours; replay appeared CPU-bound.

solution_title: 34th Place Solo: 213 Hours of Autonomous Multi-Model NeuroGolf
solution_summary: The author built a persistent multi-provider agent system that generated compact ONNX programs and admitted only verified improvements to a protected per-task bank. Local correctness, generated-case, crash, and runtime checks supported pooled submissions with regression attribution and rollback. Starting from a public baseline, the deadline artifact gained 415.08 points and scored 7655.34 on both leaderboards. A separate post-deadline mechanism-transfer system explored historical pooling semantics and float32 behavior, reaching a runtime-safe score of 7672.16 with nine perfect tasks.
compute: 213.5 hours elapsed campaign time; incremental model spend remained within existing monthly subscriptions.

solution_summary: The final ensemble combined six models selected from a pool of 30, including Dynamic Graph Networks and LSTMs of varying sizes. Nonlinear optimization chose the combination and linear weights to minimize mean angular error on a held-out batch. Models used randomly selected pulse subsets, with training and inference pulse counts sometimes differing, and predictions were averaged across four evaluations where needed. Test batches were cached across models, and training minimized the norm of the difference between the predicted vector and the true unit direction.

The pipeline applied Otsu thresholding and saved 512×512 image patches for a pretrained ViT-small encoder with TransMIL aggregation. Joint encoder and MIL training on 100 randomly selected patches performed better publicly than training MIL on fixed features. Differential learning rates and separate exponential moving averages supported training. Helpful experiments included larger-image pseudo-labeling and an Other-class rejection rule, while stain augmentation and an external ovarian dataset did not improve results.

The solution combines image model outputs with engineered tabular features in an ensemble of LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost models. Diversity comes from feature subsets, varying image meta-features, multiple image training setups, and seed averaging. Image training includes auxiliary tabular and diagnostic-cluster targets, multimodal self-supervised pretraining, mixup, and undersampling. Five-fold patient-grouped stratification guides selection, while older competition data is excluded after experiments reveal strong distribution differences.

The author framed ARC as predicting missing intermediate grids, called semi-tokens, between observed grids. A CNN encoded sliding-window pairs of grids, and the resulting embeddings were summed and normalized to represent a transformation trajectory. An FFN decoder with a Gumbel softmax output was intended to predict an intermediate grid. The model failed to predict these intermediate states accurately even on a sample from the training set, with ineffective accumulated embeddings and possible training-code issues.

solution_title: LightGBM with Season-Based Validation for March Madness
solution_summary: The solution combined men's and women's competition data to train a lightweight LightGBM matchup classifier. Nine features represented seeds, regular-season win ratios, scoring margins, and pairwise differences, with reversed matchups providing balanced labels. Season-based walk-forward validation and fold-local preprocessing reduced temporal leakage. Final probabilities were averaged across the season-validation models, with no numerical performance reported.

The final agent used behavioral cloning on curated winning replays from multiple leaderboard teams. A 7.2M-parameter entity transformer shared its trunk across two-player and four-player modes, while teacher-ID conditioning separated conflicting teacher policies. Planet features encoded board state and precomputed physics, leaving the network to predict firing, targets, and ship amounts. Local match validation selected mode-specific weights and firing thresholds; reinforcement learning attempts failed because rollout throughput and evaluation noise prevented useful iteration.
compute: Single G4 GPU × 13 hours; local validation mainly on PC CPU.

solution_summary: The author's solution combined neural network and XGBoost models through blending. The repository includes feature-building code, automatic tuning notebooks, and exploration of a magic feature. Final test predictions and out-of-fold training predictions are provided, although this brief post gives few implementation details.

solution_title: My Approach - non-parametric probability estimate + copy
solution_summary: The agent estimated bandit reward probabilities nonparametrically from replay data. It grouped observations by its own pulls, opponent pulls, and observed rewards, then averaged estimates across replays for stability. Handwritten copying rules used early-game behavior, estimated probability relative to the median, and repeated opponent pulls, with limits to prevent endless mutual copying. Additional opponent-action grouping dimensions did not materially improve performance.

The team identifies memory access and memory-based reconstruction as major contributors to its result. It also analyzed evaluation errors using score discrepancies to narrow down the responsible tasks. A binary-search-style procedure handled discrepancies of 200, 100, and 50 points, followed by exhaustive search with Claude below 50 points. The post provides an outline while deferring the full technical explanation.

The author describes an ensemble of deep neural networks and gradient boosting models used in competition submissions. The text identifies the approach as an Otto ensemble despite the supplied competition metadata. It provides no feature, training, validation, or performance details.

solution_title: Source code of the prize winners
solution_summary: The solution constructed two valid paths with nearest-neighbor initialization and improved them through segment relocation, edge reconnection, endpoint moves, and joint optimization of both paths. Simulated annealing helped the search, while an edge-swapping equalization procedure kept path lengths similar and opened opportunities for further improvements. Quadrant-based neighbor lists guided candidate selection, and repeated runs with different parameters continued from the best saved solution. The supplied configuration achieved a score around 6,580,000 in three hours, with further gains from longer and repeated runs.

solution_title: [429th Solution] Google - American Sign Language Fingerspelling Recognition - own, native)
solution_summary: The author explored Keras sequence models built from public ASL preprocessing and transformer pipelines. An encoder-decoder transformer with recurrent or convolutional additions exceeded 0.9 CV, but TensorFlow Lite conversion failed. Later experiments explored custom LSTM and convolutional layers, alternating upsampling and pooling, and averaging instead of addition. The solution concatenated correspondences from LoFTR, SuperGlue, DKM, and ASLFeat before robust geometric estimation. Calibrating image dimensions to multiples of eight and keeping all models' keypoints on the same scale were essential to effective ensembling. Carefully balancing keypoint counts improved accuracy and speed, while lowering LoFTR's border removal setting added another gain. The final ensemble scored 0.820 publicly and 0.827 privately.

The supplied code defines a GAN pipeline for generating 64-by-64 dog images from 128-dimensional latent vectors. Training images are cropped using annotated bounding boxes and augmented with random resized crops and horizontal flips. The generator combines adaptive instance normalization, learned Gaussian noise injection, pixel normalization, and spectrally normalized layers. The discriminator uses spectral normalization and batch normalization, and the configuration selects hinge loss. The excerpt ends during the loss implementation, so it provides no completed training run or measured results.

solution_title: Share my pipeline and part of post processing tricks from our team
solution_summary: The author built a flexible Keras/TensorFlow pipeline around Hugging Face transformers, sharing weights between title–question and title–answer inputs. Their trained models were not included in the team's final ensemble, but the pipeline supported experimentation and post-processing development. A customized OptimalRounder post-processing method was adopted by the team and improved teammates' leaderboard scores by approximately 0.02.

The post provides execution instructions for an Avito duplicate-ad detection pipeline. It requires data files in a data directory and an avito-cache directory for cached intermediate results. A notebook is converted into a Python script and then executed in test mode; model details and results are not described.

The post links to a notebook and gives a brief ingredient feature-processing idea. It suggests merging some ingredient names, using fish sauce and soy sauce as examples. No model, validation procedure, or detailed results are described in the post itself.

The author shared a strong submission that the team did not select as its final entry. Training used adversarial weight perturbation, pseudo-labels, and the last eight hidden layers. Maximum sequence length decreased over four epochs from 768 to 512, 512, and 470. Averaging two seeds achieved a cross-validation score of 0.4459.

The system classifies each image independently and uses data augmentation because the training set is small. The author reports that side views make driver face detection difficult and that Haar cascades fail. Experiments with upper-body pose estimation and scene or driver segmentation did not produce good results. Most system details appear in a diagram whose contents are not available in the supplied text.

The solution combined LightGBM, CatBoost, and XGBoost through a VotingClassifier using tabular features and CNN image predictions as pseudo-label features. Four EfficientNet models supplied these predictions, with the larger variants trained on additional ISIC 2019 and 2020 images to expand the training set and reduce class imbalance. Training pseudo-labels were generated only for each fold's validation samples to prevent leakage. Half-precision inference across two GPUs helped meet the 12-hour runtime limit, and the reported scores were approximately 0.1814 in cross-validation and 0.184 on the public leaderboard.
compute: Two GPUs for half-precision CNN inference, targeting less than 12 hours.

solution_title: 13th Place Solution: Task-Domain Adaptation, Prompting and Focal Loss
solution_summary: The solution progressively adapted Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B from broad binary preference modeling to domain-specific preferences and finally ternary competition labels. External preference datasets, multi-sample dropout, and carefully formatted conversation prompts improved performance. Two models trained and evaluated in opposite response orders were combined with weighted averaging to mitigate positional bias. Validation-based temperature scaling and several probability corrections refined the final predictions.
compute: Primarily one A100, occasionally one H100; some larger pretraining runs used 8 H100 GPUs. Inference split across two GPUs.
external_data: ["RLHFlow standard-format preference datasets", "Nectar, lmsys-chat-1m subset", "LMSYS 33k dataset", "toxic-dpo-v0.2", "HelpSteer2"]

solution_title: Why the magic works- is each raw variable actually a mix of two?
solution_summary: The team replaced feature values occurring only once with NaN and reported a leaderboard score of 0.917. The author also describes another post's complementary set of 200 features that masks values occurring at least twice, reportedly reaching 0.922, but says the team missed this approach. These observations motivated a hypothesis that each original variable mixes two underlying distributions. The post discusses this feature transformation rather than presenting a complete modeling pipeline.

solution_title: 11th Place Solution - Standing on the Shoulders of Supergiants
solution_summary: The agent used imitation learning from two strong players, followed by self-play PPO anchored to the imitation policy. A transformer represented planets as tokens, with engineered fleet, economic, geometric, and board-level features. Prioritized opponent sampling, stable PPO settings, and scaling to a roughly 15M-parameter model were central to improvement. The final agent used the same two-player RL weights in both game modes, with policy-only inference and startup compilation warm-up. Rust environment acceleration substantially increased training throughput.
compute: Self-play/league: 2 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and 4 RTX 6000 Ada, roughly 1,150 GPU-hours; large-model IL→RL: A100 80GB, roughly 40–60 GPU-hours; groundwork: V100; early heuristics: RTX 3060 Ti.

solution_title: 3rd Place Solution for the "ICR - Identifying Age-Related Conditions" Competition
solution_summary: The final solution was a CatBoost baseline augmented with cross-calculated features derived from the anonymous inputs. Medical indicator ratios motivated the feature construction, and the author ultimately applied cross calculations across all features. CatBoost achieved a public score of 0.21, while LightGBM with the same features scored 0.22 publicly and 0.38 privately. Correlation-based feature filtering was considered but never implemented.

A modified one-dimensional U-Net directly regressed event timing using signed, exponentially decaying targets. Daily inputs included neighboring-day context, transformed motion features, and a dummy-data flag, with dummy predictions excluded from learning. Outputs from ten cross-validation folds were averaged, adjusted using temporal and confidence weights, and converted into events through two-stage peak extraction. Post-processing improved public scores from 0.755 to 0.770 but only slightly improved private scores from 0.821 to 0.824.

solution_title: #184 | I've Learned A Lot Despite Everything
solution_summary: The author stacked 28 models built from seven estimator families and four feature subsets. Combining competition and original training data, repeated stratified validation, and model-dependent scaling and kernel approximation improved local performance. Custom wrappers handled GAM compatibility and stacking validation issues. The best stacking CV score was 0.841, although a rejected averaging ensemble performed better on the private leaderboard.

Separate men's and women's pipelines estimated team strengths with ridge and mixed-effects models before predicting game score differences with XGBoost. Team ratings controlled for factors such as opponents and home court and were the most important predictive features. A generalized linear model converted predicted margins into win probabilities, with XGBoost tuning performed through cross-validation. The men's pipeline used outside public data, and manual probability overrides had mixed outcomes; the reported private score was 0.17704.
compute: Initial full pipeline run takes multiple days.

solution_title: 23rd Place Solution: You don't need heuristics or expensive GPU
solution_summary: The solution emphasized label denoising and segmentation cleanup around a five-fold DenseNet121 model. Graph signal denoising identified confident groups of cells for label refinement rather than supplying predictions directly. Removing border cells and adapting small-nucleus removal improved the public score from 0.523 to 0.527, while inference masked neighboring cells. The final negative-class probability used the minimum complement across pattern probabilities. Crowded-cell splitting and a separate mitotic-spindle classifier did not improve scores.

solution_title: 22th solution: fine tune pre-trained GraphNet combined with plane fit by BDT
solution_summary: The author fine-tuned a pretrained GraphNet DynEdge model in two stages, using a warmup-and-decay schedule followed by training with perturbed pulse times and charges. Events were capped at 200 pulses, prioritizing pulses without the auxiliary label. A least-squares plane fit supplied an alternative direction prediction, and a boosted decision tree selected when to use the projected prediction. Noise augmentation improved the reported error by about 0.002, while tuning the tree's selection threshold added roughly 0.001 improvement.
compute: Initial fine-tuning for 10 epochs, followed by 5 epochs of noise-augmented training; maximum 200 pulses per event due partly to compute constraints.

solution_summary: The author used a GitHub implementation of ProGAN in PyTorch and retained it throughout the competition. The approach quickly reached a score of 32 but showed limited further improvement. BigGAN was mentioned as a potentially stronger alternative, without any claim that it was tested.

The post links to a solution notebook without describing its methods. The author thanks contributors of open-source kernels for helping them get started. They report starting during the final ten days.

The solution combined BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet checkpoints with separate models for question and answer targets. Inputs included category prefixes, a special title separator, and head-and-tail text truncation, while average-pooled representations fed a linear prediction layer. Freezing the transformer for the first epoch was crucial, and training also used one round of pseudo-labeling. Optimized per-column thresholds and host-based spelling corrections completed the pipeline after more than 150 experiments.

The solution combined Perch v2 with two conventional sound-event detectors and two Perch-distilled detectors. Prior-year pretrained backbones and foundation-model-based pseudo-labels were central to the strongest individual models. A weighted, rank-gated blend used Perch to suppress weak species predictions, followed by taxonomic and temporal post-processing. The distilled models reached about 0.942 standalone leaderboard scores, and inference was scheduled within a four-vCPU budget.
compute: Inference limited to 4 vCPUs, scheduled as two 2-vCPU lanes; single-model runs approximately 20 minutes.

solution_title: 0.564 Private Score Solution | LightAutoML | Feature Fusion
solution_summary: The authors built 323 features by extending publicly shared feature engineering code. They used LightAutoML with a fusion of cb_tuned, denselight, and autoint, averaging results across three seeds. This notebook achieved CV 0.595 and public LB 0.584 but was not selected for the final submission. Its private score was 0.564.
compute: GPU required to run the notebook.

solution_summary: The author used a single CatBoost regression model with historical visitor and transaction features. Monthly forecast cutoffs supplied overlapping training examples, with expanding-history features and a rolling 12-cutoff training window. Purchase frequency and recency statistics were central, alongside historical conversion-rate encodings of categorical variables. CatBoost outperformed LightGBM, while restored source-column information failed to improve performance and was removed.

solution_title: Rank8 approach - trust the CV score
solution_summary: The solution combined extensive feature engineering with diverse boosted trees and tabular neural networks. A store of over 1,000 features supported model-specific subsets, with a few strong features contributing much more than large collections of moderate ones. XGBoost provided the strongest single models, while LightGBM, CatBoost, TabM and RealMLP added diversity. AutoGluon stacking, logistic regression blending and averaging produced modest gains, although some ensembles improved validation while hurting leaderboard performance.
compute: Colab L4 and A100 (80GB) for XGBoost and LightGBM; A6000Ada for CatBoost; A100 (80GB) for TabM and RealMLP.

solution_title: LB 0.603 without data, a zero shot solution
solution_summary: The approach uses CLIP ViT-H as an encoder and appends a PCA layer trained on GPT3-generated data. It achieves a private score of 0.603, compared with 0.553 for a baseline that randomly selects 64 of 1024 neurons. The main gain comes from the learned PCA projection without using conventional training data.

The solution combined matches from four local feature detectors similar to KeyNetAffNetHardNet, using HardNet8 descriptors and AdaLAM matching across all image pairs. Matching-distance filtering and USAC_MAGSAC geometric verification supplied inlier matches directly to COLMAP incremental reconstruction. EXIF focal-length priors improved reconstruction for some scenes, while multiprocessing kept the pipeline within about 7.5 hours. A KeyNetAffNetHardNet configuration with 8,000 features and a 1,600-pixel maximum edge scored 0.414 public and 0.457 private.
compute: About 7.5 hours with four detectors, maximum image edge 1600; multiprocessing utilized the second CPU core.

solution_title: Some ML, A lot of judgement and luck
solution_summary: The approach uses LightGBM to predict future multiplicative growth rates rather than cumulative case counts directly. Features describe epidemic milestones, recent smoothed growth, and current counts, with a separate log-count-difference model added to handle zero cases. Week-four development used previous competition weeks for validation and added US county data with a small improvement. Manually chosen regional growth decays and plateau rules were the most important part of the final predictions.
compute: Windows laptop.
external_data: ["USA county-level data", "Geographical data and recoveries", "News and dashboards shared on competition forums"]

solution_summary: The author trained a universal Transformer from expert replays, adapted it to exact deck lists, and improved deck policies through PPO and self-play. Local tournaments identified Mega Lopunny as the strongest generalist but exposed a weakness against Mega Lucario, motivating targeted PPO against multiple Lucario lists. The final submissions were the resulting specialist and a confidence router that chose between it and the original policy. Paired evaluations with fresh seeds and diverse opponents supported the router's broader reliability; the submissions received ratings of 870.5 and 871.0.

solution_title: Has anyone had success with the reinforcement learning approach?
solution_summary: The author experimented with reinforcement learning to solve competition puzzles. It did not outperform optimization approaches overall, but it successfully solved some puzzles. The shared notebook achieved a combined total of 267 for the three Wreath_33/33 puzzles with IDs 334, 335, and 336.

The solution used recent purchase co-occurrences to retrieve a compact set of recommendation candidates, averaging about 25 per customer. Pair strength and purchase-history features fed LGBMRanker alongside candidates from previous purchases and age-group popularity. Generating the final submission with two models took 20 minutes, and a later FIL inference refactor reduced notebook runtime to 12 minutes.

solution_title: 24th place solution - pre-training & single model (5 folds ensemble with ONNX)
solution_summary: The solution pretrained an EfficientNet-B0 sound event detection model on earlier BirdCLEF and xeno-canto data before fine-tuning on the 2023 dataset. Raw waveform augmentation, five-second log-mel inputs, and combined clipwise and segmentwise losses were central. Five fold models were ensembled, with ONNX graph optimization and multiprocessing allowing inference within the available time. The multiple-loss ensemble achieved CV 0.7720 and private score 0.73641.
compute: Four-model PyTorch inference took nearly two hours; optimized inference used CPU multiprocessing.

solution_title: LB 15th (0.9970) Some new ideas (and a bug!)
solution_summary: The solution first generated full-resolution coarse masks with a regular U-Net, then refined contour regions with a residual U-Net operating on 384×384 patches. Refinement inputs combined RGB, background-difference features derived from the car's 16 views, and coarse-mask probabilities. Overlapping patch predictions favored center pixels, and horizontal flips were used during training and inference. An inference-pipeline bug forced rejection of refined masks with Dice similarity below 0.999 to their coarse masks, limiting useful corrections.

solution_title: Pushing the Limits: Post-Training High-Capability Models under Strict Inference
solution_summary: The excerpt compares supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for GPT-OSS-120B using difficult mathematical problems and tool-integrated reasoning. Full-parameter fine-tuning used verified trajectories from stronger models, extended training, and increased sampling of tool-use examples. Reinforcement learning used filtered boundary-of-competence problems and a modified GRPO recipe. Both approaches modestly improved tool-enabled average accuracy and majority-vote accuracy while reducing coverage; the excerpt ends before establishing the final competition inference pipeline.
compute: Evaluation: single NVIDIA H100 GPU, 5-hour limit per run. SFT: 10 epochs and approximately 10.37 billion tokens; training hardware unspecified.

solution_title: How Much Did It Rain? II
solution_summary: The pipeline replaces missing values with zeros, removes training outliers, and trains multiple neural networks using a validation holdout. Random dropin augmentation produces 61 copies of both the training and test sets. Predictions are averaged across augmented test copies, with a further average of the two strongest models described as sufficient for the winning result. Model parameters are selected by validation performance.

The team removed marked and duplicate samples using public analyses and manual inspection. They trained EfficientNet and MixNet models with several tile counts and regularization settings. The ensemble combined models trained on cleaned and raw data, with normalized weights chosen from local cross-validation. Trusting stable local validation was central to their approach.

The team trained a WaveNet forecasting model with randomly sampled sequences and randomly chosen forecast start dates. They validated on the last 16 days and stabilized fluctuating predictions through exponential moving averaging tuned on local validation. Additional processing included a maximum-observation cap and heuristic predictions for new items. Late submissions showed that the new-item adjustment slightly worsened the score by less than 0.001.

The author refined a public ensemble notebook by combining several CNN architectures, including DenseNet201, EfficientNet variants, ResNet, and EdgeNeXt. The main refinements were architecture selection and class-specific postprocessing weights. Predictions were also rounded to four decimal places, which the author reported helped the public score. The reported public and private scores were 0.47 and 0.52, respectively.

solution_title: Key Improvements in 17th Solution: A Technical Summary
solution_summary: The solution extends a mouse action recognition baseline through stricter data filtering, extensive motion and interaction features, and lab-specific models. Its features capture body mechanics, temporal coordination, and relationships between mice. Optuna jointly tunes probability thresholds, gap filling, and minimum segment length to produce coherent behavior segments. Missing body parts are handled proactively, while dtype reduction and saved models make experimentation more efficient.

The text describes a Carvana image segmentation solution despite the supplied competition metadata. It uses a modified U-Net implemented in Keras, adding residual and inception blocks, skip connections, and high-resolution training. The repository also provides weighted averaging of submission files. The reported private leaderboard score is 0.9967.

The solution combined differently seeded SE-ResNeXt50 models with custom heads for root, vowel, consonant components, and auxiliary grapheme classification. Its main improvement came from replacing seven consonant classes with six multilabel component targets, allowing related classes to share knowledge of special written forms and improving public leaderboard performance from 0.990 to 0.993. Training used all available training data, four cosine annealing cycles, and increasingly strong augmentation. Consonant threshold tuning and nearest-training-example corrections for uncertain root and vowel predictions further improved the public score to 0.9942.

The final ensemble combined diverse CatBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost, MLP and 1D CNN models trained with the same five-fold stratified group splits. Sorted hierarchical aggregations, categorical encodings, model-specific feature sets and models excluding date columns provided useful diversity. A ten-fold linear regression meta-model improved on weighted averaging, while adversarial-classifier metric hacking failed on the private leaderboard. The submitted ensemble scored 0.528 privately, and adding an omitted CatBoost model after the competition increased that score to 0.536.
compute: 1D CNN trained on TPU and inferred on GPU; TPU also used for permutation importance.

solution_summary: The solution generated recommendation candidates with SAR, trending products, and age-specific popularity, then ranked them using LightGBM classifiers with around 300 features. Features combined transaction aggregates, recall scores, and word2vec embeddings of purchase histories, with the last week used for validation. Four models were averaged, using 200 candidates per customer for training and 400 for inference. RAPIDS accelerated feature generation and inference, and the final ensemble achieved a private score of 0.0346.

solution_title: 10th Place Solution: Geometric Brownian Motion and Mixture Density Networks
solution_summary: The solution fitted geometric Brownian motion with drift to the return horizons and used the estimated drift as an additional neural-network target. A density network predicted a six-dimensional Gaussian distribution over returns and drift using a Cholesky covariance parameterization and negative log likelihood. Carefully tuned dropout helped balance overfitting and numerical instability, while purged cross-validation guided model selection. The final trading rule used the average of the predicted mean vector and traded when it was positive.

The post outlines a simple sensor-classification approach involving dataset preparation and a GRU-based model. It highlights feature engineering and data structuring as the main opportunities for improvement. It also mentions comparing classical classifiers with recurrent models, but provides no concrete training configuration, validation procedure, or numerical results.

The final approach combined ChemBERTa regression, an averaged GNN–GREA model, and CatBoost using weights of 0.33, 0.24, and 0.43. CatBoost benefited from adding several molecular fingerprints to Mordred descriptors, while molecular representation augmentation supported the neural models. Concatenating neural hidden states into an MLP and reducing descriptor dimensions with PCA did not improve the final ensemble. The writeup reports ensemble scores inconsistently as 0.065 and 0.060 and states that no post-processing was applied.

Cookie ranks within each device were especially influential, and cross-validation reduced the feature set. Out-of-sample cookie-match predictions supplemented a modified XGBoost pairwise ranking model trained after heavy cellular-IP downsampling. Predictions selected the highest-scoring cookie's handle and returned every cookie associated with that handle; the attempted ensemble scored worse than the strongest individual model.

solution_title: First Kaggle competition : 10th place public leaderboard; Nth place private leaderboard

Separate multi-input Keras networks predicted selected labels for each GO ontology using binary cross-entropy and information-accretion class weights. Predictions were averaged across five-fold training with five random splits and then combined with a public ensemble. Text features increased the public score from about 0.55 to 0.58, and the final ensemble reached about 0.62.

solution_title: While waiting for the final results.....What solutions/approaches were used
solution_summary: The author described two submissions for the ongoing evaluation period. One retrained a single LightGBM model when updated training data became available, using a 45-day validation period to choose the iteration count before full-data training. It processed only newly added data and reloaded essential artifacts after refreshing memory to reduce resource use. The other used pretrained LightGBM, CatBoost, and neural-network models, including 30 neural models with varied epochs and training-data approaches.

The post announces cleaned-up competition code and a more detailed blog writeup. It links to code on Kaggle and GitHub and a blog post on Medium. The author invites feedback but provides no technical solution details in the post itself.

The best submission stacked two DeBERTa-v3-large variants and bert-for-patents with LightGBM. Inputs were lowercased, CPC context semicolons were replaced with periods, and a new separator token joined anchor, target, and context. The stacker used model predictions and tokenizer-specific text lengths to account for varying matching difficulty. Context cleaning, special tokens, and length features each improved validation, while several pretraining, architecture, and tuning attempts did not help.

The approach repeatedly unrolled candidate helices and clustered transformed hits with DBSCAN. It sampled helix parameters from training tracks, transformed slope with arcsinh, and corrected angles for the uneven magnetic field. Candidate tracks competed using volume coverage and a quality score derived from training-track layer sequences. Merging an inner-volume model and a third similar model improved results beyond the base score of 0.785, with about 95% of centered tracks found.
