solution_summary: The solution trained sound-event detection models on mel spectrograms and iteratively added confident pseudo-labels from training soundscapes. Cleaning removed obvious speech and segments lacking the target species, while a modified cross-entropy objective reduced noisy predictions. The final ensemble combined ten models with diversity from architectures, spectrogram resolutions, and pseudo-label mixtures. It achieved public and private scores of 0.915 and 0.921, although leaderboard instability complicated model selection.

The solution exploited endpoint linkage between series, copying training labels to linked test series and using a Random Forest for the remaining predictions. It smoothed inconsistent labels along linked sequences and added forward and backward moving-average features. Signal features included MFCCs and SciPy-based detrending, peak, spectral, and stability measurements, with feature additions evaluated using original-group cross-validation. The final model used 75-fold stratified validation and achieved 0.92 on the public leaderboard but 0.76 on the private leaderboard.

solution_title: 15th Place - Trust Your CV and Model Diversity!
solution_summary: The team combined diverse transformer backbones, prediction heads, and training schedules to reduce overfitting on the small training set. Fine-tuned neural predictions were blended with Bayesian Ridge and support vector regression predictions from transformer embeddings, with combination ratios selected using out-of-fold scores. Model inclusion considered both cross-validation and leaderboard performance. The final ensemble achieved CV 0.452 and private leaderboard 0.450, with an additional prediction shift of minus 0.02.

The solution uses a four-stage matching pipeline that retrieves geographic and name-embedding neighbors, filters candidates with LightGBM, and combines tree models with multilingual transformers. String similarities, geographic distances, reduced name embeddings, and grouped statistics provide structured matching features. Match-set merging and transformer rescoring improve cross-validation to 0.9166. Linking overlapping training and test records then adds known true matches and removes false matches, producing reported private/public scores of 0.977/0.978 for one final variant.

The solution used a single list-wise DeBERTa-v3-large model trained on all competition data, with notebook cells separated by special tokens. Masked language model pretraining, shorter text preprocessing, an LSTM head, and larger cell counts and sequence lengths improved performance. The model predicted positions for both code and markdown cells, after which code cells were restored to their known order. Translation, adding code ranks to dense layers, and training a transformer over extracted embeddings did not help.

solution_summary: The pipeline detected keypoints, proposed anatomical crops with geometric heuristics, and classified crop severity. Per-image heatmap models used three consecutive slices, with simplified labels that separated level detection from side detection. DICOM world coordinates and T2 landmarks supplied missing anatomical information, while mirroring and interpolation repaired selected missing landmarks. A shared timm backbone with three series-specific severity heads classified the crops; geometric side and level inference each reached about 97% accuracy.

solution_title: 3th place solution - I CAn'T believe I won
solution_summary: The solution used L2-regularized logistic regression with increased weight for the positive class. Binary variables were encoded as zero and one, nominal and calendar variables were one-hot encoded, and ordinal variables received ordinal encoding. Categories absent from either training or test data were pooled into an other category for three nominal columns. Rare nom_9 categories with fewer than three occurrences were also pooled to reduce overfitting.

solution_title: Ensembling works.. unless you pick the (only) overfit one
solution_summary: The author combined LightGBM, XGBoost, and TabPFN models with selected feature subsets, different targets, and Bayesian-tuned configurations. Models were bagged across 10 or 20 stratified folds, with particularly poor folds removed before logistic-regression stacking or optimization of linear ensemble weights. Ensembles generally outperformed individual models, and the best unselected ensemble achieved a private score of 0.38435. The final submissions favored a Class-target LightGBM configuration that performed strongly in cross-validation and on the public leaderboard, but the author suspected its large ensemble weight contributed to private-set overfitting.

The agent used imitation learning with two U-Nets: one predicted unit actions over the world map, and the other predicted SAP targets for individual units. Training examples came from selected Frog Parade and Flat Neurons replays, with hidden state reconstructed from observations available to the replay agent. Map normalization, weighted cross-entropy, and heavy removal of all-Center examples addressed data imbalance. The submission fine-tuned on Flat Neurons performed better in local evaluation and on the public leaderboard.
compute: Several days downloading and preparing data; a couple of hours of training.

solution_title: 12th - whaouh ! - my first real kaggle game
solution_summary: The solution transformed categorical data with extensive frequency encoding, some rank encoding, and decomposed version features. It blended two LightGBM models with contrasting tree configurations: a shallow model with large leaves and a deeper model with smaller leaves. The individual models scored 0.691 and 0.693 on the public leaderboard, and validation used three or five folds. Backward feature selection removed harmful features, while an alternative using test-derived frequency encodings was tried but not retained.
compute: Home PC with 8 cores and 16 GB RAM; some EC2 machines with 16 cores.

solution_title: 70th Place Solution: 5 Model Ensemble Combining 1D-ResNet, Wavenet, Chrononet, and Two Variations of Efficientnet-B0
solution_summary: The team ensembled raw-EEG models with EfficientNet-B0 models trained on two spectrogram representations. The raw branch combined a dual-resolution attention ResNet, WaveNet-GRU, and ChronoNet, while the spectrogram branches supplied most of the ensemble weight. Five-fold patient-group validation stratified by voter-count bins improved results, and training generally progressed from stage 1 data to stage 2 data. Augmentation and a voter-count auxiliary target helped training, but reusing stage 1 validation data for stage 2 likely weakened checkpoint selection. The final ensemble scored 0.289 publicly and 0.345 privately.

solution_title: 10th(11th) Place Solution: This is my first solo gold medal !!!

Dump retrieval used compressed FAISS article indexes followed by sliding-window context retrieval, while the other sources used TF-IDF and embedding search. Predictions across contexts were combined by taking each answer's maximum probability, followed by conditional TF-IDF corrections. Training used approximately 60,000 generated examples, and inference contexts were twice the training length.

They attributed the favorable final shake-up partly to that decision, but provided no model identities or detailed training settings in the post.

The solution retrieved candidate keywords using TF-IDF on CPC and patent titles, then used a genetic algorithm to select keywords within the query limit. Whoosh Boolean operators combined categories and excluded patents with particular fields. Multiprocessing accelerated independent query generation and file processing. Broader keyword sources were discarded for runtime or score reasons, and more expensive search configurations reached 0.7–0.8 locally but exceeded submission time limits.

The team combined six strong sequence models, with LSTM and Squeezeformer performing particularly well. They used the full low-resolution ClimSim dataset for final training, standardized inputs and targets, and added physical and vertical-difference features. Training with MAE or Smooth L1 followed by MSE fine-tuning consistently improved accuracy, while physical constraints corrected predictions afterward. Nelder–Mead optimized ensemble weights, yielding public and private scores of 0.78560 and 0.79080.

The team used a 16-layer transformer encoder combining nucleotide embeddings, secondary-structure embeddings, and per-nucleotide base-pair probability statistics. Base-pair probabilities and structure adjacency matrices supplied learned attention biases, with additional structures generated by mxfold2. Training used cluster-grouped five-fold validation, AdamW, OneCycleLR, and randomized ordered positional indices to encourage longer-sequence generalization. The final predictions averaged all five folds of seven selected model variants; bfloat16 training and pseudo-labeling did not help.
compute: Models trained for 100 epochs with batch size 32; additional computing resources supplied by Freepik.

solution_summary: The team combined EfficientNet, RegNetY, and vision transformer models, selecting submissions for model diversity and public leaderboard performance. GridMask, label smoothing, stochastic weight averaging, and varied test-time crops each improved reported scores. AdamP helped the transformer and RegNetY models but reduced EfficientNet performance. The diverse submission scored 899 on the private leaderboard, compared with 897 for the submission selected for its highest public score.

The author trained LightGBM and CatBoost on three complementary feature sets covering order-book imbalances, grouped statistics, temporal changes, and moving averages. For each feature set and learner, validation selected between an overall model and a model specialized for each seconds_in_bucket value. Validation used the first 435 days for training and the final 45 days for evaluation, followed by retraining on all data. The six resulting prediction streams were averaged and mean-centered, yielding public and private scores of 5.3315 and 5.4621.

The approach centered on feature engineering and stacking. More than 110,000 pseudo-labels supported semi-supervised learning at the second stacking level. The author used default model settings without performing model optimization. The text provides only a brief outline and does not identify the individual models or features.

The team fine-tuned SDXL on high-scoring images selected from 16 earlier Flux Schnell and SDXL runs. For each prompt, they generated approximately 14–18 candidates, converted them to compact SVGs and selected the best using proxy VQA scoring. Optimized VTracer settings, scour minification and smaller bitmap sizes met the 10kB limit, while a small corner plus sign addressed OCR scoring. Local validation correlated with the leaderboard but remained noisy, so the team selected two strong submissions with different seeds.
compute: Two GPUs used in parallel for image generation and scoring; approximately 14–18 candidate images per sample.

solution_summary: The solution fine-tuned the lightweight all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model for misconception retrieval. Generated explanations from Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-AWQ were crucial, with explanation variants and similarity-based negatives refreshed each epoch. Validation grouped examples by misconception ID to assess generalization to unseen misconceptions, and the final model used all training data. Fine-tuning improved private leaderboard performance from 0.22645 to 0.28002; filtering rare misconception IDs improved scores further but was excluded from the final submission.

The solution used iterative missing-value imputation, features extracted from parquet files, and LightGBM with a custom quadratic weighted kappa objective and metric. A 10 × 10 nested cross-validation procedure supported stable predictions, with thresholds optimized once from the combined validation predictions. Seed checks produced average public and private scores of 0.440 and 0.469. Ablations identified imputation as especially important, while the custom objective improved validation without a corresponding private-score gain.

The final solution combined six groups of classification and segmentation models and achieved a public leaderboard score of 0.801. Diversity came from backbones, image sizes, channel choices, preprocessing, and simulated signals. Custom sine deformation and generated messages helped address S-shaped signals, while pseudo-labeling, checkpoint averaging, and test-time augmentation provided further gains. Autoencoder embedding analysis revealed repeated backgrounds, but that direction was abandoned.

The solution blended an LSTM with Universal Sentence Encoder and a diverse collection of pretrained transformer models using text and category inputs. Different truncation strategies and longer answer token budgets provided input diversity. Training used min-max target scaling, increased weights for rare outcomes, cosine warmup, and exponential moving averages. Optimized prediction clipping raised the reported cross-validation score from 0.4434 to 0.4852, while TPE selected the final blending weights.

solution_title: How I did it: Lee Baker on winning Tourism Forecasting Part One
solution_summary: The final forecast blends a growth-adjusted naive predictor, an ordinary linear regression, and an exponentially weighted linear regression. The naive forecast compounds the last observation by 5.5% annually, while regression weights depend on their fit quality through logistic functions of R-squared. Validation initially held out the last four training years, but later changes were assessed mainly through leaderboard submissions as local validation became less reliable. Numerical optimization of blend parameters was discarded because its training improvement did not translate to leaderboard performance.

The solution paired a ten-model classification ensemble with fifty detectors spanning RetinaNet, deformable R-FCN, and deformable relation networks. Classifiers transferred ImageNet weights through NIH ChestX-ray14 training before pneumonia fine-tuning, and extensive test-time augmentation supported both classification and detection. Detector boxes were merged in stages, with confidence adjusted by prediction agreement and classifier scores or thresholds. Shrinking predicted box widths and heights to 87.5% produced a major improvement, raising the final stage 1 score from 0.222 to 0.260.

solution_title: 10th Place Solution – Boey – End-to-End JAX RL
solution_summary: The solution used an end-to-end JIT-compilable JAX reinforcement learning pipeline with PPO, backpropagation through time, and prioritized fictitious self-play. Observations combined unit histories, persistent spatial information, and scalar game features, while action masks restricted invalid actions and sap targets. Switching from shaped rewards to sparse match-win rewards for the final 10% of training produced significant gains. A second submission used a separate centralized critic, roughly doubling sample efficiency and achieving a rating of 1884.5, although its lower throughput left wall-time efficiency neutral.

solution_summary: The solution adapted a shared LightGBM one-step-ahead forecasting approach. It used eight weeks of training data beginning May 31, 2017, with additional distribution statistics and first differences of mean values. Store and item information was represented through one-hot and count encoding. Averaging predictions across random seeds stabilized performance, and the model achieved a private score of 0.517.

solution_title: My First Kaggle Competition: A silver solution (83rd place)
solution_summary: The solution combined geographic, image, text, aggregated, and categorical interaction features. Base models comprised one XGBoost, two LightGBM models, an LSTM-based RNN, and ridge regression, followed by LightGBM stacking using five-fold cross-validation. Text representations included TF-IDF, SVD, and fastText embeddings, while image features included basic statistics and YOLO detections. Memory limits and interrupted AWS spot training prevented completion of a second neural network.

solution_title: 35th place: squeezing out the last -0.0011 RMSE
solution_summary: The solution combined heavily engineered numerical features with text and image models using XGBoost, LightGBM, and Keras neural networks. Text representations included TF-IDF, counts, weighted embeddings, and embeddings trained entirely on Avito text. Correlation pruning and specialized models for individual feature groups improved ensemble diversity. Nonlinear XGBoost and CatBoost stackers, categorical and price inputs, and a final stack of stackers collectively reduced RMSE by about 0.0011.

solution_title: 🥈24th in two weeks and `No space left on device`!
solution_summary: The approach used wav2vec2 XLS-R-300M with a five-gram KenLM language model trained on Bengali text corpora. Training combined competition audio with MadASR2023 and OpenSLR53, with filtering helping improve data quality. AudioSet background noises supplied augmentation, and a separate punctuation restoration step addressed errors identified through manual inspection. A custom dataset loaded and transformed audio on demand to avoid storage and preprocessing overhead.

solution_title: 112th Place (Silver) — 20+ Experiments, and the First Model Won
solution_summary: The final system centered on a sigmoid of schedule-adjusted efficiency margin, blended with gender-specific supporting models using manually chosen weights. Men's predictions incorporated LightGBM, Elo, and seed-matchup probabilities, while women's predictions used logistic regression and Elo. Massey ordinal rankings supplied useful additional signal for men, whereas many later experiments failed to improve walk-forward validation. Updating the data and actual tournament seeds and fixing pipeline bugs preceded a final Brier score of 0.1247.

solution_title: 5th solution summary: Learning to imitate the best leaderboard agents using Conditional Unet
solution_summary: The final agent used imitation learning with a conditioned U-Net that consumed spatial game features, global state, and the identity of the agent to imitate. Training on roughly 16,000 matches from 82 strong agents improved generalization, while the identity input allowed selecting an imitation target at inference. Separate action and policy outputs for units and cities used masked losses, and inference included horizontal flips. Training usually took less than one day on a single RTX 3090, but the author observed a substantial remaining gap to the strongest source agents.
compute: Single 3090 GPU; training usually less than one day.

solution_title: Home Depot Product Search Relevance, Winners' Interview: 2nd Place | Thomas, Sean, Qingchen, & Nima
solution_summary: The solution emphasized text preprocessing and diverse features capturing category matches, lexical overlap, co-occurrence, semantic similarity, and relevance-based statistics. Combining teammates' features proved more valuable than simply combining their predictions. The final ensemble contained 19 XGBoost, GBM, and ridge models, with ridge consistently contributing useful diversity. Random forests and Extra Trees were dropped after they stopped improving the ensemble; the best single XGBoost model achieved a public score of 0.43347.

solution_summary: The author generated cross-validated predictions from five public models and added them as five new input features. Rerunning the models with these expanded inputs produced four additional variants, while the fifth variant duplicated its original predictions. The final ensemble combined 15 models using loosely fitted Boltzmann weights with an effective total weight equivalent to roughly six models. This performed better than the simple median ensemble tested by the author.

The author implemented an S3FD-like detector in PyTorch using pretrained VGG16 and a feature pyramid network. Training combined positive pneumonia images with synthetic examples made by pasting pneumonia regions into normal images. Cluster-informed anchors, IoU-weighted classification and regression losses, and two-stage box suppression refined detection. The final submission ensembled six models with multiscale testing and achieved a private score of 0.228.

solution_title: PS S6E4 retrospective: +42 rank jump to Top 0.7% (rank 30/4316)
solution_summary: The author selected a conservative logistic-regression stack alongside an aggressive ensemble derived from a public notebook. Selection emphasized a small positive OOF balanced-accuracy minus public-score gap, different aggregation methods across the two submissions, and limited drift in High-class predictions. The successful meta-learner required logit inputs, balanced class weights, and multinomial logistic regression. The conservative submission scored 0.98059 on both public and private data, while the aggressive submission declined to 0.98051 privately.

The author built two-stage segmentation models that refine initial predictions using the original input and intermediate features. One variant used false-color images, while another consumed all nine spectral bands. Larger encoders performed better, and training used geometric augmentation. Taking the maximum over original predictions and selected one-pixel diagonal-shift predictions improved the score by about 0.01, while flip and rotation TTA hurt validation.

The author builds bidder-level behavioral features and trains scikit-learn random forests to classify humans and bots. Useful signals include bidding timing, auction activity, weekday distributions, URL and IP diversity, and IP overlap with known bots. Validation repeats random 80–20 splits 100 times, with the mean score within about 0.003 of the final leaderboard score. Final predictions are the simple average of five random forests initialized with different random seeds.

solution_title: 4th Place Solution for the March Machine Learning Mania 2025 Competition
solution_summary: The approach fits XGBoost to point differentials with a Cauchy loss, then uses logistic regression on its leaf nodes to predict wins. It extends the referenced baseline with Laplace-smoothed matchup and recent-performance features plus stacked out-of-fold predictions. Model selection relied on the Brier score for a held-out 2024 season, while leave-one-season-out models were used for averaging. The author rejected leaky validation and spline processing and used only official competition data.

The author trained ten timm image classifiers on merged 2019 and 2020 data, with validation restricted to 2020 images. Training used five stratified folds, extensive augmentation, cross-entropy with 0.3 label smoothing, AdamW, and cosine warm restarts. The final ensemble averaged predictions from 1D-CNN stacking, 2D-CNN stacking, and optimized model weights. Simple averaging was not selected for the final submission but achieved a better private score of 0.9014 versus 0.9008 for stacking.

solution_title: Finally GM & 1st time won prize money! And 3rd place solution.
solution_summary: The solution separated empty-mask detection from accurate positive-mask segmentation using a BCE segmentation model and a positive-only soft Dice segmentation model. Positive predictions from the first model were replaced by the second model's masks, then an image classifier removed additional empty predictions. The final pipeline combined DenseNet121-FPN, several FPN and U-Net segmenters, and a b1 classifier with fold ensembles and flip augmentation. Confidence-filtered pseudo labels and channel-specific classifier thresholds raised the reported leaderboard score to 0.6805.

solution_summary: The author treated defect prediction as a multi-label problem and combined PyBoost, AutoGluon, and public submissions. OpenFE generated additional features, while averaging trusted predictions was the central strategy. The selected mixture achieved a private score of 0.88936, compared with 0.88763 for the PyBoost and OpenFE submission. Multi-class modeling, standalone models, and original data were less successful.

The solution first estimated probabilities for all eight response classes using a two-level stack. Its inputs combined original attributes with embeddings, clustering, and lasso-selected interactions and random-forest node features. First-level tree, nearest-neighbor, neural-network, and linear models fed multinomial XGBoost and neural-network models whose probabilities were averaged. Final labels were optimized across the test set by repeatedly choosing assignments that maximized expected Quadratic Weighted Kappa until convergence.

The solution extracted CNN convolutional features with GeM pooling and L2 normalization for landmark retrieval. Original and horizontally flipped index and query images were processed, followed by PCA, whitening, normalization, and nearest-neighbor search. Multiple architectures were ensembled by aggregating retrieval distances, taking the minimum distance for flipped images. The ensemble achieved 0.10439 private and 0.08832 public scores, compared with 0.08813 private and 0.06335 public for the best single model.

solution_title: [72nd Place Solution] 4 Folds Single Model Could Get Private LB 0.964 (After Postprocess 0.960)
solution_summary: The solution used a DeBERTa-v3-large architecture across four folds, grouping final-layer representations into spaCy tokens before passing them to a GRU. Training used an O-class weighted loss, label smoothing, and an external-data epoch followed by two epochs on the original data. Three submissions used different inference maximum lengths and the same rule-based postprocessing. Postprocessing improved the public score by 0.001 but reduced the private score by 0.005; a version without it achieved 0.964 privately.

The solution combined two LightGBM models, Random Forest, a fastai neural network, CatBoost, PerpetualBooster, ridge regression, and kNN. Random five-fold cross-validation guided feature engineering and a weighted ensemble regularized toward equal weights, followed by additional manual smoothing. Categorical representations included leakage-controlled target encoding and neural embeddings, while text fields were parsed into features. Model diversity and strong regularization were central, and the neural network used one-cycle training followed by fine-tuning without dropout or batch normalization.

solution_title: 182nd Place Solution for the "ICR - Identifying Age-Related Conditions" Competition (plus the better one)
solution_summary: The submitted approach used CatBoost with features selected by absolute correlation with Alpha above 0.1, treating EJ as categorical. The author describes multiclass training on Alpha with class weights, binary Class validation with separate weights, and five-fold KFold evaluation. The submitted model scored 0.3974 privately, while an all-feature variant with different hyperparameters reached 0.36871. Alternative experiments included four binary subtype models, while stacking, stratified folds, scaling, broad upsampling, and adding Epsilon did not improve results.

The solution combined template-based RNA modeling with multi-seed Protenix inference, pooled their candidates, and selected five structures using physical plausibility and diversity checks. Strong-template sequences relied on template modeling, while weaker sequences received more generative exploration and ultra-long sequences used chunked inference. Deterministic execution enabled reliable experimentation, and template diagnostics exposed missing or structurally misleading references. The final pipeline scored 0.424, with candidate generation and selection providing a substantial improvement over the deterministic baseline.

Two sequence-to-sequence LSTMs forecast 28 days of sales at store-item and department-store levels. Their predictions were averaged after disaggregating the department-store forecasts, and uncertainty estimates assumed independent normally distributed residuals. Averaging predictions from 20 checkpoints per model reduced training instability. Four chronological validation windows guided development and supported stable local and leaderboard performance.

The approach used a symbolic search pipeline driven by task properties such as shapes, colors, grids, and symmetries. Tasks were simplified before searching sequences of operations, with three candidates retained according to training pixel errors. Some tasks were also decomposed into individual shapes or non-common colors and solved again. General preprocessing accounted for many improvements, and merging complementary solutions from another teammate produced a reported leaderboard score of about 0.81.

The final pipeline used RealMLP_TD_Classifier with a fixed feature set and averaged 15 models across three seeds and five stratified folds. Features included ratios, count encodings, quantile bins, and target-encoded category combinations. High-confidence test predictions were added as pseudo-labels before retraining from scratch. Additional features, LightGBM blending, and logit stacking degraded validation or public performance. The submitted pseudo-label round achieved 0.95472 OOF AUC and the same private score.

solution_summary: The solution filtered MegaDetector predictions without training a model or tracking animals. Images were split into low-density and high-density groups using a threshold of eight detections, with separate filtering rules for each. High-density images used a zero confidence threshold and modified NMS, while low-density images used overlap-dependent confidence thresholds and an additional filtering pass. The final sequence count was the maximum image count, and the best reported public score was 0.247.

solution_title: 8th Place Solution -- Decision tree part + source code
solution_summary: This team component treats each task as ten-class pixel classification using engineered features and decision trees. It explores combinations of color transformations, spatial augmentation, and featurizers tailored to input-output size relationships. A logistic regression confidence model trained on the evaluation set selects three candidate predictions. It solved 8 of 102 leaderboard tasks, 76 of 419 evaluation tasks, and 136 of 416 training tasks.

The solution combined 18 LightGBM and XGBoost models using grouped cross-validation and validation on truncated samples. Game event aggregates were included, although their high feature importance translated into little leaderboard improvement. The XGBoost pipeline also incorporated prior test assessments into training and used two truncation seeds per fold. A custom voting rule selected strongly supported classes and otherwise used distances to model thresholds, producing public and private scores of 0.549.

solution_title: 13th Place - From LB 710 to LB 726 - How To
solution_summary: The best submission used a TensorFlow RoBERTa-base span extractor with a modified head that predicted the end position before conditioning the start prediction on its logits. Preserving whitespace, splitting punctuation tokens, and choosing conservative training spans helped model annotation quirks. Label smoothing, random masking, learning-rate decay, sentiment-based sample weights, and full-data retraining improved performance. Repeated cross-validation supported the changes, and final post-processing brought the reported scores to 0.718 CV, 0.724 public, and 0.726 private.

The solution used a modified Faster R-CNN with independent region-proposal and character-classification networks operating on images resized to 512×512. Wide ResNet-34 backbones, clustered anchor sizes, ROI Align, and extensive dropout were central design choices. The final proposal network used color images, while classification used grayscale to limit overfitting. Language-model correction experiments failed to improve the best detector output and were abandoned.

solution_title: Fighting Against Variance Under Compute Constraints

Speculative decoding with an Eagle3 draft model made the workflow fit the runtime limit despite reducing concurrency. Final selection prioritized judge agreement, then combined votes, with average trace length as a last tie-breaker. The selected 65k-context configuration achieved 47/50 locally in 3h 48m and a public score of 42.

solution_summary: The solution used XGBoost with leak-derived information, group features, and a stratified split based on people IDs. The number of people per group was particularly useful, especially for single-person groups. A separate model predicting whether a group had all-zero, all-one, or mixed outcomes supplied a fuzzed and binned feature to the final XGBoost model, improving the reported score from 0.992914 to 0.993118. solution_title: 3rd Place Solution - Congratulations New Competition Grandmaster Amed!
solution_summary: The final submission combined 24 diverse models, mostly DeBERTa-v3-large variants, without pseudo labels. Model diversity came from backbones, regression heads, pooling, training settings, and an embedding-based SVR. Pseudo labels improved local validation substantially but did not improve leaderboard performance and were excluded.

The solution used diverse neural question-pair models to generate out-of-fold features for XGBoost. Its strongest network combined a Siamese bidirectional LSTM, recurrent highway layers, attention, and frozen GloVe embeddings, reaching 89.1% validation accuracy. Character, character-trigram, and convolutional networks added complementary signals alongside semantic and linguistic features. A graph-like feature derived from predicted duplicates helped further, and confident predictions were clipped.

solution_summary: The solution used CNN backbones followed by transformer encoders and decoders to translate molecular images into strings. solution_title: Learning to Build a Long-Running Agent Workflow

Separate analysis, worker, and acceptance agents prioritized tasks, optimized candidates, and evaluated changes against a frozen canonical submission. Persistent documentation, model hashes, and explicit adoption rules made experiments reproducible and allowed work to continue across conversations. Official A/B evaluation was important because local validation did not always match leaderboard behavior.

solution_title: 123rd place — not where I aimed, but here's what I learned
solution_summary: The solution segments papyrus surfaces in CT scans using a 3D TransUNet with a SEResNeXt101 encoder and 160³ voxel inputs. Training combines recall-focused Tversky loss with CenterlineDice to preserve surface continuity, using Keras 3 and JAX on TPU v4-32. Inference averages sliding-window predictions and six flip variants, then blends two checkpoints and applies morphological cleanup. The reported score was 0.579; larger spatial context, loss alignment with the evaluation metrics, and checkpoint blending were central to the approach.

solution_summary: The team averaged a diverse collection of PyTorch and TensorFlow models, including nf-resnet50, ResNeXt50, EfficientNets, and base and large vision transformers. Models varied in image size and test-time augmentation, and some used 2019 competition data. Training augmentations combined crops, geometric and color changes, blur, noise, and dropout. Average ensembling was the most consistently useful component; an unselected blend achieved 0.8978 public and 0.9019 private scores.

The solution used a one-layer bidirectional GRU alongside a dense branch for statistical text features. Frozen embeddings combined pretrained GloVe and wiki-news vectors, competition-trained fastText vectors, and binary token attributes. Batch-specific sequence lengths accelerated training, enabling an ensemble of six independently seeded models. Five-fold validation guided tuning, and averaged predictions were thresholded at 0.36; the reported final-model CV score was 0.70974.

solution_title: A Review of the CTF Competition
solution_summary: The author solved half of the CTF challenges using a mixture of exhaustive searches, optimization, data inspection, and external images. Movement-event counts identified human cells, while systematic coordinate searches optimized baseball pitch patterns. Other successes came from searching numeric keys, reenacting a video, inspecting model metadata, and exploiting unusual scoring inputs. External hot-dog and handwritten-character images also yielded flags.

solution_summary: The solution adapted public notebooks around DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B-AWQ, combining a mathematics prompt with time management and voting across generated answers. solution_summary: The pipeline first localizes and aligns whale heads, then trains recognizers on the aligned crops. It uses several VGG, ResNet, and simplified Inception variants, with test-time augmentation for alignment. Features from the recognizers feed a logistic regression ensemble, while decoded image caching reduces repeated preprocessing.

solution_summary: The solution adapted a public Gemma 9B classifier with additional labeled conversations and data filtering. It removed very short prompts and conflicting labels, adjusted learning rate and batch size, and merged LoRA weights from two epochs. DeBERTa performed substantially worse, and a generation head did not beat the classification head.

The author trained a small neural network on historical regular-season and tournament games, combining team statistics, seeds, conference indicators, and Ken Pom metrics. The final network had hidden layers of 7, 5, and 3 nodes and outperformed random forests and boosted trees. Validation used separate tournament-year holdouts, with log loss between 0.42 and 0.45; the competition result was 0.42788. solution_title: 8th Place Solution for the Child Mind Institute - Detect Sleep States Competition
solution_summary: The solution separated precise event localization from event scoring using a local 1D U-Net regressor and a global-context DensityNet. The regressor predicted relative onset and wakeup positions, while Gaussian accumulation and peak detection produced candidate events. DensityNet used Transformer modules to estimate event densities and event-presence probabilities, which scored those candidates over overlapping daily windows. Prediction shifts, event augmentation, and matrix-profile filtering improved the final detections; the reported augmentation gain was approximately 0.002 mAP.

solution_title: 8th place solution (Flying Over the 1st place again)
solution_summary: The solution improved existing diamond price predictions through domain-informed postprocessing. It capped excessive prices using training-group upper bounds derived from quartiles and the interquartile range. It also raised implausibly low predictions to training minima within carat windows matched on cut, clarity, and color. Correcting training outliers improved CV but harmed leaderboard performance, whereas prediction adjustments produced substantial reported gains.

The author converted point clouds into RGB images and applied an SSD detector. Image brightness encoded point-cloud density, while hue encoded the weighted center of the vertical position. The post links implementation code but gives no validation scores or training details.

The final pipeline used DBSCAN clustering with helix unrolling, multiple z shifts, and track extension after unsuccessful exploration of deep learning approaches. Six geometric features and Bayesian tuning of feature weights, iteration count, and DBSCAN epsilon improved clustering quality. Hits were merged into the longest eligible tracks, and six extension rounds refined the results. The solution scored 0.59229 on the private leaderboard and processed each event in roughly nine to ten minutes on a 96-core GCP machine.

solution_summary: The solution used BERT with five folds and three training epochs, closely following a public notebook. A special token separated question titles from bodies, although its benefit was uncertain. A small LightGBM postprocessor reduced the number of distinct prediction values to improve Spearman correlation. This added about 0.02 on the private leaderboard, yielding a score of 0.39507.

The agent used repeated forward simulation with persistent unit roles and goal state machines to plan actions. Its economy emphasized early lichen growth, adding robots when estimated power income supported further expansion. Factory placement balanced resources and terrain, with an aggressive ice-denial strategy supported by water transporters and blockade units. Prioritized action selection and exclusive assignments coordinated units, although ice conflicts performed poorly against an opponent that moved ice flexibly with heavy robots.

The author developed rock-paper-scissors agents from uniform randomness through multistage statistical prediction to decision trees. solution_title: Max Lin on finishing second in the R Challenge
solution_summary: The author framed package recommendation as binary classification and combined four complementary models: a metadata baseline, latent factors, user-specific topic preferences, and user-specific task-view preferences. solution_title: 95th Bronze solutions: Focal loss + KD + Supplemental data
solution_summary: The author expanded an existing fingerspelling model to 16 CNN-Transformer blocks with dimension 192, eight attention heads, and dropout of 0.4. solution_summary: The solution combined a decision-tree approach with cropping, grid-based DSL methods, tile-based DSL methods, and public kernels. The decision-tree component solved seven tasks, while the grid DSL solved three. Tile DSL methods solved seven tasks after accounting for overlap between two contributors, and public kernels contributed two tasks. The post gives a brief component breakdown and code references without implementation details.

The team ensembled two independently developed pipelines built around approximate customer and card identities. Grouped transaction statistics, temporal features, and categorical encodings supplied LightGBM, CatBoost, and XGBoost models, with CatBoost performing best. One pipeline used month-based grouped validation and multiple seeds, while the other split transactions by ProductCD and used stratified validation. Combining the pipelines provided a substantial gain, whereas neural networks, denoising autoencoders, and stacking did not work well.

The author built a time-series solution associated with an LSTM notebook, separating stocks using features 41–43. Dense time embeddings derived from feature_64 represented irregular observation times, while linear regression denoised targets and substantially improved stability. Training excluded dates before 85 and zero-weight rows, with four-fold combinatorial purged validation. The model had fewer than 100,000 parameters and received only limited manual hyperparameter tuning.

The author adapted SECOND for 3D object detection on the Lyft dataset. They adjusted anchor ranges and object sizes and added the competition metric for validation. An 80:20 scene-based split supported model selection, with VoxelNet and PillarFeatureNet working best.

solution_title: Approach: Maximum non-contiguous sub-matrix sum heuristic
solution_summary: The author developed a GPU cube solver that combines move sequences affecting a fixed number of elements across cube sizes, sharing face moves to reduce cost. The approach generates one- and two-dimensional move sets, checks special cases, and repeatedly selects moves using score per move count. A heuristic handles noncontiguous row and column combinations, while pruning rows and columns without positive scores accelerates later iterations. The implementation remained incomplete, but a laptop run solved a size-33 cube in under an hour using about 15,000 moves.
compute: Move database validation took less than 2 hours on one thread. The reduced move data structure used close to 10 GB VRAM; the first size-17 center iteration took about 20 seconds on an H100. An i7/3070 laptop solved a size-33 cube in less than an hour.

solution_title: How the 300 validation dataset is generated & 57th place solution

Predictions came from an ensemble of public and privately trained DeBERTa-v3-large models, with private training using a filtered 60k dataset and validation on a 500-sample dataset. Each network was trained ten times using fresh random 80/20 splits, retaining checkpoints selected by training and validation F2 scores. Predictions used an optimized threshold for each model and were combined by voting; selecting only models with F2 above 0.93 produced worse leaderboard results.

solution_title: Santa's Stolen Sleigh, Winners' Interview: 3rd place, Marcin Mucha & Marek Cygan

Designing the state representation, moves, and temperature schedule was the main optimization work. Mixed-integer programming helped diagnose route quality but could not scale to larger subsets, while parallel tempering failed to help. Their main retrospective finding was that more locally greedy moves appeared to converge faster than their mostly random moves.

solution_title: 5th Place Solution Overview, Looked till 100th but was right at 5th :)
solution_summary: The team combined essay-reconstruction features with several neural networks and three tree models, achieving a best 10-fold CV score of 0.5860. A 1D CNN adapted from a previous competition solution added useful diversity through public features, feature variants, and additional engineered features. One submission also blended public models at a low weight with the team's models to limit overfitting. Transformers contributed little, and trusting local cross-validation was central to the team's selection process.

The solution emphasized one engineered feature set shared by XGBoost, LightGBM, and TabM, with five seeds per model. Digit extraction, numeric bins, higher-order digit interactions, and original-data encodings supplied the main improvements. Ridge regression combined their OOF predictions with AutoGluon predictions, reaching 0.92805 CV and 0.92912 privately. Fold-specific feature caching accelerated tuning, and reliable CV guided the choice to use fold averages instead of full-data training.

solution_title: 5th place solution: kNN shortlist and rotation correction

A lightweight all-pairs matching pass generated nearest-neighbor shortlists from inlier counts, with extra pairs added to ensure coverage of every image. Rotation correction and parallel COLMAP processing improved robustness and efficiency. The best completed submission ran in 7 hours and 40 minutes; several alternatives were excluded because of accuracy, runtime, or setup problems.

Extensive image augmentation and unsupervised domain adaptation using TMA images were the most important improvements. Feature noise augmentation, alternative backbones, and conventional feature-space outlier detection did not improve the pipeline, and no model ensemble was used.

Target-dependent XGBoost loss weights addressed systematic overprediction of low scores and underprediction of high scores. Diversity came from disagreement-based selection, alternative regression objectives, outlier probabilities, and models specialized by internet access. The resulting ensemble outperformed every individual model, although no numeric final score is supplied.

The solution trained separate two-player and four-player transformer agents through pure self-play PPO with prioritized sampling of past opponents. A reachability tensor supplied travel times, launch angles, ship counts, graph features, and action masks, while semantic actions substantially accelerated learning. Custom attention biases, global conditioning, and a sparse action head helped the model reason about planetary relationships efficiently. Entropy scheduling was the most influential training choice; the submitted checkpoints accumulated about 8.4 billion and 2.7 billion training steps for the two modes.

solution_title: 6th Place Solution for Google Code Golf Championship

Longer programs were compressed with zopfli, then optimized for compressed size through static-analysis-constrained renaming followed by simulated annealing. Hand golfing contributed 955,251 score points, compression added 2,276, and code optimization added about 400.

solution_summary: The solution fed roughly 80 engineered features into a fully connected network with 128- and 64-unit hidden layers and a 199-way softmax output. Most features counted defenders in boxes and radial regions around the rusher at the current time and at projected times of 0.5 and 1.0 seconds. Minimum and mean defender distances supplemented standard rusher information. Rethinking the spatial and temporal features produced the main breakthrough, while simple offensive-player counts did not significantly improve performance.

The solution equally averaged ranked predictions from 11 subject-specific models to improve robustness with minimal weight tuning. Models used short EEG windows and engineered spectral, statistical, correlation, information-theoretic, and Riemannian tangent-space features. XGBoost, nearest neighbors, logistic regression, a linear SVM, and a GLM supplied complementary predictions, with maximum or mean aggregation back to ten-minute segments. Validation preserved one-hour sequence groups and used two complementary fold schemes because reliable evaluation was difficult. The reported ensemble scores were 0.81308 and 0.80701.

ERATO and vLLM supported periodic evaluation on unseen transformation rules. Images were downsampled to x10 and divided into 256×256 tissue patches, with duplicate WSI tissue areas removed to reduce memory use. Perceiver training used binary cross-entropy, mixup, and label smoothing, while DSMIL used cross-entropy. The final approach detected outliers when the maximum sigmoid probability was below 0.4, improving the reported private score from 0.58 to 0.60. solution_title: [88th place] How I went from 1232 on public leaderboard to 88th place
solution_summary: The author emphasized generating substantial amounts of high-quality synthetic data and maintaining a clean codebase. They deliberately limited submissions to reduce the risk of overfitting the public leaderboard. They developed independently without borrowing public notebook models or code, but stopped submitting during the final two months. The solution used a two-stage XLM-RoBERTa pipeline with one encoder and no ensemble. The first stage learned retrieval embeddings using attention pooling, contrastive loss, distance polarized regularization, and negatives mined each epoch. The second stage fine-tuned the first-stage weights to classify topic-content pairs retrieved among the top 50 candidates. Language filtering and score and distance thresholds produced a cross-validation F2 of about 0.6319, with an approximately 0.05 improvement from adding the second stage. Both stages together ran in about six hours.

solution_title: Solution #17 - Searching for the perfect helix
solution_summary: The final approach reconstructs particle tracks using DBSCAN with features derived from helix geometry. It scans curvature radius and longitudinal origin, uses the Hough equation to estimate helix centers, and clusters on center angle and an arc-length-to-longitudinal-displacement ratio. This replaced an earlier three-model ensemble that scored just over 0.66 and required many hours per event. The redesigned method eventually achieved 0.695 with a few hours of processing per event, although rotations beyond 180 degrees were not handled correctly.

solution_title: 24th place solution and my way to get it
solution_summary: The solution blended models trained at several image resolutions, mainly EfficientNet B5–B7 with ImageNet or NoisyStudent initialization, alongside ResNet152 and InceptionResNetV2. Training combined 2018, 2019, and 2020 data, while validation used only 2020 data through a triple-stratified K-fold pipeline. TPU training enabled larger models and images after early GPU experiments with smaller models plateaued. solution_summary: The solution extracted text from different HTML fields and trained a separate bag-of-words logistic regression classifier for each field. A second logistic regression model combined their predictions through stacking. Count and length features were explored, but internal cross-validation favored using only text features. The submission achieved public and private scores of 0.87777 and 0.88764.

Both reported solutions ensembled EfficientNet-b2 through b5 models with noisy-student weights, trained for about 20 epochs on 600-by-600 images. The authors adapted Iocaine Powder by adding two randomized strategies based on the opponent's move history. solution_title: 6th place solution End to End Sequence to Sequence with sliding window.

The recognition solution used precomputed embeddings from the train4.1m dataset and penalized embeddings resembling non-landmark images. These recognition-specific strategies improved a single model from 0.37843/0.36045 to 0.45724/0.43252 on public/private scores. solution_title: 178th Place Solution for the Open Problems – Single-Cell Perturbations
solution_summary: The author combined prediction blends and ridge models using cell type and compound name as features. Biological exploration informed the selection of cell types and compounds expected to have similar responses. Selecting B cells, regulatory T cells, and NK cells helped, while adding CD8 T cells worsened the score. The approach used four-fold cross-validation and per-row RMSE to guide model selection for compounds.

The solution divided the spatial prediction problem into cells and tuned models on a central spatial subset using a chronological holdout. The final ensemble summed probabilities equally across 13 models spanning nearest neighbors, tree methods, naive Bayes, and kernel density estimation. Random hyperparameter search and greedy ensemble selection balanced local performance with model diversity. Bayesian optimization of ensemble weights produced only a negligible improvement, so equal weighting was retained.

solution_summary: The solution combined eight cell classifiers and four whole-image classifiers, averaging their predicted probabilities. Cells inherited whole-image labels during training, while cells with weak green-channel signals were reassigned to class 18. Training all 12 models took about 48 hours on eight 1080Ti GPUs.

solution_summary: The agent repeatedly fitted a bagging classifier to predict the opponent's next move from the preceding five turns of both players. The tree count grew with match progress to keep the training subset per tree roughly constant. It countered predicted moves only when confidence exceeded 70%, otherwise playing randomly. A 200-turn random opening delayed training-data collection and helped obscure its strategy.

The final submission ensembled 55 models spanning U-Net pipelines, recurrent networks, WaveNet, and transformers. Features included normalized movement signals, cyclic hour encodings, signal differences, and downsampled summary statistics. Training benefited from noisy-sample removal, full-data training, exponential moving averages, label smoothing, and combined BCE and peak-specific Dice losses. Postprocessing detected device nonwear and boosted the strongest event candidates within 24-hour periods, improving the reported private score from 0.812 to 0.823.

solution_title: 15th place solution - Dive into compute_f without Grid Generation + Simple 100% KNN Floor
solution_summary: The solution used site-specific TF-IDF KNN models for floor classification and a multistage waypoint ensemble trained with iterative pseudo-labeling. LSTM and convolutional attention models fed convolutional stacking and LightGBM models with temporal and relative-position features, followed by weight optimization and Ridge regression. Repeated geometric postprocessing was central, combining grid snapping, path translation, sensor-based cost minimization, rotation correction, and hallway constraints. The floor model achieved reported 100% accuracy on both public and private data.

For CITE, the author combined log-transformed raw data, complementary dimensionality reductions, and selected gene features in a heterogeneous ensemble. Donor-grouped validation guided a three-layer stack whose reported CV score was 0.89677, with additional independent models included in the ensemble. The custom neural network replaced attention dot products with an MLP, alongside CNN, kernel ridge, and boosting models. For Multiome, the pipeline reduced inputs and normalized targets with truncated SVD, then combined neural and boosting predictions.

solution_summary: The solution represents wells as multichannel TVT-by-MD images and ensembles CNNs with UNet-style decoders. Its central investment was realistic synthetic geology, used for roughly 25 epochs of pretraining before brief fine-tuning on real wells. Auxiliary trajectory reconstruction, sibling-well type-log correction, and larger-canvas reinference improve accuracy and coverage. Cross-validation was more informative than the noisy public scores, although the late MaxViT-base variant encountered a submission-time construction error.

The author focused on limiting overfitting on a small dataset through simple modeling and substantial feature engineering. The final approach used XGBoost with parameters selected through RandomizedSearchCV. Validation used stratified cross-validation, and the reported public score was 0.18.

The main model combined WaveNet blocks, squeeze-and-excitation modules, dense concatenations, and a bidirectional LSTM in PyTorch. Inputs used drift-cleaned, Kalman-filtered, standardized signals together with random-forest probabilities, squared signal, and selected lags. GroupKFold with groups of 4,000 and a predicted test class-10 count check guided experiments and submission selection. Training coordinated macro-F1 checkpointing with cross-entropy loss, learning-rate reductions, and early stopping. The main model achieved 0.94365 local CV and 0.94513 private leaderboard score, while a three-submission vote deteriorated on private evaluation.

solution_title: Solver, ChatGPT 5.5, and Fable Traces for Cryptarithm
solution_summary: The authors replaced cryptarithm examples in an existing synthetic SFT corpus with programmatically generated search traces and teacher-model reasoning. They trained rank-32 LoRA adapters for Nemotron-3-Nano-30B and compared several trace formats, including forward reasoning and standardized teacher explanations. Search improvements expanded candidate coverage, but voting sometimes selected an incorrect answer even when the correct one was available. The authors report that the model failed to learn the procedure and that cryptarithm accuracy did not improve.

The solution combined three EfficientNet-B0 tile models with an EfficientNet-B4 model trained on resized whole images. HSV-based filtering selected useful tissue tiles, which were assembled into patch images; patch construction and binary cross-entropy were reported as the biggest improvements. Training used AdamW, OneCycle scheduling, gradient accumulation, and mixed precision. A weighted ensemble with patch-mode test-time augmentation achieved a private leaderboard score of 0.920, with labels obtained by counting sigmoid outputs above 0.5.

solution_summary: The solution adapted a public notebook into a traceback-driven code repair pipeline. Regex parsing mapped traceback paths and locations to repository code, with LLM-based search retained as a fallback. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B generated eight repair candidates per issue using git conflict marker edits, which were applied to a temporary repository to produce valid diffs. The first valid patch was selected without running tests, although the author reports that a broken submission forced a simpler final submission.

solution_title: Rank 60 solution: a first-time RL practitioner’s experience
solution_summary: The solution used self-play reinforcement learning for its four-player arm and behavior cloning for its final two-player arm. An autoregressive action head explicitly modeled launch sequences and stopping, producing cleaner decisions at some throughput cost. Local round-robin evaluation against strong prior bots and exploiters guided promotion, while policy visualization exposed action-space bugs. Exploiter training helped disrupt passive four-player self-play behavior and improved first-place rate by roughly 15–17 points in local tests.

solution_summary: The author reports using an ensemble of three different models and applying cross-validation as much as possible. The solution ensembled YOLO-V4 detectors trained on individual radiologists and on merged annotations from all radiologists. A specialized detector trained on selected annotators and two disease classes supplied replacement predictions for aortic enlargement. Classifier-based post-processing substantially improved the detector ensemble. The final reported scores were 0.348 public and 0.305 private.

The author formulated wellbore prediction as two-dimensional alignment using a ConvNeXt-backed U-Net and probability-map losses. Engineered gamma-ray features, calibrated typewell signals, particle-filter outputs and spatial-neighbor estimates supplied complementary information. Strong geological and signal augmentations improved robustness, while spatial-neighbor features were retained based on local validation despite worse public results. A reliability-dependent weighted ensemble achieved CV RMSE 4.627 and private RMSE 5.639.

solution_title: 42nd place submission | jumped 880 places = lucky seed?
solution_summary: The solution primarily used BERTweet, following the author's previously shared notebook and retaining seed 777. It substituted RoBERTa predictions whenever BERTweet encountered an unknown token. BERTweet was preferred because its performance varied less across folds, although both models had similar CV and public scores. The substitution increased the reported private score from 0.718 to 0.719, with final public score 0.712 and CV 0.709.

The team's best single model was RoBERTa-Large with an attention head, improved through layer-wise learning rate decay and layer reinitialization. It used five folds and five training epochs with a maximum sequence length of 256, achieving scores of 0.467 on the public leaderboard and 0.468 on the private leaderboard. The final solution combined two shared notebook models with their own best model using weights of 0.35, 0.35, and 0.30. This ensemble achieved 0.457 on both leaderboards.

The author's contribution combined a basic tabular approach with features extracted from fMRI component maps. Predicting four domain targets from out-of-fold age predictions and then modeling their residuals with FNC and loading features improved the leaderboard score by 0.0002. Regional fMRI summary statistics fed into LightGBM were useful in blends for domain2_var2. Out-of-fold imputation improved cross-validation without improving the leaderboard, while t-SNE and UMAP exploration did not produce a clear benefit.

solution_title: [2nd Efficiency Solution] In a few words
solution_summary: The author used DAIGT V2 and modified essays with a fixed topic prefix, separator tokens, and a padding suffix. A classification ensemble with weights of 0.08, 0.46, and 0.46 was combined with a regression model using 28 engineered features. The final predictions weighted the classification ensemble at 0.4 and the regressor at 0.6, achieving a reported public leaderboard score of 0.917. Transformers, ridge methods, alternative vectorizations, and heavier ensembles failed to improve the result despite some strong validation scores.

The solution ensembles five 3D U-Nets with pretrained ResNet3D encoders and pixel-shuffle decoders. Encoder regularization, auxiliary segmentation heads, EMA, and heavy augmentation improve generalization. Training first fits the decoder on simulated data with the encoder frozen, then fine-tunes all parameters on competition data. Overlapping inference with central-patch predictions improves scores, and final postprocessing corrections for mask and coordinate errors produced the author's best submissions.

The solution used coordinate-independent crystal geometry features with XGBoost. It constructed 80 radial-distribution features and 80 angular-distribution features for nearby atoms. Predicted formation energy became an additional input for band-gap prediction, producing a local CV score of 0.049 and public score of 0.0515. Direct density functional theory calculations were insufficiently accurate under the available CPU budget.

solution_title: Andrew Newell and Lewis Griffin on winning the ICDAR 2011 Competition
solution_summary: The method represented handwriting with multiscale oriented Basic Image Feature column histograms. Root-normalized histograms were expressed as deviations from the training mean and classified with Euclidean nearest neighbours. Test-set distance analysis and assignment constraints helped handle potentially unknown authors. A final reassignment using an unused author's second-nearest match eliminated the public error, while both later entries achieved zero final error.

The author's best submission came from a deliberately simple baseline. It used regression to impute missing training values and Optuna to optimize hyperparameters before prediction. The author accidentally omitted imputation on the test set and emphasized the risks of overfitting the public leaderboard.

The team obtained public test labels through leaderboard probing and incorporated them into training. Most models used YOLO or Faster R-CNN detections to create crops, followed by bagged image classifiers with ResNet50 and VGG16 backbones. Hill climbing selected an ensemble using two-fold validation split between the public training and test sets. The ensemble also included a custom model and a U-Net-based model, while only one model used the additional training data.

The final submission used separate default-parameter Ridge regression models for each target pair, with logarithmic returns as the only feature. Additional features and more complex nonlinear or time-series approaches did not consistently improve the baseline. Rolling backtests showed strong variation across market regimes, and combining Ridge with mean predictions reduced its upside without compensating for its lows. An unintended one-day lag in inference features worsened retrospective performance.

solution_summary: The author's best-performing agent came from a few modifications to the example agent. They also implemented Q-learning, but that agent performed poorly and may have contained bugs. A strategy-based attempt exposed a delayed-reward problem because kore totals change only after ships return. DQN and strategy-based reinforcement learning were suggested as directions for further work.

The solution ensembled U-Nets with squeeze-and-excitation blocks and several encoder families on ash-color images. Progressive training increased image resolution, followed by a final stage that removed flip and transpose augmentations while retaining affine or perspective transforms. This staged augmentation strategy improved validation from 0.6756 to 0.6838. Training used Dice loss and the provided train/validation split, with no test-time augmentation.

solution_title: Part of 3rd Place Sol: Multi-label Classifier-based PP

This improved the public score to 0.348, but its private score of 0.305 matched the simpler class14-only multiplication approach.

solution_title: Silver medal in three days of work
solution_summary: The solution used tabular features and a simple neural network trained with pinball loss at quantiles 0.2, 0.5, and 0.8. Patient-grouped three-fold validation used only the last three measurements per patient and initial Percent values to better match test conditions. Features included initial FVC and Percent, a sex–smoking-status interaction, and group statistics, with selection driven by validation performance. Image features, linear regression, LightGBM, and ensembles of those alternatives did not improve the results.

solution_title: 33th solution : Crazy 10 days sprint with 2D pipeline
solution_summary: The solution uses EfficientNet models on images assembled from mel spectrograms, Q transforms, and supplied long-duration spectrograms. Models trained on high-vote examples generate pseudo-labels for low-vote data, which are sampled to match the original target distribution. solution_summary: The solution averaged separate IMU-only and full-sensor models, combining transformers, GRUs, and a squeezeformer for IMU inputs and GRUs for full inputs. An initial 1D convolution and rolling statistical features improved cross-validation performance. Linear interpolation and median imputation handled missing time-of-flight data, while EMA and mixup improved generalization. The ensemble included both early-stopped and final models, and orientation auxiliary loss was rejected because it hurt leaderboard performance.

The pipeline began with 1D U-Net CNNs for event detection and sleep/awake classification, followed by peak detection. A second-stage LightGBM model rescored candidates using daily event constraints and longer-term context. A third stage shifted base event predictions to generate additional candidates and scored them with LightGBM. Averaging across folds and seeds plus a WBF-like ensemble of two CNN models raised the reported CV score from 0.826 to 0.844.

solution_title: 5th place solution: combining GraphNet and Transformer with LSTM meta-model
solution_summary: The solution combined a Transformer with a modified GraphNet through a bidirectional LSTM that selected which prediction to use for each event. The Transformer classified azimuth and zenith into 256 bins with neighborhood-aware, circular label smoothing. GraphNet benefited from wider latent features for graph construction, LayerNorm, increased model size, and Cartesian direction regression. Initializing the selector's hidden states with both models' embeddings produced a final score of 0.974.

solution_title: 1st place solution: A brief overview of my experience
solution_summary: The author solved a collection of AI security puzzles through brute-force search, manual input manipulation, model inspection, and adversarial examples. Several challenges used specialized approaches, including locally linear embeddings to reveal characters and logistic regression to identify humans. Other solutions exploited leaked information, altered image or video inputs, and reconstructed a malicious string through detector queries. The strategy emphasized quickly automating searches to free time for other puzzles, while Crop_2 remained unsolved.

The solution averaged EfficientNet U-Net and SegFormer predictions across multiple folds. Concatenating the test fragments and rotating them before inference produced a large early improvement, while adding IR images improved both CV and leaderboard scores by about 0.01. Predictions were converted to image-wide percentile ranks before thresholding at 0.95 or 0.96. The two final submissions achieved private scores of 0.661339 and 0.654812.

solution_title: Good Ineffective - 6th top solution: simple and effective
solution_summary: The solution represented each essay as a single sequence of discourse elements, prefixing each element with its type and separating elements with [SEP]. DeBERTa models predicted element labels with multiple dropout in the output layer. Pseudo-labeled data from the previous Feedback competition and adversarial weight perturbation improved performance. A weighted ensemble of five-fold models achieved a reported public score of 0.560.

The selected submission ensembled 15 U-Nets with pretrained ir-CSN 3D encoders, mean pooling and lightweight 2D decoders. It combined 224, 384 and 576 pixel patches, using three overlapping 24-slice volumes as input channels to preserve pretrained first-layer weights. Training included mixed-sample augmentation, BCE and hard Dice losses, AdamW and a one-cycle schedule, while inference used overlapping crops and a fixed 0.5 threshold without TTA. The selected ensemble scored 0.763384 publicly and 0.681137 privately; an unselected larger ensemble reached 0.687873 privately.

solution_title: 110th Solution : My Original GRU Model & Tuned Unet2D Model
solution_summary: The author first built a simple bidirectional GRU using full-resolution week-long sequences and sensor differences and rolling statistics. This model used clipped ENMO values and Gaussian-smoothed targets whose sigma decreased each epoch, reaching public/private scores of 0.709/0.758. The stronger submission tuned a public notebook through eight feature configurations combining sensor values, cyclic hour features, differences, absolute differences, and squared terms. An ensemble of 25 models achieved public/private scores of 0.750/0.775.

solution_title: Smile!  Alexander D'yakonov on placing third in the Photo Quality Prediction competition
solution_summary: The solution combined random forests and weighted nearest neighbors using a nonlinear weighted combination whose coefficients were tuned by gradient descent. Additional features included image aspect ratio, pixel area, and a merged word list from album and photo metadata. Word-list feature engineering was less effective than expected, and no external information was used. An accidental reduction from six algorithms to three in the final ensemble worsened performance.

The author used a stack containing two CatBoost models, two XGBoost models, two neural networks, and one LightGBM model. Ridge was used for weighted averaging. Because the dataset size made five-fold hyperparameter optimization difficult, the author relied on public notebook hyperparameters. The approach achieved a public score of 0.89740 and a private score of 0.89703.

solution_title: Another first place solution and shake up explanation
solution_summary: The author's best private-leaderboard submission used quantile regression trained for 25 epochs. These models used baseline Percent rather than the varying Percent feature. The author attributed the leaderboard shakeup to overfitting from 800-epoch training and nonlinear curves produced when using Percent. Out-of-fold FVC curves were plotted to inspect the predictions.

solution_title: 48th Place Solution: [BYU - Locating Bacterial Flagellar Motors 2025]
solution_summary: The author adapted a shared submission notebook using a publicly available pretrained MHAFYOLO model. The main change clustered detections across nearby 3D coordinates and retained the highest-confidence detection only when a cluster covered at least three Z slices. The submitted settings used a confidence threshold of 0.7, a clustering threshold parameter of 0.7, image size 1024, and at most one detection per tomogram. This emphasized spatial consistency across slices to remove redundant or unsupported detections.

The pipeline predicts TVT relative to the last known value using physics alignment candidates, spatial geological priors, and 374 features feeding a LightGBM/CatBoost stack with a linear meta-ensemble. Blending the stack with a particle-filter track provided the largest learnable improvement, while well-bootstrap tests controlled which smoothing and trajectory corrections were retained. Leakage-free validation achieved 9.27 ± 0.46 ft RMSE, down from 10.85 ft for the raw meta-ensemble. At inference, a separate guarded overlap-recovery step interpolates training TVT onto physically matching test wells when their known prefixes validate the match.

solution_title: Feature selection, Random Forest, and things I should have done better
solution_summary: The author combined chemically motivated polymer features with filtered RDKit descriptors to predict five properties. Features captured mass relative to atom count, hydrogen bonding, branching, backbone structure, and bond flexibility. The author reports that a Bayesian-tuned random forest performed best, with a loss of 0.03218, although the listed parameters leave the precise estimator unclear. More complex models performed poorly despite augmentation, and the submission preceded the supplemental dataset.

The team fully fine-tuned DeepSeekMath-Base 7B in two stages: broad mathematical chain-of-thought training followed by synthetic tool-integrated reasoning with Python execution feedback. Inference generated 48 reasoning candidates with up to four execution rounds, pruned malformed traces, and selected answers by majority vote. Eight-bit GPTQ quantization enabled faster inference within the T4 memory budget, while four internal validation sets guided model selection and reduced dependence on public scores. KTO improved an earlier model but was not applied to the final model; several larger-model, reinforcement-learning, compilation, and merging experiments were discarded.
compute: Training: one node with 8 x H100 GPUs, 10 hours per model; inference: 2 x T4 GPUs.

solution_summary: The final solution combined XGBoost, random forests, nearest neighbors, and kernel density estimation. The KDE component estimated independent densities for spatial, accuracy, and temporal properties within spatial grids. Combining two approaches to temporal activity improved predictions, and ensembling shifted grids reduced boundary effects. The resulting KDE ensemble scored approximately 0.604 on the public leaderboard.

The pipeline first used five-fold EfficientDet B3 models to pseudo-label the ten available test images and capture their source characteristics. Larger EfficientDet models were trained in stages with EMA, cosine annealing, and extensive augmentation, followed by multiscale and flip inference. The final ensemble fused EfficientDet B5, B4, and pseudo-label-trained B5 detections using weighted boxes fusion, reaching a public score of 0.7752. The author identified unsuccessful threshold tuning and insufficient augmentation robustness as weaknesses.

The solution combined five independent well-trajectory predictors spanning geometric anchors, particle filters, neural networks, and dynamic programming. A convex blend formed the baseline trajectory, and an optimal-transport stack selected local consensus paths using horizontal and typewell gamma-ray agreement. Bounded corrections, decoder uncertainty, and Gaussian smoothing controlled deviations from that baseline. The final ensemble achieved CV 5.6, with stacking improvements persisting across held-out wells and bootstrap samples.

solution_title: Rank72 - Simple ensemble with DINO-EVA backbones
solution_summary: The solution primarily used pretrained DINOv3 Huge models with shared backbones processing separate image strips, followed by feature concatenation and SwiGLU regression heads. State-stratified, month-grouped validation gave the most useful correspondence with leaderboard results. Weighted Smooth L1 loss, staged backbone unfreezing, full-data refits over multiple seeds and test-time augmentation formed the training and inference pipeline. Models with different target formulations and architectures were blended, reaching an ensemble CV score of 0.81518447 with positive-weight hill climbing. Several individual models ultimately exceeded the chosen submission, and post-processing scalers did not help the preferred submission.
