solution_title: #7 Private #3 Public approach| Simple ensemble with post-processing
solution_summary: The solution combined LightGBM, CatBoost, random forest, and gradient boosting models trained on varied feature subsets. Original data supplemented training folds, while validation and out-of-fold predictions used competition data. Least absolute deviation regression blended these models with public notebook predictions, followed by small leaderboard-driven weight adjustments. Rounding predictions to nearby training target values improved results, although the author suspected public leaderboard tuning hurt generalization.

The team reconstructed weighted least-squares GNSS baselines and blended two new trajectories with the supplied baseline. They identified difficult geographic areas from training errors and applied area-specific trajectory corrections, including snapping to a grid. LightGBM predicted stopping intervals for position averaging and supported IMU-based relative position correction downtown. The pipeline also incorporated outlier correction, Kalman smoothing, phone averaging, and device removal.

The author announces a website showcasing generated dog images inspired by similar face and cat websites. They invite competition participants to contribute generated images and code, with attribution to each model and author. The post describes a community showcase rather than the author's competition solution.

The solution first localized anatomical keypoints with separate heatmap models for three MRI series types, then classified level-wise regions around those coordinates. The classifiers combined 2.5D feature extractors with GRU heads and used both condition-specific and joint-condition outputs. Coordinate-guided slice selection, intensity normalization, and augmentation supported both stages. Final predictions averaged six classifier configurations, each ensembled across five folds.

The final submission ensembled four RoBERTa-Large comparison models without external data. Two models encoded excerpts separately and used an ESIM-like interaction module, while two encoded paired excerpts jointly. Regression on target differences and binary comparison classification supplied model diversity, and standard-error augmentation improved classification CV. Joint encoding achieved better CV scores but required substantially more inference work; the four reported CV scores ranged from 0.47296 to 0.47878.
compute: Z4 Workstation with dual RTX6000 GPUs and a ZBook with RTX5000 GPU; 24GB VRAM mentioned.

solution_summary: The author's solution relied heavily on neural networks to extract features. Manual feature engineering was deliberately omitted in pursuit of a pure deep-learning approach. In retrospect, the author believed additional engineered features could have helped. The post links to code and a more detailed explanation but supplies no architecture or training details.

The architecture combined local 1D convolutions, graph-based connections across sequence positions, and bidirectional recurrent layers. Graph convolutions used both pairing connections and base-pair probability inputs to transmit remote information. Convolutional blocks alternated with GRU layers, with spatial dropout providing regularization. The author reported roughly two to three times the speed of another shared architecture and released a simplified notebook with some blending and optimizations removed.

solution_title: 302th place solution - Ensemble of three models
solution_summary: The solution ensembled three ImageNet-initialized U-Nets with SE-ResNeXt50_32x4d backbones: one operating at 1024×1024 and two at 512×512. The large model received most of the ensemble weight, followed by channel-weighted adjustment and a percentile-based binary threshold. Training used augmented images, Dice loss, a kidney-based validation split, and a OneCycleLR schedule over 30 epochs. The selected ensemble scored 0.86 publicly and 0.458 privately, with threshold sensitivity identified as a possible contributor to the discrepancy.

The solution combined transit curve fitting with binning in time and wavelength. A baseline fit supplied parameters for 13 wavelength-specific fits, which were interpolated to produce 283 predictions. LightGBM models corrected the fitted estimates and estimated uncertainty using a nested data split. Additional curve fits from batman provided features for the correction model.

The final submission blended a public notebook model, standard TabM, oversampled TabM, and sample-weighted XGBoost. TabM contributed valuable diversity despite weaker standalone validation performance, while XGBoost received greater ensemble weight. XGBoost used target means, counts, categorical frequencies, missing-value filling, and a log1p target transformation. CatBoost was excluded because prediction-distribution diagnostics showed substantial redundancy with XGBoost.
compute: All models trained on GPU; hardware and runtime unspecified.

solution_summary: The solution fine-tuned language models on training comments and labeled examples supplied in the test data, using the public leaderboard for validation. Deduplication without subreddit, extra weighting of test examples, and loss restricted to Yes/No tokens improved training. Inference aggregated probabilities across answer variants, followed by per-rule rank normalization and a weighted six-model ensemble. The final ensemble scored 0.9344 publicly and 0.9293 privately.
compute: Reports fitting a 14B model within 16GB GPU memory using Unsloth; GPU model and runtime unspecified.

solution_summary: The solution used separate inference paths for TMA images and whole-slide images, sharing a fine-tuned MaxViT subtype classifier. Supplemental tumor masks guided tile extraction and training/validation selection. Whole-slide thumbnails first passed through a tumor classifier, after which selected regions were classified by subtype and aggregated with majority voting. StainNet did not improve over simple normalization.

The solution uses ImageNet-pretrained SE-ResNeXt and SENet models with five-fold iterative stratification. Augmentation, several label-smoothing variants, and a modified focal loss improved validation, particularly when the loss accommodated noisy and co-occurring labels. A large ensemble generated out-of-fold predictions to remove roughly 5% of training samples and pseudo-label about 5,000 public images. The final SE-ResNeXt101 and SENet154 models were retrained on the cleaned and expanded dataset and used horizontal-flip inference.

solution_title: Mapping Matter with Matlab: Sergey Yurgenson on finishing second in Mapping Dark Matter
solution_summary: The author centered galaxy and star images and computed principal components separately for their image stacks. Principal-component amplitudes served as compact inputs to neural networks, while some components also helped refine object centers. Network configuration and input dimensionality were tuned experimentally, and multiple networks were combined for final submissions. An earlier approach using modified quadruple moments and fitting produced unsatisfactory results.

The team combined two separate pipelines in a weighted ensemble, mixing neural networks trained with pairwise ranking loss and tree or linear models. Both pipelines used race-based sample weights, engineered categorical and cyclic year features, and survival target transformations. One pipeline used stratified cross-validation, while the other trained on the entire training set without cross-validation. Predictions were scaled before blending, and improvements in cross-validation often conflicted with leaderboard results.

The solution classified square animal crops from MegaDetector using three ImageNet-pretrained CNNs and a geographic and seasonal prior. Location-grouped validation guided ensemble weights, while motion detection removed static false detections. Sequence predictions used majority species voting and the maximum number of valid detections in a frame. A late experiment combining full-image and crop predictions improved both public and private scores.

solution_title: My brief overview of my solution
solution_summary: The solution combines image classifiers trained at several input resolutions, including a dilated ResNet-34. Dark-channel-prior haze removal was especially useful across multiple labels. Predictions were combined using separate ridge regressions for all 17 labels and voting, with the best submission voting across nine models. Simulated public/private splits showed meaningful score variation, motivating model selection based on cross-validation and stable ensembles.

The solution used a cascade of three text normalization layers. A contextual statistical lookup handled sufficiently confident transformations, while regular expressions processed structured formats such as dates, numbers, and URLs. Several LightGBM models resolved ambiguous alternatives left by the first two layers. Limited development time led to missed cases and simplistic local validation, with some decisions based on a public leaderboard covering only 1% of the data.

solution_title: 2nd Place and 2nd Place Solution to Kaggle Landmark Recognition and Retrieval Competition 2019
solution_summary: The post announces that the authors have released their solution on arXiv. It provides links to the paper and source code. It also thanks the organizers for the challenge.

solution_title: PUBLIC LB 24th SOLUTION by team Electrium Z
solution_summary: The team combined weather interpolation, extensive temporal and weather features, and targeted outlier removal with a diverse collection of models. They trained both joint models with meter downsampling and separate models for each meter, finding three-fold validation more useful for leaderboard performance than larger fold counts. Their main ensemble used Bayesian optimization to learn nonnegative weights separately for each meter against public leaked labels, which also replaced predictions at the leaked sites. They prepared an alternative average of strong submissions, giving extra weight to submissions with better out-of-fold performance on sites outside the leak.

The solution combined 12 logistic regression models using different subsets and averaging periods of weather variables. Species, geographic blocks, and a trap-level duplicate-row leakage feature supplemented the weather features. Limiting each model's weather variables reduced overfitting, and the ensemble scored 0.811 privately and 0.823 publicly. Fitting year-specific linear weights using the public test set improved these scores to 0.833 and 0.842.

The solution combined predictions from Mistral 7B variants and Gemma-7b-1.1-it trained on different datasets. Different opening verbs encouraged prediction diversity, and outputs were concatenated into a single recovered prompt. Appending a specially constructed suffix exploited sentence-embedding behavior associated with the token lucrarea, reportedly adding up to 0.05 to the score. Individual models stayed below 0.65, while the final diverse predictions and suffix reached about 0.71.

The solution used Dlib metric learning with a ResNet variant producing 128-dimensional embeddings from grayscale whale images. Model-derived heatmaps guided fluke cropping and PCA alignment, with training first on original images and then on crops. Mirrored whales became separate classes, playground competition data expanded training, and semi-automatic cleaning reduced label noise. Predictions ranked enrollment images by Euclidean embedding distance with a threshold for new whales, and the final ensemble concatenated embeddings from nine ResNet models. The author reported a best single-model score of 0.938, a final public score of 0.953, and a private score of 0.948.

The solution blended two-, three-, and four-hidden-layer neural networks with TabNet and DeepInsight models. Denoising-autoencoder features were concatenated with original inputs, while rank Gaussian transformation, statistical features, TabNet-specific PCA, and smoothing loss also helped. Rare-target weighted-loss models were blended with ordinary-loss models because weighting improved validation but did not improve the public score. The final submission scored 0.01608 privately and 0.01820 publicly, with a CV score of 0.01550 excluding control vehicles.

solution_title: [6th private - 3rd public] Summary of our solution
solution_summary: The solution blended neural and XGBoost models for both tasks using five-fold validation stratified by day, donor, and cell type. Feature filtering, dimensionality reduction, and denoising autoencoders supplied diverse inputs, while prediction features and pseudolabeling added smaller gains. CITE models were trained on both original and raw-count data, with the latter improving performance by about 0.001. Output standardization for CITE and restoring zero-valued targets for multiome further improved predictions.
compute: Team reported working 6 hours/day throughout the competition.

solution_title: Kaggle Competition Experience(Team: Learning at snail pace) | Rank 1473
solution_summary: The final model was EfficientNet B4 trained for 30 epochs with a step learning-rate schedule and regularisation. It achieved a public score of 0.9749 after experiments with several EfficientNet sizes, DenseNet models, and augmentations. Restarting training from existing model weights consistently worsened performance for the author. Attempts to ensemble with DenseNet also failed to improve results.

solution_summary: The solution mixed two unlearning procedures, choosing one procedure for each model. One spatially transposed convolution weights before retraining on retained examples for three epochs, reusing useful pretrained features. The other identified forget-set examples likely to be misclassified after retraining and fine-tuned with deliberately incorrect pseudo-labels. The reported mixture of 246 transposed-weight models and 266 pseudo-label models scored 0.0785184178.

solution_title: 12th place - Disjunctions of bigrams, trigrams only
solution_summary: The solution extracted meaningful bigram and trigram noun phrases and assembled patent search queries with a greedy weighted set cover algorithm. An Aho-Corasick automaton produced phrase counts and ranks, while query weights interpolated rank-based and uniform relevance assumptions. Hyphens joined phrase words to reduce token usage, and bitsets accelerated candidate selection. Phrase-only queries limited coverage and description searches were expensive; Bayesian tuning was also hindered by noisy evaluations and weak validation indexes.
compute: Some individual bigram/trigram description searches took more than 20 seconds.

solution_title: Third place solution: mode ensemble of 6 public notebooks.
solution_summary: The author combined submissions from six public notebooks using a weighted mode. The repeated symbolic regression submission was included twice to give it double weight. Ordinary mode produced the same results, suggesting that the additional class weighting was unnecessary. The ensemble performed well on both public and private leaderboards.

solution_title: 5th place partial solution - NN part (Github Updated)
solution_summary: The post describes a neural network component that pairs each raw feature with its frequency count from training and cleaned test data. Shared dense layers learn representations within these pairs, which worked better than learning interactions across all raw features. On-the-fly augmentation independently resamples feature pairs within each class while preserving each raw/count association. This improved the reported private leaderboard score from 0.92188 to 0.92376, although the team subsequently refined the network further.

solution_title: Quick overview my solution: UNet + regression on masks
solution_summary: A U-Net predicted class-specific masks of fixed-size squares centered on sea lions from augmented image patches. Thresholded mask sums and blob counts became features for separate per-class count regressors combining Extra Trees and XGBoost. Test images were downscaled by a factor of two, and the final predictions averaged models favored by either local validation or the leaderboard. The author reported substantial disagreement between local validation and leaderboard scores and avoided per-class leaderboard tuning.
compute: Single 1070; 12–24 hours training, 12 hours prediction, plus about 3 hours training and running count prediction.

solution_summary: The team averaged RoBERTa-Large, XLNet, and BERT-base-uncased models trained with five folds each. Ranking and normalizing target values before MSE or MSE-plus-BCE training improved validation, while long inputs preserved titles and the beginnings and ends of body and answer text. Output clipping and host-based spelling heuristics provided additional gains. Unreliable CV and limited model diversity complicated selection, and several augmentation and domain-pretraining experiments did not help.

solution_summary: The solution combined protein sequence embeddings and taxon features with multi-output gradient boosting, logistic regression, and neural networks. Conditional-probability variants used the GO graph to extend predictions to terms absent from training and provided valuable ensemble diversity. A graph convolutional stacker combined base predictions with GO annotation features, while graph-based postprocessing improved consistency. Gradient boosting was the strongest base-model family, and electronic annotations worked better as predictive features than as direct labels.

solution_summary: The organ pipeline segmented 3D scans, cropped organs with the resulting masks, and classified the crops using 3D models. For extravasation, YOLOv8x produced slice-level bounding-box confidence and area sequences, which were summarized with simple statistical features. Logistic regression and balanced random forest probabilities were averaged, with stratified cross-validation used for evaluation. This approach improved log loss by 0.02 over the author's best statistical approach, while TTA added little quality at four times the inference cost.
compute: TTA increased inference time by 4 times.

solution_summary: The solution combined diverse transformer models trained with extensive iterative pseudo-labeling. Pseudo-labels came from small model blends, with different iteration counts, data proportions, and soft targets providing diversity. The ensemble mixed several backbones and output heads, with some models receiving masked-language-model pretraining or augmentation. Reliable token-to-character span conversion mattered, while ensemble CV correlated poorly with leaderboard results and fold-averaged pseudo-labels compromised CV.

The main submission averaged six models with three-seed averaging, using different sequence lengths to improve ensemble diversity. Knowledge distillation against out-of-fold predictions improved DeBERTa-v3-small CV by more than 0.014 and was included in both submission tracks. The efficiency submission used a distilled DeBERTa-v3-small with maximum length 384, trained on all competition data after four-fold evaluation, and ran in 16 minutes 42 seconds. Validation used multilabel stratification with binned word counts. XGBoost on embeddings, gradient unscaling, TorchScript, and dynamic quantization did not help.
compute: Efficiency submission inference: 16 minutes 42 seconds.

solution_title: 20th place solution: SED + CNN ensemble using onnx
solution_summary: The final submission ensembled five SED and simple CNN models using NFNet, EfficientNet and MobileNet backbones. Models consumed five-second mel spectrograms, with earlier BirdCLEF datasets used for longer-duration pretraining. Oversampling, secondary soft labels, background-noise nocall examples and audio augmentation were useful. ONNX inference and shared cached preprocessing accelerated the ensemble, while longer-context inference timed out.

The team generated synthetic velocity-to-seismic data with Stable Diffusion and trained a baseline using Bartley’s architecture with logarithmic min-max input normalization. An accelerated forward simulator enabled online augmentation and training with mixed training and test data, improving the reported score from 19.3 to 13.2. Test-only fine-tuning validated by seismic reconstruction error reduced it to 12.5. Direct gradient-based velocity optimization on StyleA/B, initialized from model outputs, produced a final score of 12.3.
compute: 5090 GPU; accelerated forward simulation reached about 120 samples/s.

solution_title: How I did it: finishing second from Bo Yang's perspective
solution_summary: The author's main predictors combined degree-weighted second-neighbor KNN with a complementary global graph-distance score. A genetic algorithm blended four KNN variants and two global-distance variants, producing approximately 0.935 on the test set in about seven minutes. A rule exploiting the test-set construction process raised the author's score to approximately 0.952. The team's final system fed a broad collection of predictors into a random forest and achieved approximately 0.970.
compute: 2.66 GHz CPU, single-threaded; each predictor about 1 minute, blending about 15 seconds, complete six-predictor submission about 7 minutes.

solution_title: An Analysis of Evaluation Predicates in a Tool-Using Agent Security Competition
solution_summary: The authors crafted prompt templates targeting sentinel-based exfiltration and email-based confused deputy scoring after inspecting the evaluation SDK. They varied destinations to obtain unique-call bonuses and forged analysis turns to improve compliance and throughput. Their selected exfiltration submission scored 102.42 public but zero private, while the selected email submission scored 13.385 public and 13.37 private. An unselected adaptive strategy-selection submission improved to 19.425 private.

The final solution extended a tabular LightGBM pipeline with patient-grouped numerical normalization and categorical occurrence counts. It used five-fold StratifiedGroupKFold validation and a limited Optuna search to reduce hyperparameter overfitting. Training and undersampling across five seeds supplied the final ensemble. Feature removal, image PCA features, RGB statistics, alternative imbalance treatments, and a second-stage probability-feature model did not provide useful improvements.

solution_title: 1st place - I think it was genetic programming
solution_summary: The author combined tree models and tabular neural networks, including tuned TabM models, Keras factorization machines, and TensorFlow embedding networks. Neural-network stacking became the preferred ensembling method, with 11 genetic-programming features contributing a small additional gain at the ensemble stage. CatBoost then refined a Keras ensemble through its baseline mechanism, improving public and private scores by about 0.00002. A final hill-climbing ensemble combined four previous ensembles, while many alternative networks and automatically generated models added little useful diversity.
compute: Neural-network ensembling took 1–2 hours for 40–50 models; Optuna ensemble searches took 4–10 hours; Lasso 10x10 repeated K-fold took about 2 minutes.

solution_summary: The author built a nested ensemble of seven XGBoost models and reported a private AUC of 0.828314. The component pipelines used Tomek links, edited nearest neighbors, undersampling, and one feature-elimination variant. XGBoost configurations used depths of four or five, 300–600 rounds, and learning rates around 0.0202. The final prediction averaged an ensemble of all seven models with an ensemble containing models one, three, and four.

The solution first classified temporal image sequences for contrail presence, then segmented only images whose classification probability exceeded 0.2. Segmentation used a weighted ensemble of five 2D U-Net models with different encoders and losses, with weights optimized on validation data. Human mask soft labels, pseudo-label pretraining on other time steps, geographic fold construction, and test-time augmentation contributed to the approach. Reported scores were 0.694 CV, 0.706 public, and 0.699 private.

The solution used a 2.5D pipeline combining segmentation and classification with U-Net models using Pyramid Vision Transformer V2 and MaxViT encoders. Rescaled CT volumes were sampled into 14 frames per epoch, with body and organ masks restricting the input to relevant regions. Pretraining on 2D masks improved convergence, and six classification heads were trained with metric-weighted cross-entropy. Transformers outperformed convolutional models, especially for extravasation, while the ensemble with scaling achieved a CV score of 0.3530 and an LB score of 0.39.

solution_title: 11th place solution: batch normalization and 2D post-filtering
solution_summary: The solution averaged pre-softmax heatmaps from 32 UNet models using a mixture of ResNet architectures and random seeds. Batch normalization improved training stability and consistency across inference windows, while a recall-oriented loss combined cross-entropy and Tversky terms. Connected components produced particle candidates, with a small 2D classifier filtering false positives for two protein classes. Large elongated ribosome components were split with K-means to recover multiple nearby particles, although limited training data made cross-validation comparisons inconclusive.
compute: 32 models, each trained for 2200 epochs; hardware and elapsed time unspecified.

solution_title: How to get a top 1% scoring solution with no ensembles
solution_summary: The author used a single EfficientNet-B3 image model, removing black borders while preserving image aspect ratios. Replacing cross-entropy with MSE and increasing resolution from 120×120 to 728×728 substantially improved validation performance. A small neural network combined information from the left and right eyes, producing public and private scores of 0.84613 and 0.83880. Balanced loading, class weights, and heavy augmentation did not improve results.

solution_title: 369th place solution YOLO part with PB0.840 notebook
solution_summary: The solution used YOLOv8l and YOLO11l on resized tomogram slices, combining competition data with an external flagellar-motor dataset. Training improvements included broader target-slice coverage, flip augmentation, larger images and batches, and checkpoint selection by distribution focal loss. Slice detections from multiple models were grouped with depth-first search and averaged to obtain motor coordinates. Multiprocessing, FP16 prediction, threaded image loading, and random slice skipping reduced inference time, with the eight-model ensemble taking about three hours and scoring 0.840 on the public leaderboard; the team's highest reported public score was 0.851.
compute: Four inference processes, two sharing each T4 GPU; about 1h40m for one model after acceleration and about 3 hours for the eight-model ensemble.

solution_title: 107th solution. Our first time to kaggle!
solution_summary: The solution combined three Swin-based prediction branches. The first incorporated metadata through linear layers and an SVR, while the second combined image-only Swin models with ridge regression. The third used FastAi test-time augmentation with a Swin Large 224 model. Final predictions weighted the three branches by 0.3, 0.3, and 0.4.

The final solution combined eleven GRU models: five using at most 128 pulses per event and six using at most 160. Increasing GRU depth and width helped, as did increasing the classification resolution to 64 bins with a 4096-unit output head. Converting data to TFRecords enabled efficient TPU training on almost all available data. Training used a batch size of 4096 and stepwise learning-rate reductions, while GNN combinations and alternative prediction targets were not retained.
compute: Kaggle TPU VM and Colab Pro TPUs; 8–12 epochs per 12-hour Colab Pro session, depending on model and data size.

solution_title: A simple approach based on baseline notebooks (6th place solution)
solution_summary: The solution adapted the baseline pipeline by stacking three neighboring grayscale frames as input channels to EfficientNet models. High-resolution inputs, four-class binary cross-entropy, augmentation, and checkpoint averaging strengthened the classifiers. Final submissions used three-model ensembles with horizontal-flip augmentation, including a variant combining temporal strides of one, two, and three. Inference on alternate frames with linear interpolation and image prefetching helped meet runtime constraints.

solution_title: Santa 2025 Competition Silver 126th Solution: Hybrid Optimization Pipeline
solution_summary: The solution combined SAGA parameter optimization with Spyrrow strip packing and geometric refinement. Genetic search followed by denser local parameter searches handled broader exploration, while repeated strip-packing runs targeted small groups. Rotation, inward compression, local perturbations, and ring rearrangement tightened layouts, with conflict-based repair removing overlaps. Only group-level score improvements were merged, and historical best layouts provided recovery baselines.

solution_title: Easter egg(whats my ip)+ my rabbit holes [9 solves]
solution_summary: The author described manual approaches to several language-model capture-the-flag challenges. Semantle was solved by iteratively exploring semantic associations, while flag extraction used variations of a prompt asking for characters from the model's first sentence. Counting 2 was solved through manual brute force. Attempts involving DNS records and address redirection failed, and their significance remained unresolved.

solution_title: 39th solution utilizing Pr(is_test|X) by adversarial validation
solution_summary: The solution combined a conservative prediction built around adversarial validation with an aggressive ensemble built through cross-validation and rank averaging. Adding t-SNE features enabled a train-versus-test classifier to reach 0.89 ROC-AUC despite original features failing to separate the datasets. Its test-membership probabilities guided validation splits, model and feature selection, sample weights, and per-example blending weights. Semi-supervised learning helped in validation but was not used to generate test predictions.

The solution used the provided baseline helmet boxes without training a custom detector. It estimated camera position and rotation by matching projected tracking coordinates to detection point clouds and refining the alignment with an ICP-like procedure. Sensor-based tracking included removal of unmatched detections and isolation of the main player cluster. Bounding-box IoU tracking used a threshold of 0.35.

Separate LightGBM models predicted production and consumption using four target formulations involving lagged targets, daily averages, and baseline predictions. Simple consumption and generation baseline models were retrained daily, while the LightGBM models remained fixed. The final weighted blend combined target variants, ten seeds, and two hyperparameter settings for 160 models. The author considered this large ensemble and frequent baseline retraining less promising in hindsight than allocating time to LightGBM retraining.

The solution used B5, B6, and B7 encoders with global average pooling, batch normalization, multi-sample dropout, and separate ArcFace heads for individuals and species. Training used four body and fin crop datasets, frozen batch normalization, and Lookahead with Adam. After 40 initial epochs, the models trained for another 10 epochs using 12,157 pseudo-labels selected through model agreement and a confidence-gap requirement. Inference used larger images than training.

The solution combined two fine-tuned Luke–RoBERTa models with three pretrained Detoxify models spanning previous Jigsaw datasets. It prioritized validation results, using leak-free grouped cross-validation for fine-tuning and a separate host-derived pair set for evaluating Detoxify outputs. Weighted combinations reduced multiple toxicity labels to scalar scores, followed by a rank-based final ensemble and randomized tie breaking. The final ensemble achieved a private score of 0.81282, while attempts to incorporate Ruddit and hate-speech data were unsuccessful.

solution_summary: The main model was a molecular message-passing network inspired by neural message passing papers. It updated both node representations and the adjacency matrix at each step. Skip connections enabled deeper networks, although going beyond seven layers brought no improvement. The solution used 4/5-fold cross-validation and some stacking, with implementation in TensorFlow 2.0.

The author combined two LightGBM models with a simple forecasting baseline based on the latest increment without decay. One LightGBM model used standard regression and the other used Poisson regression. Their predictions were averaged equally, then blended with the baseline using weights specified in the linked notebook. The post reports no evaluation scores.

solution_title: 37th Place Solution(And Let's talk about CV and private score)
solution_summary: The author ensembled five EfficientNet models spanning B0, B1, B2, B3, and B5. Images received circle cropping and Fast.ai transformations including flips, rotation, zoom, and lighting changes. Models were first trained with 2015 data using 2019 data for validation, then fine-tuned for 15 epochs on an 80:20 stratified split of the 2019 data. Validation-loss checkpoint selection and a fixed split guided comparisons without cross-validation or test-time augmentation. The ensemble achieved validation kappa of 0.932 and private kappa of 0.926.

The solution combined three U-Net variants with equal voting: background prediction followed by inversion, direct car segmentation, and separate top/bottom segmentation. The background model was strongest individually, scoring 0.9970 and handling difficult edges and wheel regions well. Contour-based antenna localization followed by Canny edge processing improved continuity, although its estimated score contribution was only about 0.00004. Training used Keras with a TensorFlow backend, primarily on four GTX 1080 Ti GPUs.

solution_title: 3rd place solution & become GM!! (updated with code)
solution_summary: The solution applies CT windowing and concatenates neighboring slices from the same series to exploit continuity in hemorrhage labels. It also trains models to predict multiple slice targets and combines slice context at the stacking stage. Additional components include external CQ500 data, black-border cropping, generalized mean pooling, and stage-two retraining. The final model scored 0.045 privately, while an unselected user-stacking-only model scored 0.043.

The pipeline combined screen-time accounting features, behavioral ratios, and smoothed out-of-fold target encodings with tree-based models. A 177-member multi-seed stack was combined with an anchor stream through percentile-rank averaging, with the selected submission weighting the stack at 1% and the anchor at 99%. Stratified validation guided selection, and adversarial validation produced an AUC of 0.5654. High-confidence pseudo-labeling provided a small experimental gain, while a CPU-limited TabNet trial was much weaker; the final private score was 0.97101.

solution_summary: The solution emphasized diversity across six language models, training methods, prompts, and classification label spaces. It combined 37-class models that separated answer correctness from misconception prediction with conventional 65-class models, using LoRA, QLoRA, and full fine-tuning. Validation grouped normalized student explanations to reduce duplicate leakage, while ensemble selection relied on public leaderboard improvements after CV correlation weakened. Weighted probability averaging, targeted answer-rewriting augmentation, and question-specific misconception masking completed the pipeline.

solution_title: (2nd) Weakly supervised semantic segmentation + Synthetic data
solution_summary: The solution treated biomass prediction as density estimation using DINOv3 ViT-Large and ViT-Huge backbones with convolutional or DPT heads. It combined original data with pseudo-labeled synthetic images and zero-biomass bare-soil edits, while strong cropping, erasing, Mixup, and CutMix improved generalization. Models predicted clover, dead, and green biomass using Smooth L1 loss, with target-specific checkpoints addressing different convergence times. An ensemble with state-dependent scaling, WA dead-biomass suppression, and clipping achieved a 0.67558 private score, and FP16 with two T4 processes reduced inference to 27 minutes.

solution_title: [20th] A simple solution, attempts and thinking.

An earlier semantic binary search strategy suffered from inconsistent answers across models. The two submitted agents scored 1006 and 934.

solution_title: LB 141th/PB 515th Sol.AttentionPooling/FE expansion(Left + Right + Diff + Prod)
solution_summary: The author improved public biomass regression notebooks using attention pooling with Mamba fusion and a separate FiLM-based left/right feature-fusion model. Attention pooling emphasized useful image patches, while FiLM combined left and right features with their differences and products. EMA with decay 0.999 improved leaderboard performance for the Mamba model despite weaker cross-validation results, and affine augmentations were particularly useful. A public Google SigLIP feature model was also used, and multiplying dry-clover predictions by 0.8 yielded an approximately 0.01 leaderboard boost.

solution_summary: The approach primarily transferred coordinates from known RNA structures through template-based modeling. It combined RibonanzaNet representation-based search and alignment with conventional blastn search and Smith–Waterman alignment. Chai-1 and Boltz-1 supplied structures when templates were unavailable or incomplete, and structural superposition patched missing regions. Ablations showed substantial contributions from both template search routes, while the dot-product representation variant achieved a private score of 0.56966.

solution_summary: The solution combined one ResNet34 trained at 512×512 with three SEResNeXt50 models trained at 320×320. Six-channel images were normalized using non-black pixels and passed through a learned convolution to match ImageNet input channels. ImageNet fine-tuning used moderate augmentation and SGD with Nesterov momentum and cosine annealing for 70 epochs. The single higher-resolution ResNet34 outperformed the SEResNeXt50 ensemble, but all four models were retained and plate-based leakage was used in postprocessing.

solution_title: AMO: Agentic Math Orchestrator for Olympiad Mathematics
solution_summary: AMO wrapped frozen GPT-OSS-120B in an inference orchestration system with parallel Python-assisted solvers, asynchronous verification, and evidence-weighted answer selection. Scout agents and adaptive budgeting routed problems between standard solving and a diversity-preserving beam search, while resolver agents addressed conflicting answers. Persistent tool kernels, additional optimization libraries, and trajectory monitoring reduced wasted work and exposed recurring reasoning failures. The baseline reached a public score of 45 and the fully orchestrated version reached 41; the selected final pipeline solved 39/50 local benchmark problems with nine minutes remaining.

solution_summary: The solution used seven-fold training on experimental data, percentile normalization, and voxel patches with hard particle masks. Training combined right-angle rotations, brightness and contrast changes, flips, and Dice loss, followed by an additional weighted fine-tuning epoch. Inference scanned overlapping volumes through the seven folds with different rotations. Cross-validation reached 0.808, while weighted fine-tuning changed the reported score pair from 0.741/0.733 to 0.740/0.735. Synthetic-data variants, alternative augmentations, pseudo-relabeling, and several postprocessing approaches did not work.

The solution used a play-level spatiotemporal Transformer to jointly predict player trajectories. Moving the input/output cut before and after the pass generated roughly 200,000 additional samples and was the most important augmentation. Basic relative geometry, velocities, temporal context, and a temporally weighted Huber loss supported training. The final prediction combined 48 models across week-based folds, random seeds, and different output horizons.

The solution fitted a differentiable physical transit model to calibrated, outlier-filtered, binned sensor data. It modeled wavelength-dependent planet radius, nonlinear limb darkening, transit timing, and polynomial drift using staged Levenberg-Marquardt optimization. Post-processing removed spectral artifacts, corrected high-impact-factor planets, and reduced radius variation with three-component PCA. Gradient boosting predicted scalar corrections to AIRS and FGS means and uncertainties, raising the reported scores to 0.581 public and 0.589 private.

The author reported public scores of 54.2–54.8 and private scores of 60.1–60.7 from identifying these groups.

solution_summary: A ship/no-ship classifier filtered images before segmentation to reduce false positives on empty scenes. solution_title: [33rd place] Key points of my solution
solution_summary: The approach constructs survival targets that distinguish observed events from censored patients at the same follow-up time. Observed-event targets use Kaplan-Meier survival probabilities, while censored targets use half that probability through a conditional event-time argument. Censored samples receive a uniform weight of 0.6 to reflect their uncertainty. Dynamic weighting based on follow-up time was tried but gave unsatisfactory results.

solution_title: RL training on a laptop (80th place)
solution_summary: A small entity Transformer was initialized by behavioral cloning from winning top-player replays, which supplied most of its strength. Separate 1v1 and free-for-all policies were then fine-tuned with self-play PPO, using a champion pool and teacher KL regularization to limit collapse. Inference sampled several actions and selected the value head's preferred action, switching to the 1v1 policy when only two players remained. A deterministic ship-count planner and opening launch guards supplemented the learned policy, with all training performed locally on an M-series MacBook.

solution_title: 4th Place Solution for the Child Mind Institute — Problematic Internet Use competition
solution_summary: The solution emphasized selective preprocessing and stacked CatBoost, LightGBM, and XGBoost models trained with five-fold validation. Important missing measurements were reconstructed using KNN, linear regression, logistic regression, or direct formulas, while less reliable columns often retained missing values. Related-variable interactions and sigmoid-weighted CGAS and SDS features supplemented the inputs, and optimized rounding thresholds converted direct SII predictions into classes. The ensemble achieved validation quadratic weighted kappa of 0.3912; TabNet and predicting PCIAT totals before mapping to SII were unsuccessful.

Removing predictions whose surrounding features repeated on an adjacent day improved public and private scores by approximately 0.007 and 0.016.

The final model combined molecular message passing with Transformer-style blocks and three forms of multi-head attention. Geometry features, separate bond and scalar-coupling message paths, and auxiliary predictions of coupling contributions captured molecular structure. An eight-fold submission scored -3.039 on the private leaderboard, and including an earlier MPNN ensemble improved the score by about 0.05. solution_summary: The author developed three prompt attacks intended to produce complementary disagreements among essay-scoring models. Each attack was prefixed with random common English words and used equally often in the final submission. Local tests covered three instruction-tuned models, two prompts and 20 essay topics per model, helping assess consistency despite weak public-leaderboard correlation. Smaller attack batches were explored only briefly.

The final system combined KNN regression, CLIP interrogator, and four fine-tuned image models with weights of 0.3, 0.1, and 0.6. Diverse prompt datasets were aggressively deduplicated and filtered before regenerating images with Stable Diffusion v2. Fine-tuning used token-length-based validation, partial layer freezing, horizontal flips, and MixUp. Normalizing model outputs before the fine-tuned ensemble improved its public score from 0.59314 to 0.59673.

The author filled missing values with zero and label-encoded categorical variables. Multiclass CatBoost models predicted the training-only Beta, Gamma, and Delta variables through a five-fold procedure, and these predictions became features for predicting Alpha. Alpha probabilities were converted to the binary target by summing B, D, and G for class 1 and using A for class 0. Validation used multilabel stratification based on the Greek variables.

solution_title: 627th Solution for CommonLit ESS competition- What doesn't kill you makes you stronger
solution_summary: The final approach returned to DeBERTa-v3-base combined with LightGBM after experiments with alternative transformer models. The author added SymSpell spell correction, separated preprocessing from the submission notebook, and used Optuna to tune LightGBM. MobileBERT performed poorly, and T5 could not run within the existing pipeline. The final changes achieved a public leaderboard score of 0.44 but did not transfer successfully to the private leaderboard.

The final solution blended an 80-model feedforward neural network ensemble, a LightGBM model, and an NLP regression model with weights of 0.6, 0.2, and 0.2. The neural networks predicted all genes from categorical compound and cell features, while LightGBM used gene expression from other cell types, donor counts, and LINCS data. Regularization, seed averaging, and cell-specific gene correlation aggregation improved robustness. The most consequential final adjustment shrank low-variance compound predictions toward zero and increased the magnitude of high-variance predictions, improving the regular ensemble's public/private scores from 0.560/0.743 to 0.558/0.733.

The solution ensembles EfficientNet sound event detection models trained with a custom soft AUC loss and semi-supervised learning. The loss supports soft labels and generalized better on the leaderboard than cross-entropy, despite weaker CV results. Together with semi-supervised learning, it raised a single EfficientNetV2-B0 model's leaderboard score from 0.850 to 0.901. The final ensemble contains 16 models diversified through spectrogram settings, audio sampling and augmentation.

solution_title: Private 20th | Public 25th Soluion - Simple model + Data augmentation
solution_summary: The solution ensembles vision-transformer models using either mean-pooled features or tile-level prediction heads, with FiLM conditioning. Tile-level heads and larger backbones were the most useful architectural choices, while random sliding tiling provided modest augmentation gains. Training first optimized FiLM and heads, then unfroze the backbone with a lower learning rate and a scaled Huber objective. Both selected ensembles scored 0.64 privately, below a single model that achieved 0.65.

The solution implemented Uber's multimodal trajectory-prediction approach with a raster backbone and a separate metadata branch. Training used temporally separated frames, capped agent sampling in crowded frames, and a multiple-trajectory loss, while validation used negative log likelihood. Cumulative sums converted network outputs into trajectories before transformation to world coordinates for loss calculation. Averaging seven checkpoint-based models improved the private score from 13.580 to 13.154 and the public score from 14.265 to 13.722.

solution_title: Anchor-Based Ensemble with Controlled Sidecar Corrections

Its primary branch fused prototype and sound-event-detection predictions, with taxonomy smoothing and prior-aware adjustments. Auxiliary sidecars supplied constrained rank corrections only when agreement and movement budgets permitted them. The final scores were 0.95044 publicly and 0.94221 privately.

The solution averaged eight image models and then blended their predictions with XGBoost models trained on metadata from the previous PetFinder competition. Image training used binary cross-entropy, with some species-specific models and fold-specific pseudo-labels to avoid leakage. Ten-fold validation kept duplicate images together, and images were cropped to resemble website thumbnails. Metadata blending used AdoptionSpeed where available and separate mixture weights for previous training and test overlaps, improving CV from 17.0058 to 16.9042 and achieving private RMSE 16.89096.

solution_summary: The solution represented each tournament matchup as differences between season-level team profiles and trained jointly on men's and women's data. Features covered Elo, seeds, schedule strength, rankings, efficiency statistics, and recent form. A standardized logistic regression was blended with a 20-seed XGBoost squared-error ensemble using weights of 0.4 and 0.6. Validation held out later seasons, and final probabilities were clipped to 0.05–0.95.

The team fine-tuned five different pretrained language models and combined their min-max-scaled predictions with weights of 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1, and 0.1. Appending the unique targets sharing an anchor and context was a major improvement, supplying more useful information than longer CPC descriptions. Stratified group validation aligned better with leaderboard feedback, while a combined MSE-correlation loss slightly outperformed BCE. Training used multi-dropout and EMA, and the team also explored adversarial methods and tree-based stacking.

The final prediction averaged one LightGBM model and one neural network trained on largely the same feature space. Greedy feature elimination using LightGBM cross-validation removed all calc features and several additional variables. One-hot encoding categorical variables helped, and the neural network also needed one-hot encodings of selected low-cardinality numeric variables while retaining their originals. Regularization was emphasized, while autoencoder reconstruction error was discussed as a promising but insufficiently explored anomaly signal.

solution_title: 98th Place Solution for the DAIGT Competition: TF-IDF + fastText + Distilbert + pseudolabels + instance weighting

It used the DAIGT V2 dataset with two sources excluded and applied typo preprocessing. Confident pseudo-labels and train-versus-test instance weighting provided additional gains. Long inputs were handled by retaining their heads and tails, while metadata tokens helped question models but hurt answer models. The main improvement came from searching column-specific blending weights using out-of-fold predictions, followed by threshold-based rounding. Blending reached 0.435 CV and post-processing raised it to 0.478; a later experiment reached 0.482.

The team generated approximately 2.5 million examples, using cosine deduplication and ChatGPT keyword replacements to diversify prompts. They validated on 5,000 screened LAION2B prompts excluded from training after synthetic validation became unreliable. Their final approach combined fine-tuned OpenCLIP ViT and ConvNeXt encoders with BLIP and nearest-neighbor retrieval, using higher resolutions, partial layer freezing, and layerwise learning-rate decay. Ensembling improved the score by over 2%, while expanding training data from one million to 2.5 million improved it by 1.5%.

solution_summary: The solution used a MaxViT Tiny encoder with a U-Net decoder, trained on the kidney1 and kidney3 datasets. Heavy regularization included EMA, AdamW weight decay, CutMix, MixUp, and extensive image augmentation over 50 epochs. Inference covered the xy, xz, and yz planes using 512-pixel crops with a stride of 256. Final masks used a sigmoid probability threshold because percentile thresholds were unstable in local validation; larger models and 1024-pixel inference did not help.

The team combined eight models spanning raw-EEG 1D networks and spectrogram-based 2D networks. Important ingredients included high-vote training subsets, staged fine-tuning, varied spectrogram construction, and augmentations that preserved useful channel structure. Hill climbing selected base predictions for unweighted input to meta-learners, followed by another hill climb over meta-model outputs. Feature engineering combined numeric transformations, categorical combinations, arithmetic interactions and several ways of incorporating original data. Shared stratified validation and ten-fold meta-learning produced a CV score of 0.97742 and a private score of 0.97768.

The central technique was progressive pretraining across different mel-spectrogram settings before a shared final configuration, which performed better than directly training with the final settings. Soft secondary labels, audio augmentation, CutMix, MixUp, and combined BCE and focal losses supported training. Selected folds were ensembled, while ONNX quantization and threaded execution addressed CPU inference constraints.
