solution_title: [Vishnu]: 21st place solution along with code using Fast.ai
solution_summary: The final segmentation solution used ResNet34 with bottleneck attention and hypercolumns on images resized to 224 × 224. Training used momentum SGD, cyclic learning rates, and ten folds with 100 iterations per model. Bottleneck attention slightly outperformed scSE, and moving from five to ten folds improved the score by 0.002. Deeper backbones offered no benefit, while object context and pseudo-labeling ran into implementation problems.

The pipeline used a customized 2D–3D semantic segmentation model, extracted particle centroids with cc3d, and consolidated predictions from multiple models. Segmentation label radii strongly affected accuracy, with 0.5 or 0.6 times the particle radius used in the solution. solution_summary: The author combined three prompt attacks designed to make essay judges disagree, attaching two to random-word essays and one directly to the topic. solution_title: Autobots roll out! Ensembling 4 transformers to reach position 20.

The solution predicted a smooth geological reference surface and recovered TVT by subtracting that surface from the wellbore's vertical position. Second-order dynamic programming searched piecewise-linear paths using gamma-ray mismatch and a slope-change penalty. Kriging supplied spatial search bounds when reliable, with fixed TVT-limit bounds as a fallback. Around 120 paths per well were blended using handcrafted rules, and reported blended variants achieved leave-one-out CV scores of 6.31.

solution_summary: The solution replaced mean pooling in DeBERTa v3 large with an attention head, improving CV from approximately 0.55 to 0.51. Validation combined bundled examples, a consensus-filtered set of 2,000 generated examples per task, and separate unfiltered fresh examples to expose narrow rules and overfitting. The detectors used different backbones, slice-channel counts, and bounding-box configurations, while transformer training used augmented cached region features and staged backbone unfreezing. A weighted ensemble achieved public and private scores of 0.82494 and 0.80592, outperforming the individual pipelines.

solution_summary: The solution calibrated signals using the host procedure with binning and hot-pixel handling omitted, then split transit regions using derivatives. It estimated transit depth by combining polynomial fitting with a local relative signal-drop calculation at multiple wavelength resolutions. Uncertainty was estimated from the standard deviation of four coarse wavelength-chunk depths. The final spectrum blended global and fine-grained estimates, increasing the fine-grained contribution as estimated uncertainty grew.

solution_summary: The solution used a weighted ensemble of 1D CNNs selected through six-fold patient-based validation. solution_summary: The solution uses an IBN-ResNet50 classifier with 1024×1024 inputs to address fine-grained visual similarity and field-related domain differences. Conditional and raw gradient-boosted, logistic, and neural predictions fed an ontology-aware GCN stacker together with electronic GO annotations. It merged CAFA5 training data and used OOF base predictions plus alternative inference configurations. ESM-IF experiments provided inconsistent gains, so the original ESM inference configuration remained the main submission, which scored 0.44640.
compute: Rented GPU for protein encoding; hardware and duration unspecified.

solution_title: 1st Place Removed Solution - All Faces Are Real Team
solution_summary: This statement primarily explains why one submission was disqualified, but also describes two ensemble approaches. The retained solution used competition data alone and an unweighted mean of 12 models, obtaining a private score of 0.44531. The disqualified submission combined six competition-data models with nine models trained using additional external data and scored 0.42320. Its external data comprised license-filtered Flickr face images and manually collected faces from CC-BY YouTube videos; the dispute concerned additional permissions from depicted individuals.
external_data: ["Resized FlickrFacesHQ dataset, filtered by license", "Face images manually collected from CC-BY YouTube videos"]

solution_summary: The solution used a CNN with squeeze-and-excitation blocks, five-fold validation, geometric augmentation, and fold prediction aggregation. Test-set pseudo-labeling was the most effective technique. Iterative training added correctly classified Dig-MNIST examples to limit the harm from its distribution differences. The final model trained on approximately 75,000 images achieved 0.9924 private accuracy, while an alternative without Dig-MNIST achieved 0.9916.
compute: About 4 hours per five-fold training set on RTX 2080 and i9-9900KF

solution_summary: The layout solution combined engineered graph features with a GPS-style GNN using SAGE convolutions, Linformer attention, and random-walk positional encodings. Graph pruning retained configurable nodes and their neighbors, while a late variant merged other connected nodes and achieved the best CV on xla:default. Training used pairwise hinge loss, Adam, cosine annealing, and collection-specific fine-tuning after joint training. The final submission used different pruning strategies by collection, while the tile dataset used a simpler five-layer SAGE GNN without extra features or positional encodings.

solution_title: 4th place solution - 🎖️ my first gold medal 🎖️ (+source code available!)
solution_summary: The solution ensembled DeBERTa token-tagging models with careful preservation of line breaks and offset-based subword labels. GPU beam search enforced more coherent BIO sequences, while entity-level ensembling combined models with different tokenizers by averaging overlapping span boundaries. Training used learning-rate warmup and decay, gradient clipping, checkpointing, and frequent selection with the competition metric. Both final selected ensembles achieved a reported private score of 0.735.
compute: A100 GPU; batch size 8.

solution_summary: The team reused its previous landmark pipeline with sub-center ArcFace and dynamic margins, newer architectures and improved reranking. The retrieval ensemble combined three transformers and four CNNs, with transformers providing stronger local retrieval scores. Training used progressive image sizes for CNNs, cosine scheduling and Adam or AdamW. Reranking softly boosted or penalized similarities according to confidence that an index image was positive or negative.
compute: Multi-GPU training with DistributedDataParallel.

solution_summary: The provided pipeline generates separate XGBoost and LightGBM submissions and a combined submission. Their public scores were 0.03061, 0.03059, and 0.03063 respectively, with the combination performing best. The instructions specify Python 3 dependencies and warn that data preparation requires 30GB of memory.

solution_summary: The selected submission changed the prediction threshold to 0.152 based on an expectation of more positive samples. A separate model trained on data rotated about 15 degrees around two or three axes achieved 0.492 privately but was not selected because its public score was weaker. Rotation improved the private score by about 0.04 over the baseline while reducing the public score by 0.074. The author did not implement local cross-validation and attributed the selection mistake to reliance on the public leaderboard.

This repository documents one team member's LightGBM pipeline for click-fraud prediction. It uses cached Feather datasets and engineered click counts, temporal differences, attribution ratios, and latent features. Multiple negatively downsampled datasets are generated with different seeds, and their prediction values are averaged in the illustrated configuration. Validation is filtered to click hours matching the submission test period, and early stopping controls training.
compute: Docker container on an AWS EC2 spot instance; instance type and runtime unspecified.

solution_title: 6th Place: Select Feature Combinations based on RMSE Scores
solution_summary: The final pipeline combined five regression model families and then corrected predictions using anomalous values and reliable feature-group means. Feature combinations were evaluated by validation RMSE to select useful target encodings, while original-source rows supplied additional labeled examples. Extracting the integer part of episode length was the most impactful engineered feature. A later published five-fold single-LightGBM implementation achieved a private score of 11.63.

The author trained a RoBERTa-base encoder with an MLP regression head on data from an earlier toxicity classification competition. Toxicity targets were formed by weighting original label features, and simplifying text cleaning improved the reported private score from 0.80826 to 0.81363. Predictions were averaged across five independently sampled training subsets. Adam, a decreasing learning-rate schedule, weight decay, dropout, and validation-loss early stopping supported generalization.

The solution first removed large signal noise using methods including linear regression, Gaussian mixture models, and FFT filters. A single WaveNet then processed cleaned signal and a baseline of open-channel predictions in sequences of length 4,000, training for 150 epochs. The baseline helped the network infer noise from the difference between signal and predicted channels, allowing it to model both channel patterns and noise patterns. The single model achieved private and public scores of 0.94541 and 0.94683, and even rounded signal values worked as a useful baseline.

The team built primarily bidirectional GRU classifiers using diverse pretrained FastText and GloVe embeddings. Back-translated comments augmented training and inference, while ensemble-generated pseudo-labels expanded training with test samples. A blend of arithmetic averaging and optimized LightGBM stacking reached a reported public score of 0.9890. Careful validation, translation grouping, and model selection across multiple metrics supported the ensemble's robustness.
compute: 6 GPUs across the team; approximately 2 hours per model for eight-fold OOF training on over one million augmented and pseudo-labeled samples.
external_data: ["Common Crawl, Wikipedia, and Twitter pretrained embedding corpora"]

solution_title: One week to Silver - LB 86 Approach
solution_summary: The solution blended Arboretum, XGBoost, and LightGBM using just over 100 features drawn from public baselines and custom purchase-history statistics. It combined product embedding components, customer segments, order streaks, lag features, and purchase-state skew. A broken out-of-fold pipeline led to validation on a fixed 25% holdout, and F1 expectation optimization converted predictions into final baskets. The final blend weighted Arboretum at 0.7 and the other models at 0.15 each; retraining with lower learning rates improved the private score by 0.0002.
compute: One intensive week of work, 50+ hours; hardware unspecified.

solution_title: Silver Medal Solution (that was not selected) :(
solution_summary: The author shares a team kernel and highlights its feature-generation work. The team did not select that submission, and attempts to build on it were unsuccessful. The post provides no specific features, model architecture, validation procedure, or scores.

The solution combined DeBERTa essay-level discourse models with a second stage of LightGBM and neural models. Processing all discourses in an essay together improved accuracy and efficiency, while auxiliary discourse-type prediction and token-classification variants supplied useful diversity. Predictions were adjusted to training class means and blended with optimized weights, with second-stage models adding about 0.003–0.005 improvement. Three rounds of leak-free pseudo labeling on data from the previous Feedback competition were another major component.
compute: A linked efficiency kernel achieves 0.557 private score in 5 minutes 40 seconds.

solution_summary: The solution used a YOLOv7 segmentation approach based on a public baseline, with input resolution adjusted to account for the segmentation head's quarter-resolution output. The author finished with fine-tuning on ds1 to avoid dilation. A higher-resolution experiment from 640 to 800 achieved the team's strongest individual model scores, reported as LB 0.473 and PB 0.563. Several alternatives, including repeated pseudo-labeling, YOLOv8, and U-Net refinement inside detected boxes, did not go well.

solution_title: The thrill of the chase: Tim Salimans on how he took home Deloitte/Fide chess comp
solution_summary: The author extended TrueSkill by shrinking player ratings toward recent opponents and weighting recent matches more heavily. Rolling out-of-sample predictions supported two post-processing stages using standard and locally weighted logistic regression. These stages incorporated player ratings, match counts, opponent-strength statistics, monthly predicted win rates, and random-forest predictions. Exploiting information in Swiss-system match schedules dramatically improved the score, while follow-up data also supported the model's usefulness without that information.

The best model used one-dimensional temporal convolutions over linear-frequency log magnitude spectrograms, followed by temporal max pooling and a classification head. Training used time and frequency masking, with oversampling proving the most useful class-imbalance treatment. Longer training clips, Wav2Vec 2.0 fine-tuning, and pretraining on all 152 classes did not improve the baseline. Models overfit despite validation-based checkpoint selection, while reducing the prediction threshold from 0.5 to 0.3 improved the reported score from 0.51 to 0.57.

solution_title: LLM-Guided Evolutionary Visual Transformation (0-Score but Interesting)
solution_summary: The system combined evolutionary search over grid-transformation programs with a multimodal DistilGPT2 proposer. A small CNN supplied visual embeddings, while successful evolutionary trajectories supplied task-specific fine-tuning examples. Search used elites, mutations, extensions, novelty filtering, and local improvement; inference selected the most frequently sampled program. The approach scored zero and appeared slow, with long programs and possible model distortion identified as concerns.
compute: Local machine with a 12GB GTX3060

solution_summary: The pipeline generates physically plausible well trajectories, blends them into a parent curve, and applies a small learned residual correction. A frozen neural prior and LightGBM/CatBoost trajectory branch supply additional signals, while a multi-output Ridge decoder predicts 16 low-frequency DCT coefficients. Conservative shrinkage and physical correction caps limit damage when gamma-ray alignment selects the wrong geological layer. Nested well-grouped validation produced 6.275 pooled OOF RMSE versus 6.368 for the physical parent, with a public score of 5.766.
The post directs readers to a blog describing the author's approach. It also links to a GitHub repository containing source code. The supplied text contains no technical details of the solution.

solution_title: NeurIPS - Ariel Data Challenge 2024: Bronze Medal Solution( 113th)
solution_summary: The solution refined public notebooks into a signal-processing pipeline that calibrated, cropped, differenced, and binned the telescope readings. Gradient-based transit detection isolated the event, and Nelder-Mead optimization fitted a transit scaling factor against a polynomial signal model. Training-derived scales adjusted the predicted spectra and constant uncertainties, followed by rounding to six decimal places. Reported scores were 0.5543416 on the public leaderboard and 0.5743219 on the private leaderboard.

solution_title: Video of the 18th place solution and general discussion of the competition
solution_summary: The post links to a recorded talk about audio processing, the author's competition solution, and ideas used by the winners. It describes the ML Trainings meetup series and its Russian- and English-language videos. The post itself provides no technical solution details.

solution_title: My thoughts + Past prize-winning solution in the 2026 final results
solution_summary: The author describes spending time developing an entry and learning about a Quality feature, but gives no reproducible final pipeline. They reran three previous top solutions and report scores of 0.1278382 and 0.1393912 for two of them, while the third deteriorated late in the competition. They also ask whether others used injury information or freshman impact, without claiming to have incorporated those sources.

solution_title: 98th Place Solution for ICR Identifying Age-Related Conditions Competition
solution_summary: The approach first predicted training-only Greek variables and added their probabilities to the measurement features. A diverse ensemble of mostly underbagged models then predicted the target, with mean blending after excluding weak members. Greek preprocessing was fitted within cross-validation to prevent leakage, and the final validation scheme stratified on Alpha. The actual submission scored 0.14 publicly and 0.38 privately, illustrating the difficulty of reliable model selection on this dataset.

solution_title: First time Competition, 75th place solution silver region
solution_summary: The team addressed noisy cassava labels using label smoothing and knowledge distillation with EfficientNet-B4 and ResNeXt50 classifiers. Five-fold training, image augmentations, and eight-pass test-time augmentation supported the final inference approach. The distilled EfficientNet-B4 achieved 0.9034 private accuracy, while the distilled EfficientNet-B4 plus ResNeXt50 combination reached about 0.904 public and 0.90036 private accuracy. Taylor cross-entropy with smoothing was reported as the best loss, and NFNet was abandoned because time was insufficient.
compute: Training time limited to eight hours; teammates trained separate folds.

solution_title: 17th place finish - description of my methodology
solution_summary: The author adapted Chessmetrics to basketball by iteratively estimating team strength from opponent ratings and margin-based game scores. Ratings used current-season games equally and were regularized with two hypothetical draws against a conference-strength estimate derived from current members' previous five years of ratings. Rating differences were converted to win probabilities with separately tuned intervals for men and women. Two submissions used regular-season versus tournament-based tuning, with the tournament-tuned version performing better.

The author trained an ensemble of eight transformer models for the six scoring targets. Multi-task learning added the minimum and maximum target values as auxiliary targets after comparing several aggregate targets by cross-validation. Training used four groups of layer-wise learning rates, mean pooling, and multilabel stratified cross-validation. Nelder-Mead optimized the final blend, and the author relied on cross-validation despite limited leaderboard improvement.

The post congratulates competitors and opens a solution-sharing discussion after preliminary standings became available. It highlights the substantial leaderboard shakeup. The author asks participants to explain their solutions, final submission choices, and cross-validation strategies.

solution_title: 275 Place Solution for the Optiver - Trading at the Close (Drop from silver on public to bronze on private)
solution_summary: The team blended LightGBM, CatBoost, and LSTM models for the time series prediction task. Their most important feature compared each stock's WAP with the mean WAP across stocks at the same date and time bucket, expressing the relative difference in basis points. They identified the absence of retraining during the online period as their main mistake, with performance deteriorating over that period.

solution_title: A noob's journey to the  258th(Top 20%) place.
solution_summary: The final submission blended MobileNet and SE-ResNeXt predictions, achieving a score of 0.922. MobileNet training repeatedly resumed from saved weights and progressed from 64×64 to 128×128 images using 30,000 examples per class. SE-ResNeXt was trained on all available images for one epoch and scored 0.919. An earlier CNN with bidirectional LSTMs achieved 0.85, while limited compute credits constrained further experimentation.

solution_summary: The solution combined four-class study classification with auxiliary segmentation masks derived from bounding boxes, alongside YOLOv5 image-level detection. Study models used pseudo-labels and additional RICORD and BIMCV data, with noisy BIMCV samples manually removed. The final study ensemble combined EfficientNet variants and a transformer across input sizes, with horizontal-flip inference augmentation. Pseudo-labeling increased the reported detector mAP@0.5 from 0.567 to 0.576, while additional inference augmentations and binary classification formulations did not work.

The solution exploited value-frequency leakage by computing counts over training data and the real test subset, excluding fake test rows. Synthetic samples preserved the pairing between each feature value and its count, with roughly 20-fold positive and two-fold negative augmentation. Neural networks receiving 200 value-count pairs outperformed LightGBM, while transformed features, pseudo-labeling, and neural-network stacking provided further gains. The neural networks reached about 0.924 public leaderboard performance, and stacking added around 0.001.

The original model decoded 1,292 unique labels and struggled with unseen character combinations. After the competition, the author compared a three-head model with separate models for root, vowel, and consonant components. Combining the original model for seen combinations with the component models for unseen combinations achieved public 0.9925 and private 0.9552. Adding unspecified postprocessing further improved the reported private score to 0.9704.
compute: Trained only on TPU.

solution_summary: The solution combined EfficientNet-B5 and EfficientNet-B4 with soft voting and rotational test-time augmentation. Strong augmentation used different cropping rules for complete and cropped eyeballs, unrestricted rotations, and pixel-level changes. Models were pretrained on 2015 data and trained with class weights, an ordinal categorical cross-entropy loss, and a decreasing Adam learning rate. A single model achieved about 0.87 validation kappa without TTA, and the final ensemble scored 81.6 on the public set and 92.0 on the private set.

The solution averaged groups of correlated Fvar columns and removed constant columns after exploring the combined training and test data. It split observations into three groups according to feature availability, then imputed and modeled each group separately to minimize imputation. The final prediction was a weighted blend of random forests, gradient boosting, support vector machines, and multivariate adaptive regression splines. Repeated two-fold cross-validation guided tuning, and subsequent models did not improve the blend.

solution_title: 24th Place Solution for the RSNA 2024 Lumbar Spine Degenerative Classification Competition
solution_summary: The solution first located diagnostic points using a TD-CNN for slice selection and a heatmap-trained U-Net for vertebral coordinates. DICOM affine transformations mapped coordinates between image stacks, and fixed physical-size crops standardized diagnosis inputs across varying pixel spacings. DenseNet121-based TD-CNNs classified conditions with weighted cross-entropy, followed by a master classifier that combined outputs within each spinal level. The team corrected mislabeled training coordinates and standardized right-side subarticular views by flipping them; 3D models and a single TD-CNN consuming all images did not work well.

The solution used a custom, strongly regularized iterative LS ensemble implemented from scratch in native C. Feature development used a leave-one-out environment and produced roughly 900–1500 features depending on the number of channels. Features described temporal energy, frequency-band energy, and relationships between channels, with nonlinear transformations added. Post-processing paired likely adjacent ten-minute segments and generally assigned the maximum of their scores.

The solution used LightGBM with 40 features. Most features were count encoded. It achieved a public score of 0.68563 and a private score of 0.66370. The shared kernel reduced the data from eight million to four million rows because of memory limits.

solution_title: SMILES😘 Data Science Competition: A Deep Dive
solution_summary: The post describes exploratory analysis of donor, dose, timepoint, control, and cell-type distributions. It introduces Morgan fingerprints and applies t-SNE and PCA for visualization, alongside RDKit molecule rendering. It also reports benchmarking several conventional and neural models using MAE, MSE, and R-squared. The text does not specify a final submission pipeline, validation design, or numerical model results.

The author trained a separate graph neural network for each target and averaged predictions across five folds. Functional connectivity data became weighted symmetric adjacency matrices, while a pretrained MedicalNet 3D ResNet-10 supplied fixed component features. Node-wise implementation enabled independent edge parameters, and DropEdge provided essential regularization. The approach worked well for age prediction but was less effective for the other targets.

solution_title: A bronze for prompt engineering (Public: 20, Private: 24)
solution_summary: The author adapted a public DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B AWQ notebook with limited submission opportunities. The main change was to alternate expert mathematics prompts requesting detailed reasoning or Python code using SymPy. This prompting variant scored 20 publicly and 24 privately, while a separate configuration reached 26 publicly. An accidental switch to ordinary Qwen-14B performed substantially worse.
compute: An experimental inference configuration set a total cutoff of 4 hours 50 minutes.

solution_title: Denoising Autoencoder- Unique solution for TPS-FEB2022
solution_summary: The author developed a denoising-autoencoder pipeline to address noisy data and perceived train-test drift. The approach emphasized exploring unfamiliar algorithms rather than extensive tuning. NLP techniques were also tried, although their implementation and outcome are unspecified. The author deliberately avoided post-processing and did not provide detailed architecture or training settings.

The pipeline combined three retrievers with six rerankers, taking the union of each retriever's top ten candidates. Separate topic and content encoders, short sequences, and large batches improved retrieval, reaching candidate recall of 0.853. Some rerankers were initialized through additional retriever training, and balanced sampling accelerated convergence. Simple averaging of reranker predictions achieved validation F2 of 0.6882 and a private score of 0.693.

The final solution used a weighted ensemble of 12 neural networks and eight gradient boosting models with several hundred historical features. LightGBM models predicted 17 product-addition classes, while Keras networks predicted the presence of 16 products using two hidden layers of 512 nodes. Models varied in training periods, feature sets, and random seeds. Postprocessing substituted selected products' predictions from alternative scoring months, removed already-owned products, and adjusted product scores and ensemble weights using public leaderboard feedback.

solution_title: 18th Place: Many OOFs, Neural Networks over GBDTs, and Greedy Features
solution_summary: The final solution stacked 140 diverse models with Ridge regression and relied more on feature diversity than extensive hyperparameter tuning. Useful features included discretized numerical categories, digit and modular transformations, bi- and tri-gram interactions, and target-encoded bitwise combinations. Linear ensembling consistently outperformed nonlinear stacking, while pseudo-labeling, autoencoders, and higher-order categorical interactions did not work. The author concluded that including weak out-of-fold predictions hurt the ensemble and that stronger prediction selection could have improved it.

solution_title: 122nd Solution for Google - American Sign Language Fingerspelling Recognition Competition
solution_summary: The solution improved a public Transformer and 1D-CNN baseline through frame feature engineering and augmentation. Preprocessing gathered lip, hand, and pose landmarks, filtered frames using hand information, and resized and normalized sequences. Augmentation included cropping, temporal resampling, horizontal reflection, affine transforms, and masking. The authors reported a 0.007 improvement over the baseline score of 0.699, while supplemental data and a late learning-rate increase did not improve the final approach.

solution_title: [Rank 283 private LB] PurgedCV + Stock clustering approach
solution_summary: The approach emphasized feature engineering and trained LightGBM models on five purged validation folds. Features combined imbalance, time, rolling statistics, order-book signals, and stock cluster, sector, and market-cap information. Inference averaged the five models, subtracted the prediction mean, and clipped the outputs. Mean subtraction performed better than the alternative zero_sum function.

The solution built on 213tubo's repository and ensembled U-Net models with MaxViT and NFNet encoders. The author manually inspected every series and corrected missing or misplaced event labels. Training used Mixup, SpecAugment, and sleep-label smoothing, while sliding inference discarded window ends. Post-processing removed predictions in repeated daily sensor patterns considered invalid, reducing false positives.

The author built a neural network combining text and categorical inputs with an optional image branch made of convolutional layers, reporting a final leaderboard score around 0.2180. CBOW word2vec, CNN and RNN text processing, attention, and extensive batch normalization were helpful. Adding images improved the score by about 0.0005, while smaller architecture changes provided further gains. Images were resized to 64×64 and preloaded as uint8 NumPy arrays to manage loading time and memory.
compute: Approximately 20 GB of memory for preloaded training images.

solution_summary: The post documents experimental changes rather than a complete fingerspelling pipeline. Increasing maximum sequence length and the expansion ratio, together with borrowed post-processing, raised the reported private score from 0.741 to 0.752. Longer training produced no further private-score gain. Normalization accelerated convergence without improving leaderboard performance, while reduced dropout, moving batch normalization, and spatial masking were unsuccessful.

solution_title: 43rd place: Every cloud has a silver lining
solution_summary: The author describes an ensemble inspired by two public notebooks and advocates combining CatBoost, LightGBM, and XGBoost. The notebook ensemble achieved the author's highest private score but was not selected as the final submission because of concerns about overfitting. The discussion favors weighted averaging over ranking predictions to preserve prediction magnitudes and consistency across racial groups. TabNet was considered but explicitly not used.
compute: GPU time was exhausted; hardware and runtime were not specified.

solution_summary: This post synthesizes several teams' approaches rather than presenting the author's own final pipeline. BERT-based models commonly combined information across layers and used separate learning rates for encoders and heads. Pseudo-labeling, auxiliary training on StackExchange data, and back-translation supplied additional supervision or augmented examples. Other recurring choices included separate question and answer models, custom pooling heads, and ensembles with varied text truncation.

solution_title: A model used in the 24th solution - pure linear algebra!
solution_summary: The author predicted gene differential expression by fitting linear transformations between cell lines using chemicals measured in both source and target cells. Full-rank SVD reduced the gene space from 18,211 dimensions to 614, allowing the transformations to be fitted and applied with lower memory requirements before reconstructing gene-level predictions. The final ensemble assigned 70% combined weight to this method and a neural autoencoder imitation, with 30% assigned to public Pyboost, neural-network, and Linear SVR approaches. The pure linear algebra model achieved the best private score, reported as 0.768 private and 0.582 public, with CD4+ T cells particularly useful for predicting B cells and NK cells for predicting Myeloid cells.
compute: The direct linear model required more than 20 GB of memory and could not run on the free Saturn Cloud tier used by the author.

solution_title: Next top GB model solution to The 2nd YouTube-8M Video Understanding Challenge
solution_summary: The repository provides a reproducible video-classification workflow covering training, evaluation, weight averaging, quantization, distillation, and graph ensembling. Its worked example trains a gated NetVLAD model on frame-level RGB and audio features. Quantized models can be combined into a weighted ensemble graph, and ensemble predictions can generate distillation datasets for subsequent training. Models were trained individually on a single GPU using TensorFlow 1.8.0.
compute: Single GPU per model; creating a distillation dataset requires approximately 1.4 TB of storage.

solution_summary: The final system ensembled five compact CLIP-style transformers with varied architectures, seeds, sequence lengths, and landmark features. Strong spatial and temporal augmentation, motion features, and simple video mean/std normalization supported training. Models were trained in PyTorch and manually transferred into TensorFlow implementations to reduce inference latency and accommodate a larger ensemble. The ensemble achieved public and private scores of 0.794 and 0.87, compared with 0.786 and 0.865 for the best single model.

The author assembled an ensemble from public language-model notebooks and borrowed disagreement handling. Inference probabilities were constrained by the misconception classes observed for each question and answer pair, which the author considered central to the result. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B-bnb-4bit replaced Gemma after favorable validation and leaderboard results. Text augmentation had mixed effects, and augmented examples in local validation were identified as a source of misleading validation scores.
compute: Local GPU: 5070 Ti; GPU and time constraints limited experiments.

solution_title: 15th Place Solution: SD3.5M + Vtracer + select best from 3 image
solution_summary: The solution generated images with SD3.5M using a flat-illustration prompt suffix, then converted them with vtracer using binary-searched parameters. PaliGemma2 selected the best of three candidate images. The largest improvement came from splitting each description into three questions for evaluation.

The solution engineered card-level features from eight combinations of historical transactions, new transactions, and merchant information. Transaction aggregates, interval and interaction features, sequence embeddings, and transaction-level LightGBM predictions supplied diverse signals. Feature selection produced 12 feature sets for LightGBM and neural networks, whose predictions were stacked and averaged. Stacking and isotonic regression improved validation but hurt private results, while combining predictions with a non-outlier model delivered a small consistent gain.

The team replaced discourse text classification with transformer token classification to improve accuracy and inference speed. Models predicted discourse labels either by averaging token predictions or by using the first separator token, with weighted cross-entropy helping the averaging variant. The best public submission combined Nelder–Mead blending, LightGBM stacking, and XGBoost stacking in equal proportions. Pseudo-labeling with Feedback 2021 data and adversarial weight perturbation also improved reported validation loss.

The solution combined a probabilistic date interpolation model for groups seen in training with group-level predictive models. Each group was treated as a statistical observation, and within-group feature histograms supplied the model inputs. Predictions mixed logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, and XGBoost-based public scripts. Leaderboard feedback formed a third component, although its use was not explained.

solution_title: 142nd Place Solution — Surface Least-Squares Field + Seed-Averaged Matching Bank
solution_summary: The solution combined a sequential GR/typewell matcher with small CNN correction models, a geological surface estimate, and a GR common-error correction. The largest improvement came from a sparse least-squares surface field injected through an uncertainty gate with a capped correction. Averaging repeated jackknife gate estimates reduced deployment variance, while grouped validation and statistical controls guided decisions despite noisy public scores. The final system achieved pooled offline RMSE of 6.85 and private RMSE of 7.906.

solution_title: Last Place Solution - The Worst Kaggle Solution Ever!!!
solution_summary: The post celebrates an intentionally poor competition result and links to the author's solution notebook. It describes the score as dramatically worse than other submissions. No methods or implementation details are provided in the post.

The author trained CatBoost models separately for galactic objects, extragalactic objects, and extragalactic objects with spectroscopic redshift, using roughly 1,000–2,000 features. Features included supernova template fits, light-curve timing and slope statistics, feets descriptors, Gaussian-process features, and distance-scaled shifted flux. Class-specific weights optimized on out-of-fold predictions combined CatBoost, LightGBM, and neural-network predictions. Class99 probability formulas developed through leaderboard probing produced a further 0.057 improvement, bringing the public score to 0.680.
compute: Gaussian-process feature extraction used 30 instances.

solution_summary: The solution ensembled CNNs trained on mel spectrograms of 30-second audio crops, splitting each crop into six segments for backbone processing and using five-second snippets at inference. Mixup, background noise, rating-based loss weights, and label smoothing helped address weak and noisy labels. Validation used training soundscapes with three silent recordings removed and bootstrap sampling to assess robustness. Predictions were averaged across models and seeds, refined using a binary bird detector and metadata, and converted to labels using percentile-based thresholds. Full-soundscape validation F1 approached 0.84, and the final inference kernel took approximately one hour.

solution_summary: The post announces the release of source code and a model description in a downloadable archive. It also links to a simplified executable script. The author reports a post-deadline private leaderboard score of 0.999594 but provides no technical description in the post itself.

solution_title: 25th Place - GBDT plus NN - Trust CV
solution_summary: The final solution equally combined CatBoost, XGBoost, and a multilayer perceptron with simple feature engineering. Model selection used cross-validation AUC as a smoother proxy for the competition's accuracy metric. The neural network treated every column as categorical strings, grouping rare values and explicitly representing missing values. The ensemble achieved CV accuracy 0.9406 and private leaderboard accuracy 0.9415; adding other models did not improve ensemble CV.

The team ensembled transformer sequence-labeling models, primarily DeBERTa variants alongside BART and Muppet, using overlapping chunks to handle long essays. Training combined small batches, cosine learning-rate decay, multisample dropout, token masking, and diverse loss functions or CRF decoding. Out-of-fold predictions guided span thresholds and ensemble pruning, while post-processing linked evidence and constrained Lead predictions. Averaging one-hot CRF outputs with other models' probabilities produced final submissions with private scores of 0.723 and 0.721.
compute: GPU of unspecified type; typically five training epochs

solution_title: Rank 2 approach - a century of component feature sets and deep ensemble
solution_summary: The solution combined extensive categorical feature engineering with a three-level ensemble of boosted trees, neural networks, and ridge regression. More than 1,600 features included categorical combinations, target encodings, and both numeric and string representations of weight capacity. solution_summary: The author used CatBoost with hyperparameters optimized through Optuna. Experiments also included XGBoost and LightGBM, but CatBoost produced the best result. The post describes a simple approach and links to a notebook without providing validation details or numerical scores.

The pipeline normalized location text and generated 28 candidates per record by geographic retrieval followed by weighted text and distance similarities. A single CatBoost model used extensive geographic, string, language, frequency, TF-IDF, and candidate-rank features. Training examples were assembled from repeated POI-based splits, and final training used all data with more iterations and no early stopping. Graph-based probability smoothing and repeated neighbor expansion refined the predicted matches.

solution_title: [166th] Place Bronze Medal Solution : Deep Generalization using LLM
solution_summary: The solution combined five prediction streams to generalize rule-violation classification to unseen moderation rules. Training examples were expanded from the provided positive and negative examples, with inputs pairing rules and comments and adding URL-derived semantic cues. A few-shot Q-LoRA-tuned LLaMA model and a fine-tuned Qwen embedding retrieval stream formed the primary blend, supplemented by two DeBERTa variants and DistilRoBERTa. Predictions were converted to percentile ranks and combined through a two-stage weighted ensemble.

solution_summary: The solution generated examples for unseen misconceptions and used LLM-generated explanations as inputs to retrieval and reranking models. A Stella biencoder retrieved candidates, and a fine-tuned Qwen listwise reranker scored the top 104 candidates in two groups of 52 using single-token probabilities. Subject-grouped validation better matched leaderboard performance, and quantized inference enabled a fold ensemble with partial coverage of the third fold. The final reported ensemble achieved 0.653 public and 0.597 private scores.
compute: Local RTX 4090; rented A100 for 32B training, about 7 hours per reranker and $350 including experiments; inference about 120 minutes.

solution_summary: The solution trained sound-event detection CNNs on random 30-second crops, treating foreground and background bird labels as binary targets. An 18-model ensemble combined pooled logits, with models selected greedily using annotated training soundscapes. Inference first identified allowed species from overlapping 30-second windows, then applied a lower threshold to five-second predictions restricted to those species. Threshold tuning raised training-soundscape F1 to 0.773, and the submitted ensemble scored 0.6715 privately. A later experiment using max pooling for short windows improved results further but was not submitted.

solution_summary: The final submission averages three independently developed ECG digitization pipelines with weights of 45%, 32%, and 23%, achieving a private score of 22.03. Each pipeline rectifies images, predicts waveform segmentation or coordinate heatmaps, and extracts voltage signals, with diversity in architectures and preprocessing improving the ensemble. Detailed contributions include EfficientNetV2B1-UNet models with separate segmentation and coordinate heads, and high-resolution DINOv2 models trained on synthetic ECG images before host-data fine-tuning. Confidence-based interpolation, signal sharpening, and aligned lead-redundancy corrections further improve extracted signals; the provided text ends before the full team pipeline is described.

solution_summary: The team ensembled 14 image models, mostly trained on 512×512 RGB inputs with additional Human Protein Atlas data. Cyclic and differential learning rates, focal and LSEP losses, and 32-view test-time augmentation improved performance. External labels were taken from the website after inconsistencies were found in other label sources. A test-similarity holdout supported threshold fitting, while linear stacks with voting handled rare classes and LightGBM stacking handled the remaining classes.
compute: 4x1080ti; approximately two weeks of computing time for the full training cycle

solution_title: 14th Place - Hacking Macro Recall - Chris Writeup
solution_summary: The author contributed an EfficientNetB6 model and macro-recall-oriented postprocessing to a team ensemble. A first model generated class activation maps that guided CutMix augmentation for a second model trained on 128×256 images. Postprocessing reweighted class probabilities using predicted class frequencies raised to −1.2 before selecting labels. CAM CutMix improved CV and leaderboard scores by 0.001, while frequency reweighting reportedly improved the private score by 0.0241.
compute: Four Nvidia V100 GPUs; 24 hours training for the 150-epoch contribution model.

solution_summary: The team trained separate question-label and answer-label transformer models using head and tail text segments and special-token input layouts. Their final ensemble simply averaged BERT, RoBERTa, GPT2, and BERT-RNN predictions. BERT embeddings fed into an LSTM provided another useful model variant. Thresholding six question targets near zero and one improved the leaderboard score by about 0.004, while BERT-large, SQuAD2 pretraining, and gradient accumulation did not help.

solution_title: [3rd Place solution] Refine from Sparse to Dense
solution_summary: The solution used only 2D U-Net and U-Net++ models, with progressive pseudo-labeling to densify sparse kidney annotations. Training scale augmentation simulated the private test set's voxel spacing, while mostly 512-pixel inputs reduced risks from short orthogonal slices. Models were trained on all kidneys after checking convergence stability, with thresholds transferred from earlier validation experiments and heavy intensity augmentation. A single MaxViT model and an equally weighted four-model ensemble both scored 0.727 on the private leaderboard.

solution_title: [126th place] simple solution overview with code
solution_summary: The main solution averaged the six best-performing folds from an Inception-v4 U-Net trained across ten folds. Its strongest configuration used 202×202 images, 27 pixels of reflection padding on each side, SE layers, and hypercolumns. Training used SGD, a transition from binary cross-entropy to Lovasz loss, and the one-cycle policy, with minimal augmentation and flip test-time augmentation. A second submission averaged ResNet34, SE-ResNeXt-50, and Inception-v4 models trained over five folds.

solution_title: 710th Place Solution for the Open Problems – Single-Cell Perturbations
solution_summary: The post shares a GitHub repository containing the author's competition solution. It reflects on lessons from a first competition and invites the community to find the material useful. The supplied text contains no methodological details or numerical results.

solution_title: Rank 10 approach - FE + brute force models + ensemble
solution_summary: The author built four feature sets and augmented them with predictions from CatBoost regressors and neural network classifiers using grouped target categories. The final pipeline combined conventional LightGBM and CatBoost models with AutoGluon and H2O runs, evaluated using shuffled 10-fold cross-validation. A second-level AutoGluon ensemble followed by Ridge regression produced the final submission. Flooring predictions to integers improved the score by about 0.0001, and both reported submissions achieved a private leaderboard score of 1.02847.

solution_title: 1st place solution: transformer and acceleration data
solution_summary: The solution combined transformer encoders with two bidirectional LSTM layers in TensorFlow. Normalized sensor series were padded and converted into patches, with patchwise maximum targets reducing output resolution and repeated predictions restoring the original resolution. Separate tdcsfog and defog pipelines each averaged four models, with some defog models incorporating notype data. The eight-model submission achieved private and public scores of 0.514 and 0.527.

solution_summary: The author shares selected breakthroughs from several capture-the-flag challenges and links a notebook containing their solutions. Three-dimensional t-SNE revealed spiral structures in Cluster3, while an unusual pixel-value count helped solve Sloth. Interpreting columns as key-value pairs unlocked MNIST, and ordering high-scoring words revealed the Semantle2 clue.

solution_title: A High Schooler’s Solo Journey to get a Silver Medal.
solution_summary: The model treated notebook ordering as regression, fixing code-cell positions between 0 and 1 and predicting markdown positions between -0.2 and 1.2. CodeBERT encoded code and markdown cells separately, and an encoder-decoder used positional information and cross-cell interactions before predicting markdown positions. Training used only competition data and a differentiable soft-ranking loss inspired by Spearman correlation to approximate Kendall Tau. The author also implemented batched Kendall Tau evaluation, but reported that limited compute and time left the model undertrained.

The submission combined several neural forecasting models through weighted averaging. Each model used one LSTM layer and two fully connected layers, with diversity from input transformations and MAE or SMAPE objectives. SMAPE training worked with SGD despite its nonconvexity. The models used data only through August 31, and the author identified missing yearly seasonality as a likely source of remaining error.
compute: Final submissions were made on a laptop; training hardware and runtime unspecified.

solution_summary: The post describes the strongest single-model recipe, while the final rank ensemble is only mentioned. It uses report-derived soft targets and two-level attention MIL over feature-map cells from every series, with 3D patient coordinates linking anatomy across views. A training-only bias branch absorbs site-specific reporting habits and is removed during inference, providing the largest improvement. OrthoFoundation-L and CoAtNet performed similarly, with the best OrthoFoundation-L single model scoring 0.962 public and 0.947 private.

solution_summary: The solution stacked ten tree-based base models using an XGBoost meta model trained on original features and out-of-fold predictions. Targets were log-transformed for nine base models and the meta model. Target encoding and categorical treatment of selected numerical features, especially Health Score, were central to performance, while CatBoost handled categorical statistics internally. A three-class target classifier added probability features and improved the reported leaderboard score from 1.02355 to 1.02337.

The author combined XGBoost, LightGBM, and AutoGluon predictions, with extensive repeated cross-validation for the boosting models. The selected submissions were a majority-vote ensemble and an XGBoost stack with prediction inputs recursively removed according to CV performance. CV scores ranged from 0.836 to 0.8364, while private scores ranged from 0.83866 to 0.83935. Retrospectively, the best LightGBM model averaged over 37 folds and 20 repetitions would have performed best.

solution_title: 11th place, The 0.931 Magic Explained: Image Classification
solution_summary: The author trained EfficientNet classifiers on annotation-bounded log-mel spectrogram crops, treating species and song-type combinations as 26 classes. Binary cross-entropy was masked for unobserved classes, and frequency-position gradients helped retain absolute frequency information. Inference used sliding crops and maximum predictions, reaching a reported public score of 0.945 with EfficientNet B3. Semi-supervised methods did not improve the strongest models, and external-data models were excluded from selected submissions despite later showing better private performance.

The solution combined 10 LightGBM models, five XGBoost models, three HistGradientBoosting models, and five public notebooks. Feature engineering included row-level summary statistics, nonlinear transformations, interactions, ratios, and K-means cluster assignments. The reported cross-validation scores were 0.86940 for LightGBM, 0.86924 for XGBoost, and 0.86917 for HistGradientBoosting. The post does not specify ensemble weights or the validation split design.

The team adapted ESM2 protein language models to RNA through masked-language-model pretraining on competition train/test sequences and RNA Central data. Custom folding heads combined ESM2 embeddings, base-pair probabilities, bidirectional recurrent layers, and convolution blocks, alongside simpler linear-head models. Signal-to-noise filtering and sample weighting improved fine-tuning on DMS and 2A3 targets. The final ensemble combined 15 models across five folds each and achieved CV 0.12478 and public leaderboard score 0.14174. RNA-FM underperformed, while an auxiliary base-pair prediction loss was too costly for the larger backbones.
compute: MLM pretraining: 5–20 epochs, totaling 25M–70M samples seen.

solution_summary: The author extended a CatBoost and Polars baseline with an updated inference script and additional features. The final pipeline used 117 features and trained on all available training data, choosing tree counts separately for each question through five-fold early stopping. Six questions received constant predictions to reduce inference time with little validation penalty. The reported final scores were 0.688 CV, 0.687 public, and 0.691 private, with roughly 7 minutes 41 seconds of scoring time.
compute: Approximately 7 minutes 41 seconds scoring time; changes added about 140 seconds.

solution_summary: The author optimized word order using simulated annealing and reports reaching the global minimum for ID 3. A persistent dictionary cache avoided repeated perplexity evaluations. Four swap and shift transformations were explored with an exponential temperature schedule from 5 to 1 and 200 steps per temperature. Repeated runs reused the best phrase with different seeds, with manual word adjustments when optimization became stuck.

solution_title: 20th Place Solution Writeup For Open Problems - Single-cell Perturbations Competition
solution_summary: The post announces an attached detailed solution submitted for consideration for the Judge's reward. It states that citations are included in the PDF. It also links a GitHub repository containing referenced notebooks, but provides no approach details in the supplied text.

The author released a fastai inference kernel and locally trained weights for an audio-tagging solution. Predictions were averaged over windows sliding across each complete audio clip, using two models and ten folds. Inference preparation used an in-memory CSV of filenames and window positions, and image loading avoided PIL. The reported public leaderboard lwlrap was 0.738.

The solution used FiveThirtyEight's predicted probabilities for first-round games and its Elo ratings to generate probabilities for later rounds. Second-round probabilities were adjusted for home-field advantage. Baylor was assigned a 100% chance of winning every game. Two brackets made opposite deterministic predictions for the matchup between the Chicago and Albany region winners.

The final system used DeBERTa-v3-large trained across five folds on competition data and Nicholas Broad's external data. Careful token-label alignment and newline replacement improved preprocessing, particularly for street addresses. The model predicted eight labels, which were converted into BIO labels through post-processing, and validation used only competition data. Additional external sources, fake-PII augmentation, and broader modeling experiments did not improve the baseline, which achieved 0.968 public and 0.964 private leaderboard scores.

solution_summary: The solution extracted long-form names and acronyms with the Schwartz-Hearst algorithm, then filtered candidates with a fine-tuned roberta-base binary classifier. The classifier used a small manually annotated corpus derived entirely from competition training documents. Accepted dataset names were propagated across documents using long-form searches gated by document frequency, with acronym predictions added when present. Public leaderboard feedback guided development, and inference took roughly ten minutes compared with well over an hour for end-to-end Transformer approaches.
compute: Test inference approximately 10 minutes versus well over 1 hour for end-to-end Transformer QA/NER.

solution_title: what i have learned and moving forward
solution_summary: The team combined about 30 mostly convolutional models using raw waveforms, log mel spectrograms, and MFCCs. Class balancing and carefully selected pseudo labels helped address differences between training and leaderboard data. Test-time augmentation averaged predictions from transformed audio, while a compact depthwise convolutional model used distillation for efficient inference. The submitted ensemble scored 0.91060 on the private leaderboard, and another ensemble reached 0.91107.
compute: Compact distilled network ran in roughly 80 ms per sample under Raspberry Pi 3 deployment constraints; training hardware and time were not stated.

solution_summary: The solution used a CatBoost classifier with a log-loss objective and a few categorical features. Inputs came exclusively from competition data and included current seeds, historical win statistics, and previous-season match counts as indicators of tournament progression. Validation used only the last two available seasons. Predicted probabilities were submitted without clipping or modification.

The team cleaned landmark training images by checking label agreement among descriptor neighbors and verifying matches with DELF and spatial verification. They trained FishNet-150, ResNet-101, and SEResNeXt-101 with angular-margin losses, GeM pooling, cosine annealing, and a final full-resolution epoch. Retrieval reranking incorporated top-three descriptor similarities and spatial-verification inlier counts, substantially improving stage-two results. Several query-expansion and graph-based methods helped in stage one but did not transfer well to stage two.

solution_title: 1st place solution - with code and official documentation
solution_summary: The solution reconstructed particle tracks through staged geometric candidate generation, logistic-regression pruning, and local helix extrapolation. It resolved overlapping tracks greedily using an outlier-probability score derived from detector hit densities. Quad-tree spatial queries and analytic density lookups made the dependency-free C++ implementation efficient. The final score was about 0.92 while using about 90% of the hits.
compute: Dependency-free C++; about 8 minutes per event per CPU core for the final submission.

solution_summary: The solution used a single WaveNet-style CNN with batch normalization and light dropout on cleaned Kalman data. Constant signal offsets helped handle test-set shifts, while clustering, centroid distances, shifted signals, rolling statistics, and signal powers supplied additional features. A learning-rate scheduler controlled overfitting. A constant learning rate of 0.001 produced strong out-of-fold performance but worse leaderboard generalization.

solution_title: 5th Place Solution for the WSDM Cup - Multilingual Chatbot Arena
solution_summary: The final submission used Qwen2.5-14B as a preference judge, with vLLM producing log probabilities for answer tokens A and B. The pipeline preserved the beginning and end of long inputs, swapped response positions, added WSDM_LMSYS data, and introduced probability-based labels. When model scores were close, a number-count heuristic broke ties. The reported final public/private accuracy was approximately 0.706/0.712.

The approach used separate 1D CNN and bidirectional LSTM models to predict mouse behaviors frame by frame from 500-frame windows. Models first learned across labs and were then fine-tuned separately for each lab, with distinct models for self and pair behaviors. Engineered pose, motion, relative-position, and metadata features were combined with spatial and temporal augmentation, while unlabeled targets were masked from the loss. Probability averaging and a weighted team ensemble produced a local ensemble CV score of 0.546648.

The submission combined multiple XGBoost models with a weighted average. Features captured game progression, grouped event counts and elapsed times, previous level-group information, and predictions for earlier questions. Gain-based feature selection reduced the large feature sets, while sorting test events improved inference results. Previous-group features and earlier-question predictions mattered most, but unreliable cross-validation encouraged public-score overfitting and the similar models provided little private-score ensemble benefit.

solution_summary: The solution emphasized the competition essays outside Persuade Corpus 2.0 through two-stage training, first using all essays and then fine-tuning on that subset. DeBERTa-v3 regression models used MLM pretraining, frozen layers, explicit newline tokens, and soft targets from first-stage out-of-fold predictions. Validation stratified prompt names and scores separately for the two data sources. A Nelder-Mead ensemble of base and large models with different sequence lengths and pooling heads achieved 0.8357 CV and 0.8399 private score.

solution_title: Measuring per-well bias of the hidden test set with 4 leaderboard probes [writeup]... and losing it all to deadline-day scoring failures
solution_summary: The author builds on a public baseline and uses leaderboard probes to estimate hidden-test prediction bias when local validation is unavailable. Constant prediction shifts and the RMSE identity reveal well-specific biases, with wells identified by row-count rank across reruns. The best scored submission achieved 6.471, while a fully corrected score of about 6.45 was inferred from the probes. Five final submissions carrying corrections completed reruns but never received scores before the deadline.

solution_title: 62th Place Solution - Last Value and Rule-based Multiplier
solution_summary: The final approach forecast from each county's last observed target, adjusted for the new year and multiplied by rules based on its five most recent values. Validation reproduced the test horizon using expanding windows, two-month gaps, and three-month validation periods, with extra folds for year transitions. Linear models, boosted trees, autoregressive models, and Bayesian multiplier optimization did not beat the baseline. The rule-based adjustments produced a significant validation improvement, although exact scores were not recalled.

The solution extracted Phikon embeddings from tissue patches and classified slides with an ensemble of Chowder multiple-instance models. Matching TMA patch resolution to WSI resolution and detecting uncertain predictions as the Other class were especially important. The final submission averaged 65 selected and calibrated Chowder models, achieving public/private scores of 0.64/0.66 in approximately six hours. No extra training data or annotations were added.
compute: Final submissions approximately 6 hours; paired image processing on one P100 GPU with 0.5 GPU and 2 CPU cores per process. Experimental Phikon pretraining took 2.5 days per epoch on 2 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.

solution_title: Telstra Network Disruptions - Predict service faults on Australia's largest telecommunications network
solution_summary: The writeup presents a simplified single-model pipeline using XGBoost and separate scripts for feature extraction, feature importance, and submission generation. The supplied parameters are reported to achieve roughly 0.41 on the private leaderboard, with additional tuning potentially reaching 0.405. The author's competition solution also benefited from model averaging, though the component models and averaging details are not specified.

The agent combines a Producer Lite heuristic planner with logistic-regression behavior-cloning priors learned from high-Elo replays. The priors adjust source ranking and target scores, while physics projections and reinforcement-aware capture requirements guide launches. Player-count-specific presets, especially lowering the four-player ROI threshold to 0.90, were the most effective refinements and produced a score of 1109. A neural ranker and transplanted advanced heuristics reduced game performance despite promising offline metrics.

solution_summary: The pipeline retrieved Wikipedia passages, reranked them with a tuned pretrained reranker, and combined multiple question-answering models with Platypus2 and Xwin. Wikipedia extraction was modified to preserve numerical content, and retrieval operated directly on passages. Reranker training used inference-matched passages and hard negatives, providing a substantial improvement. The final submission scored 0.9284 private, while later ablations showed that removing Platypus2 slightly improved performance.

solution_summary: The author describes an LKH approach that achieved a score of 74265.771731100400. Four quadrants of a standard configuration were connected with one-pixel side lines, and the route was formulated as a symmetric traveling salesman problem in pixel space. Allowed steps were one or two pixels horizontally and one pixel vertically. The resulting tour was converted to arm configurations, with larger steps handled by splitting seven free configuration elements into two groups and modifying each group.

solution_title: Public 12th / Private 26th Place Solution for the HuBMAP - Hacking the Human Vasculature Competition
solution_summary: The solution ensembled four Mask R-CNN models with Swin-S and Swin-T backbones using MMDetection. Models initialized from COCO weights were first trained on dataset2 and then fine-tuned on dataset1, with whole-slide-separated validation. ROI-level weighted box fusion and weighted mask fusion combined models, flip augmentations, and folds. Masks overlapping glomeruli by more than 90% were removed, while sliding windows, neighboring-tile context, and rotation TTA did not improve the final evaluation.

solution_summary: The solution combined public and private AutoML approaches, with gradient boosting models forming a major component. A multi-input neural network run with 25 seeds supplied additional diversity and robustness. The main models were then retrained with high-confidence pseudo-labeled test rows, yielding a small additional improvement.

solution_title: My Solution to this Competition with Code (Score: 0.58655)
solution_summary: The solution first explored and filtered the signals. It then calculated peaks and constructed other engineered features. Multiple models were combined for prediction, but the post provides no model identities, validation details, or numerical results.

The solution stacked 22 models trained on shared four-fold splits. SVR and Ridge used selected embeddings from pretrained models, with SVR achieving a single-model CV of 0.4467. Repeated pseudo labeling and Ridge/LightGBM stacking provided the largest gains. A weighted average of the two stackers achieved CV 0.4423.

The author built a diverse EfficientNet ensemble using shared leak-free folds and selected members and weights through greedy improvement of out-of-fold AUC. Random crops from higher-resolution images and heavy test-time augmentation reduced overfitting and stabilized AUC. The main submission combined eight image models with a metadata model through a geometric mean and achieved CV AUC 0.9505. Additional submissions incorporated public models, with the final weighted blend achieving private AUC 0.9429.

solution_summary: The solution used YOLOv5l6 models trained only on images containing annotated objects, with three-fold validation grouped by video. Rotation augmentation, multiscale training, and image resolution were central to performance. A simple temporal attention-area rule boosted detections overlapping confident boxes from the preceding frame. The final ensemble combined four models across 11 resolution and rotation configurations using WBF, achieving public 0.648 and private 0.737.
compute: Final ensemble was designed to use as much of the 9-hour inference quota as possible.

solution_summary: The system first localized intervertebral keypoints and estimated axial spinal levels, then classified patch sequences with a 2D backbone and encoder-decoder Transformer. Patch-model pretraining substantially improved convergence, and anatomical symmetry allowed training on individual level-sides while evaluating complete studies. Metadata supplied spatial context, and max pooling combined bilateral representations for spinal canal stenosis. Selected submissions used RegNet or HGNet ensembles with test-time augmentation; the best reported private score was 0.4118.

The solution processed remote-sensing imagery with two independent CNN branches, one for RGB and another for altitude, NIR, and NDVI. ImageNet initialization, heavy dropout, and spatial block-label swapping helped the models handle sparse presence-only species labels. Ten ResNet-50, Inception-v4, and DenseNet-201 models were combined using weights derived from prediction variance across test-time augmentations. Architecture selection, label swapping, and ensembling each contributed roughly two percentage points of improvement, while environmental covariates and more elaborate pretraining did not help.
compute: Training distributed across two workstations, each with a 16-core CPU, 128GB RAM, and RTX 3090, plus an HPC system with a Tesla V100.

solution_summary: The solution combined multiclass and multilabel bird classifiers using mel-spectrogram and PCEN inputs. EfficientNet backbones with noisy-student weights dominated, with a SE-ResNet101 model adding diversity. Extensive audio augmentation, class-specific thresholds, and hierarchical averaging supported noisy-label learning. Final checks used spectral statistics and file-versus-chunk predictions to suppress false positives and identify no-call segments.

The agent used an 8-bit LLaMA-3-8B-Inst with a precomputed question tree followed by LLM-generated questions. The answering bot generated a keyword definition and reasoning to reduce ambiguity, while the guesser retained candidate words and previous guesses in memory. Tree depth and other changes were evaluated through local self-play on 200 selected words, with answer prompts also checked against successful game replays. LLaMA-3-8B-Inst outperformed the tested alternatives, while LoRA fine-tuning severely overfit. An emoji-based resource-exhaustion tactic sometimes disrupted opponents but also appeared to cause losses.
compute: Single RTX 4090 GPU

solution_summary: The final approach blended four diverse LightGBM submissions and two heavily modified XdeepFM submissions. Most tree models used 60–70 features, minimal cleanup, and factorized or count-encoded categories, with AvSigVersion removed from most models. Diversity came from feature selection, hyperparameters, folds, and the different model families. The author favored generic models after filtering, feature engineering, and attempts to exploit the time split produced inconsistent results.

The strongest submission combined six folds of a MuRIL Large model adapted to BigBird for longer contexts. The author initialized BigBird from MuRIL, tiled its position embeddings, and continued masked language model pretraining on multilingual mc4 data before staged QA training. XLM-R, MuRIL Large, and RemBERT were also trained, but a cross-model ensemble did not finish within the submission limit. The long-context model achieved private/public scores of 0.756/0.796, making long-context handling the main improvement.
compute: TPU v3-8; base MLM pretraining for 150k steps, large for 90k steps, batch size 1; Kaggle TPUs for RemBERT.

solution_title: Two BERTs are better than one (2nd place solution)
solution_summary: The solution averaged five transformer models with separate question and answer inputs, using dual and siamese architectures with RoBERTa and XLNet backbones. Ordinal binary targets trained with binary cross-entropy were converted into expected values. Grouped validation repeatedly sampled one answer per question and excluded the unstable spelling target from model assessment. Optimized clipping thresholds created ties at prediction extremes, while differential learning rates and warmup supported effective fine-tuning.
compute: V100 for dual RoBERTa-large training with batch size 1 and fp16; final kernel inference close to two hours.

solution_summary: The notebook trains an unconditional convolutional GAN to generate 64×64 dog images from 128-dimensional latent vectors. It filters annotated dog boxes by size and aspect ratio, crops the dogs, and applies random resized crops, horizontal flips, and normalization. Training uses binary cross-entropy, Adam, and softened real labels, while submission generation samples a truncated normal distribution to produce 10,000 images. The introduction reports an earlier CV score of 40.6601 and leaderboard score of 40.49519; although Gaussian noise is announced, the shown loader constructs images from the original crop rather than the computed noisy array.

solution_summary: The solution used a single LightGBM model with lag, difference, rolling, and calendar features. A custom time-series split supported validation, and the Poisson objective worked better than Tweedie. Optuna tuning was tried but excluded from the final submission in favor of a robust configuration. The reported public and private scores were 0.61444 and 0.60825.

solution_title: 7th place solution (with inference kernel + training code)
solution_summary: The solution combined four global embedding models using two CNN backbones at two image resolutions, taking the geometric mean of their similarities. Training continued from retrieval checkpoints on 3.2 million images, with seesaw loss and higher resolution contributing to a five percentage point local validation improvement. SuperPoint and SuperGlue reranked retrieved candidates after HRNetv2 removed keypoints on irrelevant semantic classes. Local reranking improved public leaderboard scores by four to six percentage points, although its gains were difficult to validate locally.
