solution_summary: The author pretrained EfficientNet B5 and B4 on the 2015 competition data, then fine-tuned on an 85:15 split of the 2019 training data using 300×300 images. The pipeline treated severity prediction as regression with MSE loss, heavy augmentation, and checkpoint selection by kappa. Different preprocessing methods and flip/rotation test-time augmentation supported both single-model and ensemble predictions. The final submissions were the best single B5 model and a two-model B5 ensemble; an evaluated three-model ensemble achieved the highest reported private score of 0.9292.

solution_title: 6th Place Solution: Many model ensembles were detrimental?
solution_summary: The solution ensembled XGBoost and LightGBM with Optuna hyperparameter tuning. Training included the original dataset, and validation used five stratified folds. The author observed substantial randomness and strong performance from small ensembles or individual models. An existing notebook using recursive feature elimination with cross-validation inspired the approach, although the author did not explicitly claim to use that selection procedure.

The solution combined SE-ResNeXt-50 and SE-DenseNet-161 with PartialConv, using six folds with iterative stratification. Training proceeded through frozen-encoder, full-network, and tags-only stages, with gradient accumulation, learning-rate scheduling, label smoothing, and mixup. Separate validation-selected thresholds were applied to cultures and tags, and predictions were averaged across folds and checkpoints with flip augmentation. Manual cleaning mattered, while pseudo-labeling appeared prone to overfitting and a LightGBM second layer could not be deployed in time.

The team trained property-specific Uni-Mol models using competition data and five external datasets, removing training molecules that could not generate 3D conformations. Density and Rg were trained jointly, while FFV, Tc, and Tg had separate models. An XGBoost fallback handled test molecules that Uni-Mol v2 could not process, which was central to reaching approximately 0.063. Final submissions balanced stronger five-fold models against a faster configuration with fewer folds for some properties.
compute: RTX 4090 with 24 GB; increasing folds raised submission evaluation time from 1.5 to 2 hours.

solution_summary: The pipeline selected image pairs with EfficientNet, matched features with SuperPoint and SuperGlue, filtered matches with MAGSAC, and reconstructed scenes with pycolmap. Matching used three resolutions and five SuperGlue Sinkhorn iterations. Rotating poorly matched images and swapping pair order improved scores, while early termination on low-match pairs reduced test runtime to six hours. Adding LoFTR, DKM, or GlueStick did not improve reconstruction, and optical-flow filtering struggled with wide-baseline pairs.
compute: Test-data inference completed in 6 hours.

solution_summary: The author's solution relied entirely on a modified version of Miroslaw's Python code. The changes centered on feature selection, including a minimum improvement threshold and pruning previously selected variables after adding a new one. Categories with fewer than three cases were grouped as rare, and cross-validation used a 15% test split with median score aggregation. The code also supported randomized starts, optional reuse of selected predictors, and automatic multiprocessing to improve computation speed.

The solution used a causal language model to judge response pairs by comparing the logits of tokens A and B, with a chain-of-thought initial prompt. Post-pretraining used external preference data, full-vocabulary cross-entropy, reversed response pairs, and shorter inputs, followed by binary fine-tuning on competition-related data. Soft labels from three large teacher models and two fine-tuning epochs improved validation performance. Final inference used vLLM with constrained token outputs and GPTQ 8-bit quantization, achieving a reported private score of 0.714.
compute: 40 × A100 80GB GPUs provided as support.

solution_title: 16th Place Solution: CNN, Yolov5, and use image-wise model to predict the cell
solution_summary: The pipeline combined five cell-level EfficientNet models, three image-level EfficientNet models, and a YOLOv5 detector. Weighted averaging mixed cell predictions, image predictions, detector confidence, and image-model predictions on isolated cells. Square padding before resizing improved cell classification, while split-based pseudo-labeling addressed unreliable cell labels. CellSegmentator masks connected detector outputs to cells and enabled inference with all other cells masked out.

solution_title: 81st Place Solution for the "Linking Writing Processes to Writing Quality" Competition
solution_summary: The author extended a public solution with features measuring time between selected keyboard actions. These features were added to the Public LGBM and Writing Quality fusion components, while the LightAutoML plus LightGBM component was unchanged. The author selected the modified submission based on improved cross-validation despite a worse public score; the reported private score improved slightly from 0.56886 to 0.568179.

The solution combined five neural network variants with LightGBM and learned corrections to the neural predictions. Correction models used market-wide features for each time_id, reduced with PCA, to predict multiplicative adjustments. An additional correction ensemble used clustering-based splits to separate market conditions during training and validation. The final weighted ensemble achieved a reported public leaderboard score of 0.1953.

The final solution used a single nnUNet model initialized from weights trained on the earlier dataset. After the test-set correction, switching from precision-focused Tversky loss to Skeleton-Recall loss improved the score by 0.004. Post-processing removed small or incomplete sheets while preserving plausible edge and corner fragments, then applied tuned hysteresis. Hyperparameters were assessed on folds before fitting the final model on the full dataset.

solution_title: Simple linear regression for sigma (40th place)
solution_summary: The post describes uncertainty estimation for a constant predicted planetary spectrum. It repeatedly estimates the mean signal while excluding different nonoverlapping wavelength windows, then measures the standard deviation of those estimates. This variability correlates with spectrum prediction error and becomes an input to linear or quantile regression for sigma. The resulting mean and sigma can optionally be scaled across wavelengths using a prior distribution.

The final system stacked eight XGBoost models, four neural networks, GLMNET, and a random forest using a second-layer XGBoost trained on out-of-fold predictions. Feature engineering combined user dates and categorical indicators with extensive per-user session statistics, entropy measures, counts, durations, and proportions. Destination-specific helper features summed selected features whose destination means were unusually different. Action n-grams initially appeared unhelpful, but the strongest individual model on the private leaderboard used them.

solution_title: Two XGBoost models + rainfall fraction per group
solution_summary: The solution combined out-of-fold predictions from two XGBoost models trained on the competition and original datasets. Predictions from the original-data model received a weight of 0.3. Grouped mean, standard deviation, skewness, and rainfall-fraction features were added, with rainfall fraction especially influential. An inner/outer fold structure produced modest public performance but strong private performance.

The solution used residual 3D U-Nets to predict particle heatmaps from percentile-clipped, per-experiment standardized volumes. Constant-radius Gaussian targets, recall-focused weighted cross-entropy, and a second training dataset containing mined false positives were central to balancing recall and precision. Experiment-level validation informed an exponential learning-rate schedule for training on all seven experiments, producing a five-seed ensemble near epoch 40. Final detections used connected-component centroids and independently tuned particle thresholds, while non-maximum suppression and component-shape filtering were omitted after offering little improvement.

solution_title: 6th Place Solution for the March Machine Learning Mania 2024 Competition

The author manually classified men's matchups by location and added a five-percentage-point advantage when only one team was considered at home. More elaborate models had been explored previously, but time constraints led to this simple ratings-based submission. It achieved a private leaderboard score of 0.05564, with the code taking about one minute to run.

solution_summary: The solution combined aggregate game features, agent components, and features extracted from LudRules with LightGBM and CatBoost regressors. Features were selected separately within grouped folds, and model variants used different feature counts with or without fold-specific TF-IDF. The final submissions used weighted ensembles of either six models without TF-IDF or twelve models including TF-IDF, both scoring 0.437 on the private leaderboard. The author reported overfitting and questioned whether the game-result features introduced leakage.

solution_title: 34th place solution, end-to-end learning with a single neural net.
solution_summary: The post congratulates competitors and thanks contributors for starter scripts and advice. The author says they joined with one month remaining and relied heavily on those resources. It links to an external page without describing the solution in the provided text.

The final blend assigned 40% weight to a TF-IDF method averaging 2–5-gram variants and 60% to an ensemble dominated by 7B Mistral and Llama models. The best submission used an adversarially selected training dataset. A small language model trained on 10% of the data identified difficult examples in the remainder, which were mixed equally with the original PERSUADE dataset. This selection strategy was discovered late, so the final models were trained hastily on the last day.

The author describes separate approaches for several capture-the-flag challenges, including clustering with DBSCAN and KMeans and visualization with t-SNE. The Granny pipeline used MobileNet2 preprocessing, Torchattak, and postprocessing, while Semantile involved manual work and GloVe. Other challenges were addressed with a pickle serialization snippet and specific DNS-related prompts, although several solutions are only shown in images.

solution_title: 247th Place / Silver Medal — A CV-Robust Ensemble of Tabular Models, Local GR
solution_summary: The final solution blended five complementary trajectory estimates, led by a neural local GR refiner anchored to a tabular and physics ensemble. Robust polynomial projection, a semi-Markov decoder, an independent tree ensemble, and structural-surface-guided GR matching supplied additional paths. Well-level nested validation selected matcher variants and conservative nonnegative blend weights. The final pooled OOF RMSE was 8.4064 ft and private RMSE was 8.384 ft, with remaining error concentrated in a few catastrophic wells.

The pipeline used a lung localizer, EfficientDet-D5 disease detection, and separate classifiers to suppress detections on healthy images. Each image-annotation pair was treated independently, and detector outputs were ensembled with weighted boxes fusion. A blend of EfficientNet-B7 and ResNet200d classifiers supplied healthy/unhealthy probabilities that adjusted box confidence scores and added the no-finding prediction. This fusion improved CV from 0.36 to 0.47 and the private score from 0.219 to 0.297; YOLOv5 and external-data pseudo-labeling were unsuccessful.

The selected solution took the median predictions of 15 stratified-fold LightGBM regressors trained on the competition dataset. Inputs combined essay statistics, count-vectorizer features, Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings, and six writing-quality predictions from models trained on the ELL dataset. Five Bi-LSTM models produced those auxiliary features, with ONNX export substantially accelerating inference. The ELL features improved QWK by about 0.01, and the reported solution achieved CV 0.8172 and private score 0.817.

solution_summary: The submission used a single PyTorch BERT model, fine-tuning a SQuAD-trained whole-word-masking BERT-large checkpoint for one epoch at a learning rate of 3e-5. The pipeline removed HTML tags and heavily downsampled null training instances. Its loss combined start, end, and answer-class cross-entropy, giving answer-containing examples twice the weight. The author thanks the organizers and competitors for a challenging contest. They describe improving their public leaderboard score from around 0.9860 to nearly 0.9870. The post requests more solution sharing and provides no technical approach.

solution_title: GiGPO: A Thought Experiment at Kaggriculture
solution_summary: The approach combined macro farm-state planning with micro control of workers, tasks, and market actions. A spatial bottleneck transformer supplied global grid reasoning, while critic-free GiGPO training combined episode-level and intermediate-state economic credit. A routing heuristic handled final-day liquidation, leaving earlier days to the neural policy. Training exposed difficulty revisiting valuable intermediate states, motivating a proposed reverse curriculum.

solution_title: Would-be 39th place solution with single model (yolov4) from a first time competitor
solution_summary: The author describes a YOLOv4 pipeline, while noting that the team's two final submissions used EfficientDet. YOLOv4 was trained in Darknet at 704×704 resolution for 94 epochs, followed by a short 12-epoch pseudolabel training stage to limit overfitting without mosaic augmentation. Bayesian optimization, test-time augmentation, and weighted boxes fusion improved the reported YOLOv4 scores from 0.7115 public and 0.6371 private to 0.7406 public and 0.6625 private. Modified anchors and CutMix performed worse than the default configuration in cross-validation.

solution_summary: The pipeline generated up to 200 candidates using prioritized session items, covisitation, word2vec, and ALS strategies, then reranked them with separate XGBoost models for clicks, carts, and orders. Increasing candidate coverage and engineering session-position, candidate-rank, conversion, and recency features delivered the largest gains. Candidate generation achieved an overall local recall of 0.6573, while feature additions pushed the reported score to about 0.59. LightGBM ensembling and further tuning did not improve the leaderboard score, and Polars made feature generation faster and less memory intensive.

solution_summary: The team modified a public fingerspelling transcription notebook with coordinate normalization, motion and shape features, and temporal feature augmentation. They reduced the model dimension from 384 to 192, increased the convolution/transformer block count from three to ten, and added an auxiliary CTC loss. Supplementary-data pretraining, new features, and augmentation each reportedly improved the leaderboard score by about 0.01. Training used 100 epochs, batch size 256, and a learning rate of 0.01.

solution_title: Solution #35 : Whoa woke up to a massive jump in rankings!
solution_summary: The author built several classifiers using different combinations of the original and competition-provided data. They selected features, reduced dimensionality, and optimized hyperparameters before combining classifiers through voting. Classifiers trained on the combined original and provided data received less voting weight. The author later felt that relying on the original data alone might have been preferable.

The final submission ensembled eight customized GraphNet models. The main training intervention repeatedly removed training events with MAE above one and retrained when validation improved. Model changes included time-aware KNN construction, neighborhood sizes from 8 to 32, attention pooling, and PReLU activations. A single graph model scored 0.982 publicly and 0.984 privately, suggesting limited ensemble benefit; several alternative architectures and post-processing ideas failed.

solution_title: 13th place solution, Imitation learning with language modeling
solution_summary: The final agent used imitation learning, treating game actions as token sequences predicted by an encoder-decoder model. Custom tokenization encoded fleet destinations, split ship counts into two positions, and separated shipyard actions with a dedicated token. A pix2seq-style architecture combined board features from custom ConvNeXt blocks and toroidal convolutions with transformer encoding and decoding. Adding positional information at each attention layer improved convergence, and decoder inputs also included shipyard coordinates and sequence indices.

The solution used a three-stage pipeline: a pretrained 3D nnU-Net segmented C1–C7, a multitask 2.5D U-Net extracted slice embeddings, and an RNN with attention made downstream predictions. The segmentation model trained on 87 annotated cases achieved a Dice score of 0.95 and generated masks for cropping all 2,019 cases. The second stage combined three adjacent axial slices with vertebral-level information and learned five segmentation and classification tasks using bounding-box annotations. Training this stage beyond one epoch hurt downstream performance, while inference VRAM limits restricted ensembling to at most two folds.

solution_summary: The solution customized the previous year's winning image-matching pipeline, matching and correcting rotation for every image pair before clustering. Clusters were connected components of an inlier-count similarity graph after weak edges were removed, with isolated images and small components treated as outliers. Experiments with MASt3R-SfM and track refinement from VGGSfM or VGGT did not improve results.

The author used Gurobi 9.0 to solve a mixed-integer assignment model within narrow bounds around estimated daily occupancies. Those estimates came from a preliminary relaxation augmented with quadratic constraints that restricted occupancy mixtures to adjacent values. This reduced overly optimistic accounting costs and supplied useful occupancy targets before the preliminary model finished. The restricted MIP ran in under ten minutes on a MacBook, while producing the occupancy estimates took about 25 minutes. SCIP through OR-Tools had reached a score of 68910.94.

solution_summary: The pipeline combined chart classification, pix2pix-based segmentation and chart transformation, easyOCR, and extraction logic. Images were padded to squares and resized when necessary, with coordinates resized back during inference. Generating balanced synthetic charts substantially improved the simple CNN classifier, while scatter plots remained difficult because nearby points merged or were confused with noise and text. The solution scored 0.8 locally but could not exceed 0.58 on the leaderboard.

The team tuned public temporal 3D U-Net detection and transformer linking models, then extended the tracking graph with consolidation, mitosis detection, identity repair, and learned recentring. Conservative guards protected existing divisions and topology while learned CNN and LightGBM components repaired missed divisions, links, and positions. The final submissions scored 0.970 public and 0.946 private, with later repair stages contributing more on private than public. A major limitation was that full-chain validation used graphs from networks trained on the same videos, overstating private performance by about 0.03.

solution_summary: The solution ensembled 25 CatBoost models from five-fold stratified cross-validation repeated five times. It combined balanced class weights, metric-aware sample weighting for log loss, ordered boosting, and Stochastic Gradient Langevin Boosting. Optuna tuned parameters, while Bernoulli bootstrapping and row and column subsampling kept training practical. XGBoost, LightGBM, TabPFN blending, feature removal, and post-processing did not improve the approach.

solution_title: XGBoost in Compressed Space | 425th Place Solution Writeup for Open Problems – Single-Cell Perturbations
solution_summary: The solution compresses differential gene expression into 36 TruncatedSVD components and trains XGBoost to predict those components before inverse transformation. Features combine drug-specific averages over other cell types, target encodings, and indicators of which cell types contributed to the averages. Six-fold validation was used, with dimensionality reduction performed before splitting. The unensembled method reported public and private scores of 0.594 and 0.777 in about three minutes, with compression limiting the information it could recover.

solution_title: 20th place solution 🥈  - Ensemble of diverse DeBERTas and external data
solution_summary: The final solution averaged logits from seven fully fine-tuned DeBERTa V3 Large models with varied datasets, learning rates, and maximum sequence lengths. Training combined generated data from nbroad and mpware with competition data, while limiting external dataset size to avoid distribution shift. A 0.99 threshold on the O class provided the only final postprocessing. The strongest single model scored 0.967, and an unselected four-model ensemble achieved the author's best private score.

solution_title: source code & description, 66th place, R, glmnet + xgboost
solution_summary: This post is a collection of links for a Rossmann sales forecasting solution. It points to a detailed blog description, a short strategy document, and source code. No solution methods or experimental findings are included in the provided text.

The solution treated opacity detection as semantic segmentation, training three DeepLabV3+ variants with SE-ResNeXt101 or SENet backbones on resized or cropped images. Ellipses inscribed in the annotation boxes supplied segmentation targets, and training progressively introduced negative images and stronger augmentation. An ensemble averaged 90 predictions across architectures, folds, checkpoints, and input transformations. Thresholded masks became bounding boxes scored by their peak segmentation probability, with thresholds selected using public leaderboard feedback. The reported Stage 2 private score was 0.218, while a later image-resizing experiment reached 0.234.

The team blended individual models, including the author's LightGBM model using passband feature ratios, adjusted sample weights, and 55 selected features. The main contribution described is class-specific probability scaling tuned on out-of-fold predictions, followed by row normalization. This improved the author's CV loss from 0.52 to 0.493 and public score from 0.968 to 0.915. A final confidence-based probability adjustment further improved the team submission from 0.854 to 0.851 publicly and from 0.87021 to 0.86777 privately.

The solution combined public notebooks into a retrieval and selective reranking pipeline. For each comment, it retrieved two semantically similar positive examples and two negative examples, then ran three models with four variations of example context. Qwen2.5-32B handled only the 20% of test rows where the initial predictions were uncertain. Predictions were ranked within each rule before averaging to match the competition's rule-specific AUC metric.

The solution adapted public notebooks with changes motivated by anticipated distribution drift. It used time-grouped validation, joint train/test normalization and quantile transformation, and 15 k-means label features, while removing stock_id from one blended model. Three LightGBM seeds were blended with weights estimated from validation scores. Several changes worsened public performance but were considered possible contributors to better private performance; price-amplitude augmentation did not work.

solution_title: #13: U900 team - PYBOOST is what you need
solution_summary: The team combined multi-target PYBOOST models with several neural-network families, emphasizing target encoding and ensemble diversity. Neural variants included learned SMILES embeddings, separate prediction of three gene clusters, and features derived from aggregated raw RNA counts through PCA and target encoding. Raw-count features contributed diversity rather than stronger standalone performance, while chemical descriptors and pretrained chemical embeddings were excluded from the final ensemble. The report attributes stability to careful validation and diversity control, reporting a public-private score correlation of 0.98.

solution_title: 4th Place Solution: Stabilizing Convergence in Understanding Clouds
solution_summary: The final system averages seven folds of EfficientNet-B4-FPN and three folds of Resnet34-ASPP segmentation models. Training stability under noisy rectangular labels was the main concern, addressed through RAdam, initial BCE training followed by Symmetric Lovasz fine-tuning, and pseudo-labeling on all test images. Training and inference use flip augmentations, with additional geometric augmentation during training. Predictions use a shared 0.4 threshold and a minimum mask size of 5,000 pixels; separate false-positive classifiers were discarded because their cross-validation performance was unstable.

solution_summary: The project provides an open U-Net-based pipeline for salt identification, including metadata preparation, training, evaluation, and inference. It exposes experiments through optional Neptune tracking and provides cross-validation execution. Nine reported solution versions improve the listed leaderboard score from 0.745 to 0.849, with the last version reporting CV of 0.853. The text provides setup instructions but few architectural or training details.

The team retrained a public image model for five epochs and selected the best five folds to generate out-of-fold predictions. These predictions became an additional feature in a public LightGBM, CatBoost, and XGBoost pipeline. The reported scores were 0.177 for cross-validation, 0.178 on the public leaderboard, and 0.169 on the private leaderboard.

solution_title: Lost my silver medal and my first lesson on trusting public LB 😥
solution_summary: The author describes submission selection and validation mistakes without specifying the underlying models. They selected submissions by leaderboard performance and did not evaluate ensembles with cross-validation. The disappointing final outcome led them to emphasize the need for proper validation.

The final solution equally averaged character-level predictions from six DeBERTa models. Continued masked language modeling on all patient notes used a corrected token-logit computation and achieved 75–85% masked-token accuracy. Manually correcting roughly 120 noisy annotations improved scores by about 0.003, alongside multi-sample dropout, random masking, and added newline tokens. The ensemble scored 0.889 publicly and 0.890 privately, although feature-text mismatches and omitted models limited the final submission.

solution_summary: The solution trains two nnUNet 3D full-resolution models for 2000 epochs with different patch sizes. Training resumes from checkpoints iteratively to identify models with strong cross-validation scores. Their probability maps are averaged with weights 0.7 and 0.3, followed by topology post-processing with adjusted thresholds and component settings. The larger-patch model performed better privately despite weaker public performance.

solution_title: 23rd private (1437th public, 4 submissions total) - regular expressions
solution_summary: The solution used a rule-based procedure to extract dataset names from text. It searched for five trigger words and examined five words on each side for capitalized words. It retained sequences longer than two words and added labels found from the training dataset. The post provided a notebook link but no evaluation scores.

The pipeline first trained all 11 targets, then specialized the model into ETT, NGT, and CVC experts before fine-tuning each expert on pseudo-labeled NIH images. Auxiliary line segmentation and endpoint or anatomical landmark regression encouraged the network to focus on relevant structures. NIH images were deduplicated against competition training data and filtered by predicted line presence before pseudo-labeling. Four trained fold models used three ResNet200d backbones and one EfficientNet-B7 at 672×672 resolution, achieving CV 0.9712 and private leaderboard 0.9756.

solution_title: Two main tricks helped us to avoid the shake
solution_summary: The post describes an ensemble that augments each model's predictions with their ranks computed jointly over training and test predictions. Standardized ensemble features feed a ridge regression with leave-one-out cross-validation for regularization selection. The authors identify cross-validated ensembling as the main reason their submissions avoided a leaderboard shake-up. H2O AutoML is also reported to perform well for ensembling.

solution_title: # 40th public → 2000th private: an exact LB instrument aimed at the wrong target
solution_summary: The author built a prediction stack on public notebook artifacts, adding spatial components and roughly twenty leaderboard-fitted correction constants. Despite improving public RMSE from 6.358 to 5.799, the final private RMSE worsened from 9.443 to 9.520. By-well validation exposed useful model diversity, but public-score tuning suppressed a spatial model that later proved valuable privately. The writeup attributes the failure to a small effective number of wells, repeated leaderboard fitting, and comparisons against baselines that differed from the deployed artifacts.

The solution combined lung and tissue segmentation with rich features extracted from CT scans. The authors considered segmentation quality and CT-derived features the main factors behind their results. They used robust cross-validation and an ensemble of 10 models. Their lung segmentation extended a community notebook with tweaks and added tissue segmentation.

The final translator used a single ByT5-base model with averaged checkpoints and beam-search decoding. DeepSeek-assisted sentence splitting aligned training examples with test granularity, while Gemini translations of published texts provided the largest improvement. Gemini-generated synthetic pairs, transliteration normalization, and higher weighting of gold data supplied further gains. The final model achieved 38.9 private and 38.3 public scores.
compute: Single GPU on AutoDL; five training epochs; four weeks of experimentation.

solution_summary: The author encoded order-book and trade data as 60 ten-second intervals and processed these sequences with an LSTM–Dense–GRU network. A separate recurrent model supplied stock-time embeddings, which an attention mechanism combined across other stocks at the same time. These representations, aggregate market features, and one-hot stock identifiers were concatenated into an MLP. Cross-stock attention improved the score by about 0.002, and inference used the 40th percentile of predictions from five folds grouped by time identifier.

The solution used a late interaction mechanism to approximate pairwise toxicity comparisons efficiently, with Muppet RoBERTa Large as the backbone. Pseudo-labels from earlier competition datasets and public notebooks supplied more than 20 labels per comment. Training combined Dice loss, large batches, mixed precision, cyclic learning rates, weight averaging, and EMA. Late interaction raised the public score from 0.844 to 0.872, but its private-score benefit was smaller.
compute: TPU training; RoBERTa Large on 200k+ comments took under 5 minutes per epoch with batch size 512 and mixed precision.

The post gives a high-level outline without specifying individual vision architectures or training details.

solution_title: BirdCLEF 2026: A Multi-Branch Ensemble Solution (60th Place Private LB)
solution_summary: The final system combined Perch embeddings with a ProtoSSM correction branch, retrained SED models, and multiple EfficientNet branches. Pseudo-labeling supplied additional training data and diversity, including a Noisy Student model with confidence filtering and sampling. Branch outputs were blended in rank space, then adjusted through conservative gating and taxonomic smoothing. The submission scored 0.955 publicly and 0.948 privately, but leaderboard-guided weight selection lacked systematic local optimization.

The solution averages 16 EfficientNet B7/B8 classifiers trained on the full competition training set at image sizes of 896 or 1024. An auxiliary U-Net segmentation head regularizes training using available line annotations, while only the classification head is retained for inference. Stratified five-fold validation guided model selection and correlated well with leaderboard results. Aspect-ratio-aware cropping, image inversion, and other augmentations supported training without external data.

solution_title: Silver zone solo, no credits used.
solution_summary: The solution combined three single-frame classifiers with an LRCNN using an EfficientNetB1 backbone and three consecutive frames. The author emphasized balanced random sampling of real and fake faces each epoch, with at most one fake video per source real video, and a fixed folder-based validation split. Inference classified 20 frames per video and aggregated their predictions by the median, while the final ensemble weighted the single-frame models at 0.85 and the LRCNN at 0.15. Reported validation scores were approximately 0.22–0.25, with training taking 1–1.5 hours per model on a local GTX 1080 Ti.

solution_title: Third (3rd) Place solution (Technique that worked out and Lessons learnt so far)
solution_summary: The author selected three of their own submission files that strongly favored Class_2 and ensembled them. The resulting submission scored 1.08514 on the public leaderboard and 1.08769 on the private leaderboard.

solution_title: 12th place- predict joint probabilities for start & end indices
solution_summary: The solution ensembled two RoBERTa-based models and benefited from initialization with SQuAD2-fine-tuned weights. A modified head predicted joint start/end logits for every possible span instead of independent endpoint distributions. This enabled decoding by maximizing expected Jaccard score, reportedly adding about 0.003. Additional post-processing contributed about 0.008, while ensembling added about 0.004.

solution_title: Rank 83rd Silver Solution: DINOv2/3 + Depth Fusion with Uncertainty Calibration
solution_summary: The solution fused DINO RGB features with EfficientNet depth features through learned gates and attention pooling. Its final ensemble combined a two-tile DINOv2 Large configuration with an eight-tile DINOv3 Large configuration. Training used LoRA, uncertainty-aware regression, stratified cross-validation, and cosine-restart snapshots. Test-time batch-normalization adaptation, augmentation, OOF calibration, and physical consistency refinement completed the pipeline; reported public and private scores were 0.74 and 0.62.

The solution used a Transformer-style landmark model with 90 keypoints and 1,050 distance, motion, and acceleration features. Videos were center-cropped to 256 frames, normalized by landmark groups, and augmented with flips. Training combined cross-entropy, label smoothing, and an epoch-dependent dropout schedule. The PyTorch model was converted through ONNX to TFLite, with FP16 quantization producing an approximately 26 MB model and a reported runtime of about 60 minutes for five folds.
compute: Approximately 60 minutes for five folds; hardware and runtime phase unspecified.

solution_summary: The solution combined MultinomialNB, SGDClassifier, LightGBM, and CatBoost using a VotingClassifier. Their respective ensemble weights were 0.09, 0.42, 0.27, and 0.94, and the vocabulary size was set to 15 million. Based on a public notebook, the approach achieved a public score of 0.963 and a private score of 0.901.

The author trained a baseline on the entire dataset for 11 epochs using cross-entropy, small augmentations, half-resolution images, gradient accumulation, and cosine learning-rate annealing. Most gains came from adjusting output probabilities to compensate for class frequency and match the expected test class counts. Repeated damped count adjustments raised the score to about 0.74, and horizontal flipping added approximately 0.005. Training itself did not explicitly address class imbalance.
compute: Borrowed 1080Ti for an extended weekend; trained 11 epochs.

solution_summary: The final submission combined LightGBM and logistic regression, selected using out-of-fold validation performance. Product and ratio interactions, compact feature subsets selected through IV/WoE and target permutation importance, and sample weighting were central to the approach. Training used repeated stratified cross-validation, and individual model instances were weighted by inverse validation balanced log loss during inference. The selected ensemble scored 0.1752 CV, 0.1717 public, and 0.4197 private, while an unselected XGBoost submission achieved a better private score of 0.3679.

solution_title: Rank 318 Solution: Replay-Efficient Confused Deputy Search
solution_summary: The final approach specialized in Confused Deputy behavior using short, single-message delegation prompts that induced an email action. Six templates and distinct recipient addresses created diverse scoring cells, and execution traces filtered out unsuccessful candidates. A warm-up interaction and adaptive latency estimates controlled generation under a 950-candidate ceiling, using the same strategy for GPT-OSS and Gemma. The post also describes an unsuccessful broader capability-discovery approach with source profiling and a contextual Q learner.

The approach used nested leave-one-year-out validation to guide model-specific feature engineering and tuning. Adversarial validation motivated removing time features when adding the original dataset, while ratio and annual-relative temperature features improved multiple model families. The selected submissions averaged either LightGBM, random forest, and logistic regression, or four untuned tree models, with the latter achieving 0.90282 privately. A separately reported rank ensemble of XGBoost and LightGBM achieved 0.90669 privately but was not selected by local or public leaderboard performance.

DINOv3 provided the primary biomass predictions by processing two image halves and fusing their representations with a Mamba layer. SigLIP supplied semantic guidance through image-to-text similarity scores. The final blend favored DINOv3, and clover predictions came directly from that branch. Constraint-based post-processing enforced consistent sums among biomass components.

The solution used ImageNet-pretrained six-channel CNNs with combined ArcFace and cross-entropy training, followed by plate-aware linear sum assignment. Progressive pseudo-labeling added confident test examples every epoch while preserving class uniqueness within each plate. The final ensemble contained six DenseNet161 and five DenseNet201 models with flip, rotation, and crop-resize TTA, achieving 0.99763 private and 0.99480 public scores. A reference-image conditioning approach failed to improve ordinary classification.

The solution converts audio into spectrograms and extracts interesting patches through image processing. Template matching generates features, which are merged with the supplied segment histograms and location information before training random forest regressors. Submission files are exported when cross-validation AUC exceeds 0.93. The supplied settings reportedly produce a private leaderboard score around 0.954.
compute: Intel Core i5 2500, 16 GB RAM, Windows 7; template matching feature generation takes 10–12 hours and can run in parallel.

solution_summary: The author combined a custom floor predictor with diverse public coordinate predictions and extensive postprocessing. Coordinate bias correction, snapping predictions to known locations, cost minimization, and temporal leakage methods drove improvements. Blending predictions from different origins and repeatedly applying postprocessing kept the approach roughly 0.4 metres ahead of the best public notebook. Changing the postprocessing order produced a final improvement, and the two selected submissions used different floor models.

solution_title: Released: my Source Code and Analysis
solution_summary: The post announces a GitHub repository containing the author's code and analysis. It describes implementations of Elo, Glicko, Chessmetrics, and an experimentation framework for improving rating systems. It does not explain the submitted approach or report which experiments worked.

The author trained collections of LightGBM, CatBoost, and decision-tree models with different swap-noise perturbations and mixed their predictions. The best local submission was blended with other participants' DAE and AutoWoe predictions. The shared notebook was reported to score 0.81325 on the private leaderboard. The author was uncertain whether swap noise was enabled in the best submission, so its contribution remains unclear.

This notebook provides an updated Rock-Paper-Scissors testing dojo built from public agents rather than describing a final submitted agent. It standardizes agents as classes, supplies a local evaluator, and organizes opponents by complexity and performance. The included baselines exploit move frequencies, transition probabilities, and recurring action-history patterns, alongside random opponents. Performance coefficients control evaluation effort, and slow multi-armed-bandit meta-agents are excluded.

solution_summary: The final solution used DenseNet169 on 1024-pixel images, trained across five folds for 50 epochs three times. A sampler selected images with masks 60% of the time, and training combined BCE, Dice, and focal losses with Adam and cosine annealing. DenseNet169 and DPN92 performed best, but DPN92 was excluded because of its large model files. The models were not retrained on the new second-stage training set.

The solution distilled an XGB teacher into the competition-provided RandomForest by training the forest on the teacher's training predictions. Both models used three selected input columns, while XGB additionally received an oxygen mean feature. Threshold-based outlier removal and selective replacement of low oxygen values with missing values improved training data quality. The forest retained a reported 88–90% of the teacher's effectiveness in cross-validation, while IsolationForest filtering performed poorly.

The author implemented seven binary logistic regression models from scratch, one for each fertilizer class. Each model estimated a class probability using a sigmoid and was trained by gradient descent on binary log-loss. L2 regularization penalized large weights to reduce overfitting. The approach supplied probabilities for the competition's ordered three-fertilizer prediction task, but the writeup provided no validation or final score.
compute: One CPU core per one-versus-all sub-model.

solution_summary: The team built two large transaction feature sets using aggregations, categorical frequencies, sequence embeddings, and historical-versus-new transaction interactions. Pairing weakly correlated features and filtering features by missingness, correlation, uniqueness, and model importance improved validation. Around 32 diverse tree models were stacked using Bayesian regression, reaching approximately 3.630 validation RMSE and 3.675 public leaderboard RMSE. An outlier module intersected the top 100 predictions from four classifiers to select 21 outliers, improving the public score to 3.666; both chosen submissions scored about 3.599 privately.

solution_title: Homesite Quote Conversion, Winners' Interview: 2nd Place, Team Frenchies | Nicolas, Florian, & Pierre
solution_summary: The team built approximately 600 diverse base models using several model families, feature representations, and column subsets. Engineered features included row counts, dimensionality reductions, cluster IDs, and feature differences. Five-fold stratified validation supported stacking with logistic regression, XGBoost, and bagged neural networks. The final prediction averaged the ranks of these three blends, which each outperformed the best individual model.

solution_title: Solution Write-up: Unleashing the Healing Potential: Abdominal Trauma
solution_summary: The post describes a tabular exploratory analysis of organ health and injury labels rather than a detailed CT-image prediction pipeline. It cleans the data, examines injury prevalence and correlations, and uses K-means to identify healthy and injured patient clusters. Random Forest, SVM and Gradient Boosting models were evaluated for accuracy, with Random Forest reported at 96%. The validation design and a final competition submission pipeline are not specified.

solution_title: Yirun's Solution (1st place): Training Supervised Autoencoder with MLP
solution_summary: The final submission blended a supervised autoencoder MLP with teammates' XGBoost models. The autoencoder and prediction network were trained jointly within each purged time-series fold to avoid validation label leakage. Multiple response targets, response-magnitude sample weights, and averaged predictions across targets and seeds supported the neural approach. Only models from the last two folds were retained, and the standalone AE-MLP achieved a private leaderboard score of 6022.202.

The solution combined four models with small differences in architecture and target cleaning, assigning extra weight to the fourth model. Its main improvement came from identifying how extra spaces in the original text caused systematic offsets in annotated answer spans. One model reversed this corruption during preprocessing, and final postprocessing reproduced the expected span offsets. The ensemble scored 0.723 publicly before postprocessing and 0.731 publicly and 0.729 privately afterward.

The solution used a transformer with three layers and an embedding size of 480, adapted from public kernels. It standardized each sign sequence using its own mean and standard deviation and engineered distances among approximately 106 selected landmarks. Augmentations such as flipping and concatenation improved cross-validation performance from about 0.76 to 0.78, while increasing model size brought single-model public leaderboard performance to around 0.80. Adversarial weight perturbation, random frame masking, and exponential moving averages helped control overfitting.

The solution treated tissue tiles as sequences, combining an ImageNet-pretrained DenseNet121 feature extractor with two GRU layers to regress ISUP grade using log-cosh loss. Whole-slide rotation, 256 × 256 tissue extraction, and normalization across each image's tiles formed the preprocessing pipeline. Image-hash similarity clusters were kept together during five-fold validation, with Gleason score frequencies balanced across splits. Training alternated frozen and unfrozen backbone stages with different sequence lengths, used batches of two, and repeatedly discarded images whose prediction error exceeded 2.5.

Separate LightGBM models predicted production and consumption through normalized differences from their targets two days earlier. Features combined calendar information, normalized target lags and differences, weather forecasts, historical weather, and weekday/weekend aggregates. Validation used January through May 2023, followed by full-data training with two seeds per task. Feature importance limited production to 300 features and consumption to 400, and both models were retrained at three points during inference.

solution_title: 1st place solution models (it’s not all BirdNet)
solution_summary: The author trained sound-event detection models with EfficientNet and NFNet backbones, contributing them to a final blend that also included BirdNet. Training used 15-second audio chunks, secondary labels, noise augmentation, and weighting to address class imbalance. Pretraining on both competition years was followed by fine-tuning on recordings containing scored birds. Centered five-second inference and checkpoint averaging helped, while fixed thresholds worked better for ensembles than quantile thresholds. Both reported backbones achieved a private score of 0.78.

solution_title: Ideas unnoticed on the forum before
solution_summary: The author generated 200 spatial features by measuring pickup and dropoff distances to 100 cluster centers. These features substantially helped, but expanded the training data to 5 GB, which they could train only with LightGBM. Other models received 10 PCA components instead. Coordinate-only nearest-neighbor models with 15, 30, and 45 neighbors were also used in the stack, with 45 neighbors performing best.

solution_title: 7th place solution with no external training data
solution_summary: The author generated soft labels through three GPT-6 astra image-and-report reading protocols, corrected site-dependent Synovitis bias, and blended the result with cross-model teachers. A multiview 2.5D network combined spatially aligned tokens with label-query and attention-MIL heads, using EfficientNetV2-S and ConvNeXt backbones. Label improvements contributed more than architectural changes, while the four-model rank ensemble offered little private-score benefit. The best single model reached 0.958 private AUC, compared with 0.957 for the selected ensembles.

solution_summary: The solution combined 21 models using target-specific weighted averaging optimized with Nelder–Mead. Preserving capitalization, prepending target names, and replacing line breaks with [Chapter] improved cross-validation. Adversarial weight perturbation, larger fold counts, and two pseudo-labeling pipelines using Feedback Prize and CommonLit data also helped. The author reported a best listed individual-model private score of 0.4378 and found several post-processing and architecture additions ineffective.

solution_summary: The solution used a two-stage text-normalization pipeline. XGBoost first classified whether each word required changing using two context words on either side. Words requiring normalization were passed to a character-input sequence-to-sequence model built around a memory-augmented neural network. Training lasted four epochs, and resource constraints prevented completing hyperparameter optimization, so the model retained the research paper's parameter settings.

solution_summary: The author built a rule-based agent that scored factory locations using resource access, rubble, open areas, and nearby factories, then adjusted bidding to the quality of available positions. During play, it projected bot positions, canceled conflicting plans, and reassigned actions through a priority scheme. Its broader strategy balanced economic development with attacks on vulnerable enemies and targeted rubble clearing. A late shift toward solar power remained insufficiently polished, while bot congestion and expensive computation limited planning and experimentation.

solution_title: Like Popping Bubble-Wrap: Keith T. Herring on Placing Second in Wikipedia's Participation Challenge
solution_summary: The solution scraped editing histories for approximately one million Wikipedia editors and derived 206 behavioral features. It generated roughly 3,000 randomized decision-tree models with varying random forest parameters. An iterative quadratic optimizer used out-of-bag predictions to select and weight 34 complementary models. Exponentially decayed edit volume with an 80-day half-life was the strongest feature.

solution_summary: The final solution blended two public notebook approaches with the author's own four-fold DeBERTa-v3 base and large models. The three components received weights of 0.8, 0.1, and 0.1, with the second component restricted to its SVR models. Layer-wise decreasing learning rates helped the author's fine-tuning. Metric learning, T5 encoders, further pretraining, target reassignment, GPT-2 likelihood features, and a random-forest vocabulary estimator did not work.

The author shares a competition notebook built on public starter notebooks. The post credits other contributors and presents its strategy through an embedded image whose contents are unavailable in the supplied text. It explicitly says the alpha binary-search questioner was not used. Further implementation details were promised but are absent here.

The team submitted two separate ensembles: SE-ResNeXt101 with mit_b2, and EfficientNet with SE-ResNeXt. The first approach stabilized training with gradient accumulation to an effective batch size of 128, stronger augmentation, and 1024-pixel training images, achieving 0.586 privately. The second used kidney detection and segmentation to accelerate vessel inference and suppress predictions outside the kidney, achieving 0.519 privately. Mirror padding and morphological repair improved its predictions, while stronger augmentation and pseudo-labeling were excluded after validation and public-score declines.

The writeup describes a candidate-generation and ranking pipeline with 50 co-visitation candidates and user, item, and interaction features. Its LightGBM ranker used LambdaRank, NDCG at 20, DART boosting, and 200 estimators. The author reported that heuristics finally surpassed the ranker after adding co-visitation features and expanding candidates to the top 50. Future-action features and Optuna did not help.

solution_summary: The pipeline denoised acoustic signals with discrete wavelets and generated quantile-crossing features across multiple decomposition levels and wavelet lengths. Spectrum statistics, peak counts, and autocorrelation features supplemented these inputs to LightGBM. Shuffled folds stratified by time and earthquake guided feature development, with nested validation added later. solution_summary: The final submission combined a regularized generalized linear model, a random forest, and bagged linear support vector machines using a weighted average. solution_title: Long live Wikipedia: Dell Zhang on placing third in Wikipedia's Participation Challenge
solution_summary: The solution modeled recent changes in users' edit counts and numbers of edited articles. Choosing suitable temporal scales made these behavioral dynamics highly predictive. OpenCV's gradient boosted trees outperformed the other tested methods, with parameters tuned on a large validation dataset shared by another participant.

solution_summary: The solution used a two-stage pipeline combining a 3D U-Net ensemble with heuristic probability extraction. A ResNet3D backbone predicted 13 heatmaps supervised by Gaussian kernels centered on aneurysm coordinates. Non-maximum suppression identified peaks, and candidates below the top three were suppressed with an exponent of 1.5 before computing an overall presence probability. Five-fold validation scored approximately 0.75, while both public and private leaderboard scores were 0.73.

solution_summary: The solution combined a pretrained wav2vec2 speech recognition model with a six-gram KenLM language model. ASR training began with Common Voice, Fleur, and Bn data, followed by stages described as using 10% and 20% data. Audio augmentation included speed, volume, reverberation, and noise changes, and training used learning-rate warmup. Inference applied Bengali character-combination corrections, while the language model used competition text and external training data.

solution_summary: A shared-backbone XLM-RoBERTa-large biencoder retrieved 50 content candidates, followed by a multilingual BERT crossencoder trained on out-of-fold retrieval results. Language-matched batches and candidates, bidirectional cross-entropy, and a positive-class margin improved retrieval, reaching 91% recall@50 on CV. Positive oversampling and differential learning rates improved the crossencoder, which achieved 63.6% CV and 68.3% private leaderboard scores. Post-processing supplied a nearest neighbor for empty predictions and reused contents from matching topic hierarchies.

The solution used a GRU encoder-decoder with explicit seasonal lags and page-level features to forecast web traffic. Lagged observations outperformed the more complex attention approach and allowed shorter encoders. Training used random temporal windows, a smoothed SMAPE loss, and COCOB with gradient clipping. Walk-forward validation guided tuning, while final models trained without validation. Averaging 30 checkpoints across three seeds, with averaged weights within each checkpoint, reduced variance and produced future-data SMAPE similar to historical validation.

The solution used XGBoost trained on June and December 2015 accounts that added products. Eleven months of lagged product ownership and other engineered features were central to the approach. A 100-model ensemble provided only a small additional gain. The author also provided runnable binary and multiclass single-model variants reported to exceed 0.0305 on the public leaderboard.

solution_title: A throughput floor plus a genuine multi-step search
solution_summary: The author built a three-phase attack search guided by direct inspection of the competition SDK and hosted gateway code. It allocated budget to a public guardrail argument-ordering exploit, a confused-deputy mechanism, and novelty-driven exploration of fixture cross-references. The best public score was 19.560, but the private score was 0.030, attributable to one surviving confused-deputy finding. Benign priming and reward-weighted archive selection were tested and reverted after lowering public scores.

The final speech recognition pipeline combined a single Wave2Vec model with an N-gram language model. An initial model trained on external speech datasets identified noisy competition samples, excluding those with WER above 0.5 before a longer training stage. Dataset caching, increased warmup, and an MSD output layer helped, while additional fine-tuning led to overfitting. Adding the language model improved the reported public leaderboard score from 0.407 to 0.396.

The solution emphasized diversity by combining nine 2.5D segmentation models trained along three axes with three 3D models. Validation used five folds grouped by case. Averaging model outputs and applying a 0.3 threshold improved the public score from a best single-model score of 0.875 to 0.889. Removing predictions smaller than 50 pixels increased it to 0.890.

solution_summary: The solution trains XGBoost with both competition data and original data while controlling their distribution mismatch through sample weights. Original observations receive prognosis-dependent weights to reproduce the competition data's prognosis distribution. A grid-searched multiplier further controls the relative contribution of the two sources, and weights are also supplied to evaluation sets. Original data supports fitting and early stopping but is excluded from model selection; the author reports that one submission performed well on both public and private evaluations.

The solution combined DeBERTa-v3-large models trained on different mixtures of competition and external data. Overlapping tokenizer windows covered long essays while word IDs mapped predictions back to essay tokens. A fixed holdout guided model-specific thresholds, after which voting combined the models. Custom synthetic data, Longformer, LLM predictions, weighted averaging, and class-weighted losses did not help.

The solution used three levels of models to detect six movement events from EEG while preserving temporal causality. Subject-specific first-level models extracted covariance, evoked-potential, and low-frequency signal information. Global second-level models learned event relationships and temporal structure from prediction histories, with bagging improving robustness. AUC-optimized weighted ensembles formed the third level, and the final YOLO submission averaged 18 such ensembles, achieving 0.98109 private AUC.

solution_title: 4th Place Solution - Split images into tiles and do 3D CNN
solution_summary: The solution removed large white background regions from very large pathology images before splitting them into tiles. A 3D CNN learned from the resulting tiles. The author reported stable local cross-validation without post-processing.

solution_title: 38th place (silver): what actually moved the score
solution_summary: The solution improved report-derived targets by applying clinical thresholds and distinguishing below-threshold findings from explicit negatives and omissions. A training-only site bias absorbed reporting habits, while complementary whole-knee and landmark-crop models supplied different anatomical views. Conservative nested validation screened changes before a percentile-rank ensemble combined surviving model legs with timeout protection. The reported final scores were 0.964 public and 0.952 private.

The solution combined EEG signals with supplied and EEG-derived spectrograms in three models: EfficientNet-B1, ResNet-1D plus EfficientNet-B1, and WaveNet plus EfficientNet-B1. Training used patient-grouped five-fold validation, two-stage training, label refinement, and CutMix. The three model predictions were combined with weights of 0.34, 0.32, and 0.34. Teacher and student models were both retained to mitigate possible drift from two-stage training, with reported public scores of 0.29 and 0.27.

The solver served gpt-oss-120b through vLLM and generated eight independently seeded, Python-enabled attempts per problem. Minimal prompts replaced elaborate reasoning scaffolds, while inverse-entropy voting selected answers and four matching attempts triggered early stopping. Adaptive time budgets gave difficult problems additional time within the notebook limit. The public score rose from 40/50 to 45/50 after prompt and configuration changes, with no isolated attribution; retries and several verifier-based pipelines did not improve the final configuration.

solution_summary: The solution blended many Regularized Greedy Forest tree ensembles using a generalized linear model with exponential loss and nonnegative coefficients. It mostly retained the supplied features, added features from new particle combinations, accounted for physical symmetries, and removed unhelpful phi features. Submodels estimated either the weighted signal-to-background ratio directly or its class-probability and conditional-weight components separately. The two target formulations performed similarly individually, while blending them gave the best results; the blend was fitted on seven-fold out-of-fold predictions.

solution_summary: The solution combined an EfficientNet-B6 binary classifier with YOLOv5, EfficientD6, and VFNet detectors. Weighted boxes fusion consolidated training boxes, and customized fusion at postprocessing improved mAP by 0.015. YOLOv5 training used multiple mosaic variants and quadruple mean teachers with a ramped consistency-loss weight. The classifier achieved AUC 0.992 and AP 0.96, while mean teachers improved detection cross-validation by about 0.02 mAP but added little ensemble diversity.

solution_title: Jack of Trades, Loser of Cryptarithm
solution_summary: The writeup describes synthetic problem generation and structured reasoning traces, reserving all supplied training examples for validation. Generators reproduce observed ranges, noise, vocabulary, and problem formats across five puzzle families. The most detailed work constructs byte-consistent bit-manipulation reasoning using primitive operators, valid continuations, and compact encodings. An initial exhaustive reasoning format performed poorly through hallucinated rules and fallback answers; the excerpt ends with formatting revisions rather than a complete final training recipe.

solution_title: Megatron: LoRA Fine-Tuning of Nemotron-3-Nano-30B for Structured Reasoning
solution_summary: The author fine-tunes Nemotron-3-Nano-30B using rank-32 LoRA initialized from Kien's public tinker-adapter. Conservative delta scaling anchors updates to the initial adapter, and Unsloth supports training with offline dependencies and fallback Mamba operations. The short 150-step run achieved 0.86, compared with 0.85 for a 3,000-step run using broader adapter training and cosine decay. Local generation validation failed because of GPU memory pressure, making competition evaluation the source of reported accuracy.

solution_title: 15th place solution - Don't Test At Home
solution_summary: The agent uses an Extra Trees-style ensemble inspired by an earlier decision-tree agent. It fits randomized trees with one candidate feature for as much of each turn's time budget as possible. An internal timer limits fitting to the first 950 milliseconds, adapting the number of trees to server load and fitting cost. Accumulated tree probabilities then weight random action selection.
compute: 950 milliseconds of tree fitting per turn; tree counts varied from 100 to over 800 with server load and fitting steps.

solution_title: Public -> 254 rank, Private -> 42 rank, and Potential Top 15 solution
solution_summary: The submitted approach stacked nine AutoGluon models with a RidgeClassifier and combined the resulting predictions by mode. The AutoGluon models used different collections of CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM models. A basic CatBoost baseline treated every feature as a string without cleaning and achieved mean out-of-fold accuracy of 0.94059 across 15 folds. An alternative AutoGluon stack using 24 base models trained over 20 folds was evaluated but not selected.

solution_title: 8th place solution. And gold on last attempt
solution_summary: The solution ensembled sound event detection models with an EfficientNet-B0 backbone across several preprocessing and training variants. Manual removal of segments without bird sounds, audio chunking, secondary-label targets, and inference-time class weights improved the earlier models. A later variant used normalized Kaldi filterbank features, random five-second crops, per-class sampling, and scheduled mixup, followed by mean-median aggregation and class-specific prediction boosts. The final submission averaged the best previous ensemble with a model trained on confidence-filtered recordings, achieving a private score of 0.79 compared with 0.78 for the previous best.

The final submission closely followed a public notebook, replacing DeBERTa-v3-base with DeBERTa-v3-large. Training ran in Google Colab. Masked-language-model training, adding prompt material to the input, and feeding manual features into the NLP head did not help. The author identified the small number of training prompts and the absence of shared prompt IDs between training and test data as central challenges.
compute: Training performed in a Google Colab notebook; hardware and duration unspecified.

solution_title: 6th place solution in 3 days - AutoGluon + AutoXGB
solution_summary: The solution combined AutoGluon pipelines with an independently tuned XGBoost model using weights based on cross-validation scores. One AutoGluon pipeline used eight folds and one stacking level, while another used pseudo-labels from the first models. Both the original and generated datasets were used. AutoGluon training took about 13 hours, and XGBoost hyperparameter tuning took about 24 hours.
compute: Approximately 13 hours for the two AutoGluon solutions and approximately 24 hours for XGBoost hyperparameter tuning; hardware unspecified.

solution_summary: The pipeline first segmented organs in 3D to define study crops, then classified injury using 2.5D CNN or CoaT backbones with GRUs. Organ visibility from segmentation masks supplied slice-level soft targets, while auxiliary segmentation losses stabilized training and improved scores. Predictions were maximized across slices and ensembled across folds, architectures, and preprocessing variants. The reported ensemble OOF score was 0.31x, compared with 0.326 for the best single four-fold model.

solution_title: Compact description of the competition problem(958th place)
solution_summary: The author frames surface classification as reconstruction of a directed graph whose nodes represent sensor series. Manually labeled connections from orientation data train a connectivity classifier, while a separate classifier estimates probabilities for eight surface types without orientation features. These edge and label probabilities define a graph reconstruction problem, but the post does not provide a completed reconstruction algorithm or quantitative results. It also suggests using reconstructed motion extents to distinguish two hard-tile classes.

The solution generated candidate word arrangements with large simulated annealing runs, then refined them through smaller local searches. Refinement used local windows and replacements of n-grams up to length four. For ID 4, strings and perplexities were cached to avoid repeated computation. Once perplexity fell below 70, the first ten and last four words were fixed during further annealing.

The team generated full-resolution CT images using publicly shared windowing and extracted image metadata. CNNs first predicted image-level pulmonary embolism, followed by an LSTM producing image- and exam-level predictions. They used five-fold validation and optimized the sequence model directly for the competition metric. EfficientNet experiments suffered from overfitting.

solution_summary: The author created additional binary toxicity labels and more-toxic/less-toxic pairs, then trained several pretrained language models. Models used either binary cross-entropy or margin-ranking loss, with larger models generally performing better in cross-validation. Training used a maximum sequence length of 256, AdamW, and a linear warmup schedule over one to three epochs. Optuna tuned weighted ensemble predictions using out-of-fold pair-ordering accuracy.

solution_title: A quick summary of Team Mystic (3rd place) solution
solution_summary: The solution combined historical demand statistics and recent weekly measurements with interaction signals learned by linear and factorization models. Features were generated from earlier weeks, and models trained on a later week predicted subsequent weeks. A single XGBoost model using both feature groups achieved the reported public leaderboard score.

The pipeline used breast ROI detection followed by four ConvNeXt-small classifiers at 2048×1024 resolution, trained with additional mammography datasets. Positive oversampling, extensive augmentation, dropout, and soft positive labels supported training on the imbalanced data. YOLOX-nano supplied breast crops, with thresholding and whole-image fallbacks. A later ablation found that external data improved F1 by about 0.02, while soft positive labels did not clearly outperform standard label smoothing.

solution_title: 9th place - Custom CUDA kernel for wave propagation
solution_summary: The solution used CaFormer and ConvNeXtV2 models with an emphasis on efficient experimentation and augmentation. A custom batched CUDA wave propagation implementation regenerated seismograms from augmented targets about 100 times faster than the original CPU implementation. Training runs were continued at a constant learning rate before cosine-scheduled refinement with extra weight on difficult classes. Predictions were combined using a median across recent checkpoints followed by a mean across runs.
compute: GPU wave propagation with a custom CUDA kernel; approximately 100x faster than the original CPU implementation.

solution_summary: The post proposes post-processing predictions with a target-specific array of rater counts. Each prediction column is first min-max normalized. Predictions are then rounded to discrete increments determined by the corresponding rater count. The author invites others to test the method but provides no measured improvement.

The final system retrieved context with TF-IDF over a Wikipedia STEM corpus expanded by 159K articles, then ensembled three DeBERTa-v3-large models. Retrieval improvements mattered most: sublinear term frequency and corpus expansion each produced measurable leaderboard gains. Models used different training and validation subsets, including question-length matching to the competition data. The ensemble favored strong, weakly correlated models and simple weight combinations after validation-based weight optimization proved unreliable.

The authors trained four network models with different random seeds for the Galaxy Zoo challenge. Their best reported score was 0.08246. Training took about six days on two NVIDIA Titan cards, but the post gives little architectural or inference detail.

solution_title: 4th Place – Residual XGBoost + Meta NN + Hill Climb Opt
solution_summary: The solution centered on XGBoost residual models, engineered delta features, and Optuna parameter tuning. Fourteen XGBoost models incorporated shared out-of-fold predictions as additional features, followed by a neural network meta-blender trained with 17 seeds. Hill climbing optimized ensemble weights, and final blending combined the strongest neural and hill-climbing results. Reported cross-validation improved from 0.05598 initially to 0.055821 after hill climbing.

The author built the agent using HandyRL, although input and model details are absent from the provided text. Inference summed outputs from the three best leaderboard models and selected the highest-scoring legal direction, excluding reversal of the previous action. Each checkpoint was evaluated over 100 games against one imitation-learning agent and two copies of a public reinforcement-learning agent. The highest-scoring new checkpoint each day was submitted.

The final solution trained a BigGAN with a 10M-parameter generator and an 8M-parameter discriminator to generate 64×64 dog images. It removed extreme-aspect-ratio and intruder images, used the supplied bounding boxes, and applied random crops and horizontal flips. BCE loss, Adam, label smoothing, and truncated noise sampling were used without EMA. Earlier DCGAN and AC-GAN variants performed worse; the final reported scores were 31.09602 public and 55.42142 private.

solution_summary: Customers were divided into recent buyers, historical buyers without recent purchases, and customers with no purchase history. Customers with history received candidates from nine retrieval methods, while customers without history received popular items. Each retrieval method supplied 100 items per customer before deduplication. LightGBM ranking and binary models used item and customer aggregates, purchase-window interactions, recency, and retrieval scores, followed by an ensemble based on a linked public method.

The author adapted a starter pipeline to a three-channel 1D ResNet using the accelerometer signals. Training used 1000 ms cuts with 50 ms of future context and a plateau-based learning-rate scheduler. Five models trained on the notebook's folds were ensembled for submission. Cross-validation was approximately 0.30, with public and private scores of 0.351 and 0.356.

solution_summary: The solution used LightGBM with regular-season statistics and a rating derived from averaged system ranks. Added basketball efficiency features included true shooting percentage, the Four Factors, points per possession, and possessions. Four models each held out one season from 2016–2019 while training on the remaining seasons from 2003–2019, and their probabilities were averaged. Neural networks did not work, and the reported competition score was 0.56346.

The team used out-of-fold teacher predictions to softly relabel about 500 suspicious training images, improving EfficientNet B4 cross-validation accuracy from 0.899 to 0.915. They added deduplicated 2019 cassava images and confidence-filtered, pseudo-labeled Mendeley plant images exclusively to training. Six pretrained architectures were trained across five folds using strong augmentation, progressive resizing, and mixed precision with gradient accumulation. Their two final submissions used prediction averaging or maximum-confidence selection, achieving private scores of 0.896 and 0.897 respectively.

solution_title: How I missed a gold medal in my first kaggle competition (could've got 13th place)
solution_summary: The author described a dataset-mention extraction notebook that achieved a private leaderboard score of 0.444 but was not selected for final evaluation. It split training text into 256-token chunks, retained all positive chunks, and discarded half of the negative chunks. The model initialized a binary classification head from the O and MISC output weights of a CoNLL03-fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa model and trained for three epochs. The selected submission instead came from a leaderboard-probing notebook whose method was not detailed.

solution_title: 31th/5k+ with 1 single model without stacking and blending possible, wow!
solution_summary: The author expresses satisfaction with their competition result as a beginner in machine learning. They thank the participants and competition organizers. The post provides no modeling, training, or validation details.

The solution used RGB images and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 with a two-layer classification head. External data and oversampling were particularly helpful, with binary cross-entropy outperforming focal loss. Training used five folds and progressed from 256-pixel to 512-pixel images, with layer-specific learning rates and a cyclical schedule. Averaging eight test-time augmentations and applying a 0.2 threshold produced public and private scores of 0.595 and 0.523.
