solution_title: 3th on Public and 6th on Private, A Very Simple Solution: Big Pretrained-Model is All You Need!
solution_summary: The pipeline randomly selected 1,000 tiles per image, duplicating tiles when necessary, and extracted 768-dimensional features using pretrained iBOT-ViT-Base weights. Chowder multiple-instance learning models classified these image-level feature sets. Seven models were ensembled, with average prediction entropy and an adjusted threshold used to identify the other class. Ensemble uncertainty estimation raised the public score from 0.59 to 0.65, while a PathDINO patch-selection method did not improve results.

solution_title: 51th place solution. Single Model. Private Score 0.35175, Public Score 0.24019.
solution_summary: The author adapted shared competition code and used cropping and padding to reduce overfitting to sequence lengths in the public and private data. Cropping plus padding achieved the best reported score, 0.35175, compared with 0.35215 without either operation. Cropping alone produced a slightly worse score of 0.35274.

The author blended LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, and DenseLight predictions from two complementary feature sets. One set contained 1,504 engineered features, while the other combined public tabular features with DistilRoBERTa predictions from reconstructed essays. Compressing repeated q characters into run lengths improved transformer tokenization, and all tabular models were averaged over ten folds and five seeds. The final weighted blend achieved CV 0.5870 and private score 0.563; later DeBERTa experiments showed additional possibilities beyond the submitted approach.

The solution used a two-stage retrieval and reranking pipeline based on FlagEmbedding, with Qwen2.5-32B for both stages. Each model was trained sequentially on two external datasets and then competition training data. Stage-specific retrieval models generated hard negatives for the corresponding reranker stages, and cross-device negatives improved retrieval training. Reranking the top 18 candidates increased the public score from 0.582 to 0.623.

solution_title: Try to improve your solution with the leak
solution_summary: The author improved predictions from an existing public kernel without training any models. The main improvement exploited the observation that examples sharing an incidence angle almost always shared a label. Predictions agreeing with training labels were pushed toward clipped certainty, while disagreements were resolved through majority voting within angle groups. Extending certainty to consistent groups with angles absent from training improved the public score but not the private score.

solution_title: 10th place: BC + PPO on a Single RTX 5090
solution_summary: A single 21.83M-parameter policy learned from recent leaderboard replays through behavior cloning and then approximately 370M PPO environment steps. Its architecture combined a ResNet map encoder, attention, and autoregressive unit and market heads with legal-action masks. Fresh imitation data, larger networks, realistic recorded opponents, and game-aligned action representations drove the largest gains. Training took approximately 23 hours on one RTX 5090, and inference used greedy decoding without search or ensembling.

solution_title: 41st Solution to AI Agent Security: Multi-Step Tool Attacks
solution_summary: The public approach used model-adapted prompt structures, reliable singleton candidates, and compact URL variations to maximize replay throughput against synthetic tool guardrails. Moving candidate variation late in prompts and ordering candidates by token-prefix similarity improved opportunities for persistent KV-cache reuse. The public POST family scored zero privately, while an orthogonal synthetic email CONFUSED_DEPUTY strategy achieved a private score of 26.85. Deferred Harmony Injection demonstrated control-token materialization on GPT-OSS without reliable behavioral takeover, and multi-action variants failed to outperform singleton flooding.

solution_title: 0.480 public LB solutions! (ensemble of 7 fingerprint/SMILES/atom-level features models)
solution_summary: The solution combined molecular fingerprint neural models, feature-mixture models, and fingerprint-based LightGBM. Individual models scored 0.615–0.650 under 15-fold validation, while their public leaderboard scores varied substantially. Ensembling all models reached approximately 0.480 on the public leaderboard. The author attributed the weaker graph model performance partly to omitting bond features and suggested SMILES-based models were better suited to the private leaderboard.

solution_title: First solo gold, 7th place solution: transformers with convolution/deconvolution
solution_summary: The solution used ConvTransformerEncoder models that combined local convolutions with global self-attention. Convolved base-pair probability and distance matrices supplied attention biases, while deconvolutions restored dimensions for residual stacking. Sequence-reconstruction pretraining and variation in model depth, kernel size, and training-data quality thresholds supported a diverse ensemble. The final ensemble used only models without positional encoding and averaged the central portion of predictions with beta=0.7, improving the reported score from 0.34701 to 0.34550.

This post describes one contributor's portion of a larger ensemble, combining different preprocessing pipelines with boosted trees and neural architectures. Features included integer and raw inputs, temporal aggregations, 50 PCA components, and products of globally ranked features sharing a trend. Models comprised LightGBM with a combined focal and log loss, XGBoost, fully connected networks, and a dual-input fully connected plus Transformer model. The hybrid model alternated training its branches while freezing the other branch for roughly 30 epochs per stage.

The approach focused on avoiding overfitting, selecting models with local five-fold cross-validation, and then training on all available data. Averaging five models improved the private score from 99.180 to 99.280, and pseudo-labeling increased it further to 99.420. Several training and inference tricks produced no significant improvement.

solution_title: Pseudo Data Augmentation (27th place short writeup)
solution_summary: The author created two predictive features by training models on previous loans and applying them to current applications. One LightGBM model estimated whether a previous loan had payments more than three days late, using all installments, while another predicted mean days past due. Previous-loan attributes replaced corresponding application fields during training. Together, the two generated features improved cross-validation performance by about 0.003.

The author trained 24-class audio classifiers on log-mel spectrograms, starting with masked binary cross-entropy on verified positive and negative annotations. Repeated soft pseudo-labeling and retraining raised initial scores from about 0.86 to the 0.96 range, with verified regions sampled half the time to limit confirmation bias. A normalized frequency-coordinate channel improved local metrics, and the final ensemble combined EfficientNet and ReXNet models across four folds. Inference used half-second sliding windows, maximum pooling over each clip, and averaging across models.

The author trained a modified Qwen2-VL model to convert ARC grids into object-based Python representations using roughly 850,000 synthetic grids. Its visual embedding was adapted to discrete colors, and its input arrangement preserved two-dimensional positional information. The resulting representations supported induction and transduction solvers trained on filtered BARC puzzles. Combining several models scored 8 hidden-test points, and merging with a public notebook increased that notebook's score from 26 to 27.

The author used pageviews, mobile status, channel grouping, country, metro, and an aggregated new-visits feature. Categorical features were one-hot encoded and reduced to 24 columns with PCA. LinearSVR performed best among the tested regression models, including nonlinear SVR and several tree-based alternatives.

The post recounts a broad experimental search rather than specifying the final team pipeline. The author trained 96 full-fold models and obtained reasonable progress with shallow four-layer 1D networks before exploring many alternative representations, augmentations, and architectures. Trials included gravitational-wave injection, pretraining, constant-Q transforms, signal transformations, and transformer models. Some approaches had explicit limitations, including poorly converging 2D networks and extended-signal whitening that did not improve performance.

solution_title: Aevion Nemotron v0.19 — P100 sm_60 blocker, pretrained adapter packaging, and Open Contribution write-up
solution_summary: The final v0.19 submission packaged a public pretrained LoRA adapter for the competition's Nemotron base model without additional training. The notebook copied the adapter files, normalized the base-model and inference metadata, and generated submission.zip. An earlier locally trained notebook adapter scored 0.85 public and 0.84 private, but subsequent training attempts failed because the allocated P100 was incompatible with the installed software stack and lacked sufficient memory. The final packaged adapter's score was still pending.

solution_summary: The author primarily represented comments using character n-grams and trained logistic regression with scikit-learn. These features and the linear classifier formed the core of the reported solution. The post points to published code and a blog discussion but provides no validation details or numerical results.

The solution used Ben's radius-based cropping and affine, flip, and contrast augmentations to produce 256×256 inputs. First-stage SE-ResNeXt and SENet models were trained with regression loss on the 2019 training data plus the 2015 dataset. Their weighted predictions supplied pseudo labels for a second stage initialized from first-stage weights and trained with fold-specific portions of the 2019 test set. Averaging the second-stage predictions achieved public and private leaderboard scores of 0.826 and 0.930.
